May it please your Highness to resolve me now,
And what your pleasure is shall satisfy me.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Ay, widow? Then I’ll warrant you all your lands,
An if what pleases him shall pleasure you.
Fight closer, or, good faith, you’ll catch a blow.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: I fear her not, unless she chance to fall.

speaker: RICHARD
text: God forbid that, for he’ll take vantages.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: How many children hast thou, widow? Tell me.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: I think he means to beg a child of her.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Nay, then, whip me; he’ll rather give her two.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Three, my most gracious lord.

speaker: RICHARD
text: You shall have four if you’ll be ruled by him.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: ’Twere pity they should lose their father’s lands.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Be pitiful, dread lord, and grant it then.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Lords, give us leave. I’ll try this widow’s wit.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Ay, good leave have you, for you will have leave
Till youth take leave and leave you to the crutch.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Now tell me, madam, do you love your children?

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Ay, full as dearly as I love myself.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: And would you not do much to do them good?

speaker: LADY GREY
text: To do them good I would sustain some harm.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Then get your husband’s lands to do them good.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Therefore I came unto your Majesty.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: I’ll tell you how these lands are to be got.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: So shall you bind me to your Highness’ service.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: What service wilt thou do me if I give them?

speaker: LADY GREY
text: What you command that rests in me to do.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: But you will take exceptions to my boon.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: No, gracious lord, except I cannot do it.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Ay, but thou canst do what I mean to ask.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Why, then, I will do what your Grace commands.

speaker: RICHARD
text: He plies her hard, and much rain wears the marble.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: As red as fire! Nay, then, her wax must melt.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Why stops my lord? Shall I not hear my task?

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: An easy task; ’tis but to love a king.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: That’s soon performed because I am a subject.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Why, then, thy husband’s lands I freely give thee.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: I take my leave with many thousand thanks.

speaker: RICHARD
text: The match is made; she seals it with a cursy.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: But stay thee; ’tis the fruits of love I mean.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: The fruits of love I mean, my loving liege.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Ay, but, I fear me, in another sense.
What love, think’st thou, I sue so much to get?

speaker: LADY GREY
text:
My love till death, my humble thanks, my prayers,
That love which virtue begs and virtue grants.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: No, by my troth, I did not mean such love.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Why, then, you mean not as I thought you did.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: But now you partly may perceive my mind.

speaker: LADY GREY
text:
My mind will never grant what I perceive
Your Highness aims at, if I aim aright.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: To tell thee plain, I aim to lie with thee.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: To tell you plain, I had rather lie in prison.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Why, then, thou shalt not have thy husband’s lands.

speaker: LADY GREY
text:
Why, then, mine honesty shall be my dower,
For by that loss I will not purchase them.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Therein thou wrong’st thy children mightily.

speaker: LADY GREY
text:
Herein your Highness wrongs both them and me.
But, mighty lord, this merry inclination
Accords not with the sadness of my suit.
Please you dismiss me either with ay or no.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Ay, if thou wilt say “ay” to my request;
No, if thou dost say “no” to my demand.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: Then no, my lord; my suit is at an end.

speaker: RICHARD
text: The widow likes him not; she knits her brows.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: He is the bluntest wooer in Christendom.

speaker: KING EDWARD
LADY GREY
text:
’Tis better said than done, my gracious lord.
I am a subject fit to jest withal,
But far unfit to be a sovereign.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Sweet widow, by my state I swear to thee
I speak no more than what my soul intends,
And that is, to enjoy thee for my love.

speaker: LADY GREY
text:
And that is more than I will yield unto.
I know I am too mean to be your queen
And yet too good to be your concubine.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: You cavil, widow; I did mean my queen.

speaker: LADY GREY
text: ’Twill grieve your Grace my sons should call you father.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
No more than when my daughters call thee mother.
Thou art a widow and thou hast some children,
And, by God’s mother, I, being but a bachelor,
Have other some. Why, ’tis a happy thing
To be the father unto many sons.
Answer no more, for thou shalt be my queen.

speaker: RICHARD
text: The ghostly father now hath done his shrift.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: When he was made a shriver, ’twas for shift.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Brothers, you muse what chat we two have had.

speaker: RICHARD
text: The widow likes it not, for she looks very sad.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: You’d think it strange if I should marry her.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: To who, my lord?

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Why, Clarence, to myself.

speaker: RICHARD
text: That would be ten days’ wonder at the least.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: That’s a day longer than a wonder lasts.

speaker: RICHARD
text: By so much is the wonder in extremes.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Well, jest on, brothers. I can tell you both
Her suit is granted for her husband’s lands.

speaker: NOBLEMAN
text:
My gracious lord, Henry, your foe, is taken
And brought your prisoner to your palace gate.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
See that he be conveyed unto the Tower.
And go we, brothers, to the man that took him,
To question of his apprehension.—
Widow, go you along.—Lords, use her honorably.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Ay, Edward will use women honorably!
Would he were wasted—marrow, bones, and all—
That from his loins no hopeful branch may spring
To cross me from the golden time I look for.
And yet, between my soul’s desire and me,
The lustful Edward’s title burièd,
Is Clarence, Henry, and his son, young Edward,
And all the unlooked-for issue of their bodies
To take their rooms ere I can place myself.
A cold premeditation for my purpose.
Why, then, I do but dream on sovereignty
Like one that stands upon a promontory
And spies a far-off shore where he would tread,
Wishing his foot were equal with his eye,
And chides the sea that sunders him from thence,
Saying he’ll lade it dry to have his way.
So do I wish the crown, being so far off,
And so I chide the means that keeps me from it,
And so, I say, I’ll cut the causes off,
Flattering me with impossibilities.
My eye’s too quick, my heart o’erweens too much,
Unless my hand and strength could equal them.
Well, say there is no kingdom then for Richard,
What other pleasure can the world afford?
I’ll make my heaven in a lady’s lap
And deck my body in gay ornaments,
And ’witch sweet ladies with my words and looks.
O miserable thought, and more unlikely
Than to accomplish twenty golden crowns!
Why, Love forswore me in my mother’s womb,
And, for I should not deal in her soft laws,
She did corrupt frail Nature with some bribe
To shrink mine arm up like a withered shrub;
To make an envious mountain on my back,
Where sits Deformity to mock my body;
To shape my legs of an unequal size;
To disproportion me in every part,
Like to a chaos, or an unlicked bear-whelp,
That carries no impression like the dam.
And am I then a man to be beloved?
O monstrous fault to harbor such a thought!
Then, since this Earth affords no joy to me
But to command, to check, to o’erbear such
As are of better person than myself,
I’ll make my heaven to dream upon the crown,
And, whiles I live, t’ account this world but hell
Until my misshaped trunk that bears this head
Be round impalèd with a glorious crown.
And yet I know not how to get the crown,
For many lives stand between me and home;
And I, like one lost in a thorny wood,
That rents the thorns and is rent with the thorns,
Seeking a way and straying from the way,
Not knowing how to find the open air,
But toiling desperately to find it out,
Torment myself to catch the English crown.
And from that torment I will free myself
Or hew my way out with a bloody axe.
Why, I can smile, and murder whiles I smile,
And cry “Content” to that which grieves my heart,
And wet my cheeks with artificial tears,
And frame my face to all occasions.
I’ll drown more sailors than the mermaid shall;
I’ll slay more gazers than the basilisk;
I’ll play the orator as well as Nestor,
Deceive more slyly than Ulysses could,
And, like a Sinon, take another Troy.
I can add colors to the chameleon,
Change shapes with Proteus for advantages,
And set the murderous Machiavel to school.
Can I do this and cannot get a crown?
Tut, were it farther off, I’ll pluck it down.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text:
Fair Queen of England, worthy Margaret,
Sit down with us. It ill befits thy state
And birth that thou shouldst stand while Lewis doth sit.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
No, mighty King of France. Now Margaret
Must strike her sail and learn awhile to serve
Where kings command. I was, I must confess,
Great Albion’s queen in former golden days,
But now mischance hath trod my title down
And with dishonor laid me on the ground,
Where I must take like seat unto my fortune
And to my humble seat conform myself.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text: Why, say, fair queen, whence springs this deep despair?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
From such a cause as fills mine eyes with tears
And stops my tongue, while heart is drowned in cares.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text:
Whate’er it be, be thou still like thyself,
And sit thee by our side.
Yield not thy neck
To Fortune’s yoke, but let thy dauntless mind
Still ride in triumph over all mischance.
Be plain, Queen Margaret, and tell thy grief.
It shall be eased if France can yield relief.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
Those gracious words revive my drooping thoughts
And give my tongue-tied sorrows leave to speak.
Now therefore be it known to noble Lewis
That Henry, sole possessor of my love,
Is, of a king, become a banished man
And forced to live in Scotland a forlorn;
While proud ambitious Edward, Duke of York,
Usurps the regal title and the seat
Of England’s true-anointed lawful king.
This is the cause that I, poor Margaret,
With this my son, Prince Edward, Henry’s heir,
Am come to crave thy just and lawful aid;
And if thou fail us, all our hope is done.
Scotland hath will to help but cannot help;
Our people and our peers are both misled,
Our treasure seized, our soldiers put to flight,
And, as thou seest, ourselves in heavy plight.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text:
Renownèd queen, with patience calm the storm
While we bethink a means to break it off.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: The more we stay, the stronger grows our foe.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text: The more I stay, the more I’ll succor thee.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
O, but impatience waiteth on true sorrow.
And see where comes the breeder of my sorrow.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text: What’s he approacheth boldly to our presence?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: Our Earl of Warwick, Edward’s greatest friend.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text: Welcome, brave Warwick. What brings thee to France?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
Ay, now begins a second storm to rise,
For this is he that moves both wind and tide.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
From worthy Edward, King of Albion,
My lord and sovereign and thy vowèd friend,
I come in kindness and unfeignèd love,
First, to do greetings to thy royal person,
And then to crave a league of amity,
And, lastly, to confirm that amity
With nuptial knot, if thou vouchsafe to grant
That virtuous Lady Bona, thy fair sister,
To England’s king in lawful marriage.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: If that go forward, Henry’s hope is done.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
And, gracious madam, in our king’s behalf,
I am commanded, with your leave and favor,
Humbly to kiss your hand, and with my tongue
To tell the passion of my sovereign’s heart,
Where fame, late ent’ring at his heedful ears,
Hath placed thy beauty’s image and thy virtue.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
King Lewis and Lady Bona, hear me speak
Before you answer Warwick. His demand
Springs not from Edward’s well-meant honest love,
But from deceit, bred by necessity;
For how can tyrants safely govern home
Unless abroad they purchase great alliance?
To prove him tyrant, this reason may suffice:
That Henry liveth still; but were he dead,
Yet here Prince Edward stands, King Henry’s son.
Look, therefore, Lewis, that by this league and marriage
Thou draw not on thy danger and dishonor;
For though usurpers sway the rule awhile,
Yet heav’ns are just, and time suppresseth wrongs.

speaker: WARWICK
text: Injurious Margaret!

speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
text: And why not “Queen”?

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Because thy father Henry did usurp,
And thou no more art prince than she is queen.

speaker: OXFORD
text:
Then Warwick disannuls great John of Gaunt,
Which did subdue the greatest part of Spain;
And after John of Gaunt, Henry the Fourth,
Whose wisdom was a mirror to the wisest;
And after that wise prince, Henry the Fifth,
Who by his prowess conquerèd all France.
From these our Henry lineally descends.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Oxford, how haps it in this smooth discourse
You told not how Henry the Sixth hath lost
All that which Henry the Fifth had gotten.
Methinks these peers of France should smile at that.
But, for the rest: you tell a pedigree
Of threescore and two years, a silly time
To make prescription for a kingdom’s worth.

speaker: OXFORD
text:
Why, Warwick, canst thou speak against thy liege,
Whom thou obeyed’st thirty and six years,
And not bewray thy treason with a blush?

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Can Oxford, that did ever fence the right,
Now buckler falsehood with a pedigree?
For shame, leave Henry, and call Edward king.

speaker: OXFORD
text:
Call him my king, by whose injurious doom
My elder brother, the Lord Aubrey Vere,
Was done to death? And more than so, my father,
Even in the downfall of his mellowed years,
When nature brought him to the door of death?
No, Warwick, no. While life upholds this arm,
This arm upholds the house of Lancaster.

speaker: WARWICK
text: And I the house of York.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text:
Queen Margaret, Prince Edward, and Oxford,
Vouchsafe, at our request, to stand aside
While I use further conference with Warwick.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: Heavens grant that Warwick’s words bewitch him not.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text:
Now, Warwick, tell me, even upon thy conscience,
Is Edward your true king? For I were loath
To link with him that were not lawful chosen.

speaker: WARWICK
text: Thereon I pawn my credit and mine honor.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text: But is he gracious in the people’s eye?

speaker: WARWICK
text: The more that Henry was unfortunate.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text:
Then further, all dissembling set aside,
Tell me for truth the measure of his love
Unto our sister Bona.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Such it seems
As may beseem a monarch like himself.
Myself have often heard him say and swear
That this his love was an eternal plant,
Whereof the root was fixed in virtue’s ground,
The leaves and fruit maintained with beauty’s sun,
Exempt from envy but not from disdain,
Unless the Lady Bona quit his pain.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text: Now, sister, let us hear your firm resolve.

speaker: LADY BONA
text:
Your grant or your denial shall be mine.
Yet I confess that often ere this day,
When I have heard your king’s desert recounted,
Mine ear hath tempted judgment to desire.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text:
Then, Warwick, thus: our sister shall be Edward’s.
And now forthwith shall articles be drawn
Touching the jointure that your king must make,
Which with her dowry shall be counterpoised.—
Draw near, Queen Margaret, and be a witness
That Bona shall be wife to the English king.

speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
text: To Edward, but not to the English king.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
Deceitful Warwick, it was thy device
By this alliance to make void my suit.
Before thy coming, Lewis was Henry’s friend.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text:
And still is friend to him and Margaret.
But if your title to the crown be weak,
As may appear by Edward’s good success,
Then ’tis but reason that I be released
From giving aid which late I promisèd.
Yet shall you have all kindness at my hand
That your estate requires and mine can yield.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Henry now lives in Scotland at his ease,
Where, having nothing, nothing can he lose.—
And as for you yourself, our quondam queen,
You have a father able to maintain you,
And better ’twere you troubled him than France.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
Peace, impudent and shameless Warwick,
Proud setter-up and puller-down of kings!
I will not hence till with my talk and tears,
Both full of truth, I make King Lewis behold
Thy sly conveyance and thy lord’s false love,
For both of you are birds of selfsame feather.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text: Warwick, this is some post to us or thee.

speaker: POST
text:
My lord ambassador, these letters are for you,
Sent from your brother, Marquess Montague.
These from our king unto your Majesty.
And, madam, these for you—from whom, I know not.

speaker: OXFORD
text:
I like it well that our fair queen and mistress
Smiles at her news, while Warwick frowns at his.

speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
text:
Nay, mark how Lewis stamps as he were nettled.
I hope all’s for the best.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text: Warwick, what are thy news? And yours, fair queen?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: Mine, such as fill my heart with unhoped joys.

speaker: WARWICK
text: Mine, full of sorrow and heart’s discontent.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text:
What, has your king married the Lady Grey,
And now, to soothe your forgery and his,
Sends me a paper to persuade me patience?
Is this th’ alliance that he seeks with France?
Dare he presume to scorn us in this manner?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
I told your Majesty as much before.
This proveth Edward’s love and Warwick’s honesty.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
King Lewis, I here protest in sight of heaven
And by the hope I have of heavenly bliss,
That I am clear from this misdeed of Edward’s—
No more my king, for he dishonors me,
But most himself, if he could see his shame.
Did I forget that by the house of York
My father came untimely to his death?
Did I let pass th’ abuse done to my niece?
Did I impale him with the regal crown?
Did I put Henry from his native right?
And am I guerdoned at the last with shame?
Shame on himself, for my desert is honor!
And to repair my honor lost for him,
I here renounce him and return to Henry.
My noble queen, let former grudges pass,
And henceforth I am thy true servitor.
I will revenge his wrong to Lady Bona
And replant Henry in his former state.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
Warwick, these words have turned my hate to love,
And I forgive and quite forget old faults,
And joy that thou becom’st King Henry’s friend.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
So much his friend, ay, his unfeignèd friend,
That if King Lewis vouchsafe to furnish us
With some few bands of chosen soldiers,
I’ll undertake to land them on our coast
And force the tyrant from his seat by war.
’Tis not his new-made bride shall succor him.
And as for Clarence, as my letters tell me,
He’s very likely now to fall from him
For matching more for wanton lust than honor,
Or than for strength and safety of our country.

speaker: LADY BONA
text:
Dear brother, how shall Bona be revenged
But by thy help to this distressèd queen?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
Renownèd prince, how shall poor Henry live
Unless thou rescue him from foul despair?

speaker: LADY BONA
text: My quarrel and this English queen’s are one.

speaker: WARWICK
text: And mine, fair Lady Bona, joins with yours.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text:
And mine with hers and thine and Margaret’s.
Therefore at last I firmly am resolved
You shall have aid.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: Let me give humble thanks for all, at once.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text:
Then, England’s messenger, return in post,
And tell false Edward, thy supposèd king,
That Lewis of France is sending over maskers
To revel it with him and his new bride.
Thou seest what’s passed; go fear thy king withal.

speaker: LADY BONA
text:
Tell him, in hope he’ll prove a widower shortly,
I wear the willow garland for his sake.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
Tell him my mourning weeds are laid aside
And I am ready to put armor on.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Tell him from me that he hath done me wrong,
And therefore I’ll uncrown him ere ’t be long.
There’s thy reward.
Be gone.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text:
But, Warwick,
Thou and Oxford with five thousand men
Shall cross the seas and bid false Edward battle;
And as occasion serves, this noble queen
And prince shall follow with a fresh supply.
Yet ere thou go, but answer me one doubt:
What pledge have we of thy firm loyalty?

speaker: WARWICK
text:
This shall assure my constant loyalty:
That if our queen and this young prince agree,
I’ll join mine eldest daughter, and my joy,
To him forthwith in holy wedlock bands.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
Yes, I agree, and thank you for your motion.
Son Edward, she is fair and virtuous.
Therefore, delay not; give thy hand to Warwick,
And with thy hand, thy faith irrevocable,
That only Warwick’s daughter shall be thine.

speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
text:
Yes, I accept her, for she well deserves it,
And here, to pledge my vow, I give my hand.

speaker: KING LEWIS
text:
Why stay we now? These soldiers shall be levied,
And thou, Lord Bourbon, our High Admiral,
Shall waft them over with our royal fleet.
I long till Edward fall by war’s mischance
For mocking marriage with a dame of France.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
I came from Edward as ambassador,
But I return his sworn and mortal foe.
Matter of marriage was the charge he gave me,
But dreadful war shall answer his demand.
Had he none else to make a stale but me?
Then none but I shall turn his jest to sorrow.
I was the chief that raised him to the crown,
And I’ll be chief to bring him down again:
Not that I pity Henry’s misery,
But seek revenge on Edward’s mockery.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Now tell me, brother Clarence, what think you
Of this new marriage with the Lady Grey?
Hath not our brother made a worthy choice?

speaker: CLARENCE
text:
Alas, you know ’tis far from hence to France.
How could he stay till Warwick made return?

speaker: SOMERSET
text: My lords, forbear this talk. Here comes the King.

speaker: RICHARD
text: And his well-chosen bride.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: I mind to tell him plainly what I think.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Now, brother of Clarence, how like you our choice,
That you stand pensive, as half malcontent?

speaker: CLARENCE
text:
As well as Lewis of France or the Earl of Warwick,
Which are so weak of courage and in judgment
That they’ll take no offense at our abuse.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Suppose they take offense without a cause,
They are but Lewis and Warwick; I am Edward,
Your king and Warwick’s, and must have my will.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
And shall have your will because our king.
Yet hasty marriage seldom proveth well.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Yea, brother Richard, are you offended too?

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Not I.
No, God forbid that I should wish them severed
Whom God hath joined together. Ay, and ’twere pity
To sunder them that yoke so well together.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Setting your scorns and your mislike aside,
Tell me some reason why the Lady Grey
Should not become my wife and England’s queen?
And you too, Somerset and Montague,
Speak freely what you think.

speaker: CLARENCE
text:
Then this is mine opinion: that King Lewis
Becomes your enemy for mocking him
About the marriage of the Lady Bona.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
And Warwick, doing what you gave in charge,
Is now dishonorèd by this new marriage.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
What if both Lewis and Warwick be appeased
By such invention as I can devise?

speaker: MONTAGUE
text:
Yet to have joined with France in such alliance
Would more have strengthened this our commonwealth
’Gainst foreign storms than any home-bred marriage.

speaker: HASTINGS
text:
Why, knows not Montague that of itself
England is safe, if true within itself?

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: But the safer when ’tis backed with France.

speaker: HASTINGS
text:
’Tis better using France than trusting France.
Let us be backed with God and with the seas
Which He hath giv’n for fence impregnable,
And with their helps only defend ourselves.
In them and in ourselves our safety lies.

speaker: CLARENCE
text:
For this one speech, Lord Hastings well deserves
To have the heir of the Lord Hungerford.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Ay, what of that? It was my will and grant,
And for this once my will shall stand for law.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
And yet methinks your Grace hath not done well
To give the heir and daughter of Lord Scales
Unto the brother of your loving bride.
She better would have fitted me or Clarence;
But in your bride you bury brotherhood.

speaker: CLARENCE
text:
Or else you would not have bestowed the heir
Of the Lord Bonville on your new wife’s son,
And leave your brothers to go speed elsewhere.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Alas, poor Clarence, is it for a wife
That thou art malcontent? I will provide thee.

speaker: CLARENCE
text:
In choosing for yourself you showed your judgment,
Which, being shallow, you shall give me leave
To play the broker in mine own behalf.
And to that end, I shortly mind to leave you.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Leave me or tarry, Edward will be king
And not be tied unto his brother’s will.

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text:
My lords, before it pleased his Majesty
To raise my state to title of a queen,
Do me but right and you must all confess
That I was not ignoble of descent,
And meaner than myself have had like fortune.
But as this title honors me and mine,
So your dislikes, to whom I would be pleasing,
Doth cloud my joys with danger and with sorrow.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
My love, forbear to fawn upon their frowns.
What danger or what sorrow can befall thee
So long as Edward is thy constant friend
And their true sovereign, whom they must obey?
Nay, whom they shall obey, and love thee too,
Unless they seek for hatred at my hands;
Which if they do, yet will I keep thee safe,
And they shall feel the vengeance of my wrath.

speaker: RICHARD
text: I hear, yet say not much, but think the more.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Now, messenger, what letters or what news from France?

speaker: POST
text:
My sovereign liege, no letters and few words
But such as I without your special pardon
Dare not relate.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Go to, we pardon thee. Therefore, in brief,
Tell me their words as near as thou canst guess them.
What answer makes King Lewis unto our letters?

speaker: POST
text:
At my depart, these were his very words:
“Go tell false Edward, the supposèd king,
That Lewis of France is sending over maskers
To revel it with him and his new bride.”

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Is Lewis so brave? Belike he thinks me Henry.
But what said Lady Bona to my marriage?

speaker: POST
text:
These were her words, uttered with mild disdain:
“Tell him, in hope he’ll prove a widower shortly,
I’ll wear the willow garland for his sake.”

speaker: KING EDWARD
POST
text:
“Tell him,” quoth she, “my mourning weeds are done,
And I am ready to put armor on.”

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Belike she minds to play the Amazon.
But what said Warwick to these injuries?

speaker: POST
text:
He, more incensed against your Majesty
Than all the rest, discharged me with these words:
“Tell him from me that he hath done me wrong,
And therefore I’ll uncrown him ere ’t be long.”

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Ha! Durst the traitor breathe out so proud words?
Well, I will arm me, being thus forewarned.
They shall have wars and pay for their presumption.
But say, is Warwick friends with Margaret?

speaker: POST
text:
Ay, gracious sovereign, they are so linked in friendship
That young Prince Edward marries Warwick’s daughter.

speaker: CLARENCE
text:
Belike the elder; Clarence will have the younger.—
Now, brother king, farewell, and sit you fast,
For I will hence to Warwick’s other daughter,
That, though I want a kingdom, yet in marriage
I may not prove inferior to yourself.
You that love me and Warwick, follow me.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Not I. My thoughts aim at a further matter:
I stay not for the love of Edward, but the crown.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Clarence and Somerset both gone to Warwick?
Yet am I armed against the worst can happen,
And haste is needful in this desp’rate case.
Pembroke and Stafford, you in our behalf
Go levy men and make prepare for war.
They are already, or quickly will be, landed.
Myself in person will straight follow you.
But ere I go, Hastings and Montague,
Resolve my doubt: you twain, of all the rest,
Are near to Warwick by blood and by alliance.
Tell me if you love Warwick more than me.
If it be so, then both depart to him.
I rather wish you foes than hollow friends.
But if you mind to hold your true obedience,
Give me assurance with some friendly vow,
That I may never have you in suspect.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: So God help Montague as he proves true!

speaker: HASTINGS
text: And Hastings as he favors Edward’s cause!

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Now, brother Richard, will you stand by us?

speaker: RICHARD
text: Ay, in despite of all that shall withstand you.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Why, so. Then am I sure of victory.
Now therefore let us hence and lose no hour
Till we meet Warwick with his foreign power.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Trust me, my lord, all hitherto goes well.
The common people by numbers swarm to us.
But see where Somerset and Clarence comes.—
Speak suddenly, my lords: are we all friends?

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Fear not that, my lord.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Then, gentle Clarence, welcome unto Warwick,
And welcome, Somerset. I hold it cowardice
To rest mistrustful where a noble heart
Hath pawned an open hand in sign of love;
Else might I think that Clarence, Edward’s brother,
Were but a feignèd friend to our proceedings.
But welcome, sweet Clarence; my daughter shall be thine.
And now, what rests but, in night’s coverture
Thy brother being carelessly encamped,
His soldiers lurking in the town about,
And but attended by a simple guard,
We may surprise and take him at our pleasure?
Our scouts have found the adventure very easy;
That, as Ulysses and stout Diomed
With sleight and manhood stole to Rhesus’ tents
And brought from thence the Thracian fatal steeds,
So we, well covered with the night’s black mantle,
At unawares may beat down Edward’s guard
And seize himself. I say not “slaughter him,”
For I intend but only to surprise him.
You that will follow me to this attempt,
Applaud the name of Henry with your leader.
Why then, let’s on our way in silent sort.
For Warwick and his friends, God and Saint George!

speaker: FIRST WATCH
text:
Come on, my masters, each man take his stand.
The King by this is set him down to sleep.

speaker: SECOND WATCH
text: What, will he not to bed?

speaker: FIRST WATCH
text:
Why, no, for he hath made a solemn vow
Never to lie and take his natural rest
Till Warwick or himself be quite suppressed.

speaker: SECOND WATCH
text:
Tomorrow, then, belike shall be the day,
If Warwick be so near as men report.

speaker: THIRD WATCH
text:
But say, I pray, what nobleman is that
That with the King here resteth in his tent?

speaker: FIRST WATCH
text: ’Tis the Lord Hastings, the King’s chiefest friend.

speaker: THIRD WATCH
text:
O, is it so? But why commands the King
That his chief followers lodge in towns about him,
While he himself keeps in the cold field?

speaker: SECOND WATCH
text: ’Tis the more honor, because more dangerous.

speaker: THIRD WATCH
text:
Ay, but give me worship and quietness;
I like it better than a dangerous honor.
If Warwick knew in what estate he stands,
’Tis to be doubted he would waken him.

speaker: FIRST WATCH
text: Unless our halberds did shut up his passage.

speaker: SECOND WATCH
text:
Ay, wherefore else guard we his royal tent
But to defend his person from night foes?

speaker: WARWICK
text:
This is his tent, and see where stand his guard.
Courage, my masters. Honor, now or never!
But follow me, and Edward shall be ours.

speaker: FIRST WATCH
text: Who goes there?

speaker: SECOND WATCH
text: Stay, or thou diest!

speaker: SOMERSET
text: What are they that fly there?

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Richard and Hastings.
Let them go. Here is the Duke.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
The Duke?
Why, Warwick, when we parted, thou call’dst me king.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Ay, but the case is altered.
When you disgraced me in my embassade,
Then I degraded you from being king
And come now to create you Duke of York.
Alas, how should you govern any kingdom
That know not how to use ambassadors,
Nor how to be contented with one wife,
Nor how to use your brothers brotherly,
Nor how to study for the people’s welfare,
Nor how to shroud yourself from enemies?

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Yea, brother of Clarence, art thou here too?
Nay, then, I see that Edward needs must down.
Yet, Warwick, in despite of all mischance,
Of thee thyself and all thy complices,
Edward will always bear himself as king.
Though Fortune’s malice overthrow my state,
My mind exceeds the compass of her wheel.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Then for his mind be Edward England’s king,
But Henry now shall wear the English crown
And be true king indeed, thou but the shadow.—
My lord of Somerset, at my request,
See that forthwith Duke Edward be conveyed
Unto my brother, Archbishop of York.
When I have fought with Pembroke and his fellows,
I’ll follow you and tell what answer
Lewis and the Lady Bona send to him.—
Now for awhile farewell, good Duke of York.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
What Fates impose, that men must needs abide;
It boots not to resist both wind and tide.

speaker: OXFORD
text:
What now remains, my lords, for us to do
But march to London with our soldiers?

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Ay, that’s the first thing that we have to do,
To free King Henry from imprisonment
And see him seated in the regal throne.

speaker: RIVERS
text: Madam, what makes you in this sudden change?

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text:
Why, brother Rivers, are you yet to learn
What late misfortune is befall’n King Edward?

speaker: RIVERS
text: What, loss of some pitched battle against Warwick?

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text: No, but the loss of his own royal person.

speaker: RIVERS
text: Then is my sovereign slain?

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text:
Ay, almost slain, for he is taken prisoner,
Either betrayed by falsehood of his guard
Or by his foe surprised at unawares;
And, as I further have to understand,
Is new committed to the Bishop of York,
Fell Warwick’s brother and by that our foe.

speaker: RIVERS
QUEEN ELIZABETH
text:
Till then fair hope must hinder life’s decay;
And I the rather wean me from despair
For love of Edward’s offspring in my womb.
This is it that makes me bridle passion
And bear with mildness my misfortune’s cross.
Ay, ay, for this I draw in many a tear
And stop the rising of blood-sucking sighs,
Lest with my sighs or tears I blast or drown
King Edward’s fruit, true heir to th’ English crown.

speaker: RIVERS
text: But, madam, where is Warwick then become?

speaker: QUEEN ELIZABETH
text:
I am informèd that he comes towards London
To set the crown once more on Henry’s head.
Guess thou the rest: King Edward’s friends must down.
But to prevent the tyrant’s violence—
For trust not him that hath once broken faith—
I’ll hence forthwith unto the sanctuary
To save at least the heir of Edward’s right.
There shall I rest secure from force and fraud.
Come, therefore, let us fly while we may fly.
If Warwick take us, we are sure to die.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Now, my Lord Hastings and Sir William Stanley,
Leave off to wonder why I drew you hither
Into this chiefest thicket of the park.
Thus stands the case: you know our king, my brother,
Is prisoner to the Bishop here, at whose hands
He hath good usage and great liberty,
And, often but attended with weak guard,
Comes hunting this way to disport himself.
I have advertised him by secret means
That, if about this hour he make this way
Under the color of his usual game,
He shall here find his friends with horse and men
To set him free from his captivity.

speaker: HUNTSMAN
text: This way, my lord, for this way lies the game.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Nay, this way, man. See where the huntsmen stand.—
Now, brother of Gloucester, Lord Hastings, and the rest,
Stand you thus close to steal the Bishop’s deer?

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Brother, the time and case requireth haste.
Your horse stands ready at the park corner.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: But whither shall we then?

speaker: HASTINGS
text: To Lynn, my lord, and shipped from thence to Flanders.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Well guessed, believe me, for that was my meaning.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Stanley, I will requite thy forwardness.

speaker: RICHARD
text: But wherefore stay we? ’Tis no time to talk.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Huntsman, what sayst thou? Wilt thou go along?

speaker: HUNTSMAN
text: Better do so than tarry and be hanged.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Come then, away! Let’s ha’ no more ado.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Bishop, farewell; shield thee from Warwick’s frown,
And pray that I may repossess the crown.

speaker: KING HENRY
text:
Master lieutenant, now that God and friends
Have shaken Edward from the regal seat
And turned my captive state to liberty,
My fear to hope, my sorrows unto joys,
At our enlargement what are thy due fees?

speaker: LIEUTENANT
text:
Subjects may challenge nothing of their sov’reigns,
But, if an humble prayer may prevail,
I then crave pardon of your Majesty.

speaker: KING HENRY
text:
For what, lieutenant? For well using me?
Nay, be thou sure I’ll well requite thy kindness,
For that it made my imprisonment a pleasure,
Ay, such a pleasure as encagèd birds
Conceive when, after many moody thoughts,
At last by notes of household harmony
They quite forget their loss of liberty.—
But, Warwick, after God thou sett’st me free,
And chiefly, therefore, I thank God and thee.
He was the author, thou the instrument.
Therefore, that I may conquer Fortune’s spite
By living low where Fortune cannot hurt me,
And that the people of this blessèd land
May not be punished with my thwarting stars,
Warwick, although my head still wear the crown,
I here resign my government to thee,
For thou art fortunate in all thy deeds.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Your Grace hath still been famed for virtuous
And now may seem as wise as virtuous
By spying and avoiding Fortune’s malice,
For few men rightly temper with the stars.
Yet, in this one thing let me blame your Grace:
For choosing me when Clarence is in place.

speaker: CLARENCE
text:
No, Warwick, thou art worthy of the sway,
To whom the heav’ns in thy nativity
Adjudged an olive branch and laurel crown
As likely to be blest in peace and war;
And therefore I yield thee my free consent.

speaker: WARWICK
text: And I choose Clarence only for Protector.

speaker: KING HENRY
text:
Warwick and Clarence, give me both your hands.
Now join your hands, and with your hands your hearts,
That no dissension hinder government.
I make you both Protectors of this land,
While I myself will lead a private life
And in devotion spend my latter days,
To sin’s rebuke and my Creator’s praise.

speaker: WARWICK
text: What answers Clarence to his sovereign’s will?

speaker: CLARENCE
text:
That he consents, if Warwick yield consent,
For on thy fortune I repose myself.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Why, then, though loath, yet must I be content.
We’ll yoke together like a double shadow
To Henry’s body, and supply his place—
I mean, in bearing weight of government—
While he enjoys the honor and his ease.
And, Clarence, now then it is more than needful
Forthwith that Edward be pronounced a traitor
And all his lands and goods be confiscate.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: What else? And that succession be determinèd.

speaker: WARWICK
text: Ay, therein Clarence shall not want his part.

speaker: KING HENRY
text:
But with the first of all your chief affairs
Let me entreat—for I command no more—
That Margaret your queen and my son Edward
Be sent for, to return from France with speed,
For till I see them here, by doubtful fear
My joy of liberty is half eclipsed.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: It shall be done, my sovereign, with all speed.

speaker: KING HENRY
text:
My lord of Somerset, what youth is that
Of whom you seem to have so tender care?

speaker: SOMERSET
text: My liege, it is young Henry, Earl of Richmond.

speaker: KING HENRY
text:
Come hither, England’s hope.
If secret powers
Suggest but truth to my divining thoughts,
This pretty lad will prove our country’s bliss.
His looks are full of peaceful majesty,
His head by nature framed to wear a crown,
His hand to wield a scepter, and himself
Likely in time to bless a regal throne.
Make much of him, my lords, for this is he
Must help you more than you are hurt by me.

speaker: WARWICK
text: What news, my friend?

speaker: POST
text:
That Edward is escapèd from your brother
And fled, as he hears since, to Burgundy.

speaker: WARWICK
text: Unsavory news! But how made he escape?

speaker: POST
text:
He was conveyed by Richard, Duke of Gloucester,
And the Lord Hastings, who attended him
In secret ambush on the forest side
And from the Bishop’s huntsmen rescued him,
For hunting was his daily exercise.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
My brother was too careless of his charge.
But let us hence, my sovereign, to provide
A salve for any sore that may betide.

speaker: SOMERSET
text:
My lord, I like not of this flight of Edward’s,
For doubtless Burgundy will yield him help,
And we shall have more wars before ’t be long.
As Henry’s late presaging prophecy
Did glad my heart with hope of this young Richmond,
So doth my heart misgive me in these conflicts
What may befall him, to his harm and ours.
Therefore, Lord Oxford, to prevent the worst,
Forthwith we’ll send him hence to Brittany
Till storms be past of civil enmity.

speaker: OXFORD
text:
Ay, for if Edward repossess the crown,
’Tis like that Richmond, with the rest, shall down.

speaker: SOMERSET
text:
It shall be so. He shall to Brittany.
Come, therefore, let’s about it speedily.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Now, brother Richard, Lord Hastings, and the rest:
Yet thus far Fortune maketh us amends,
And says that once more I shall interchange
My wanèd state for Henry’s regal crown.
Well have we passed, and now re-passed, the seas,
And brought desirèd help from Burgundy.
What then remains, we being thus arrived
From Ravenspurgh Haven before the gates of York,
But that we enter as into our dukedom?

speaker: RICHARD
text:
The gates made fast? Brother, I like not this.
For many men that stumble at the threshold
Are well foretold that danger lurks within.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Tush, man, abodements must not now affright us.
By fair or foul means we must enter in,
For hither will our friends repair to us.

speaker: HASTINGS
text: My liege, I’ll knock once more to summon them.

speaker: MAYOR
text:
My lords, we were forewarnèd of your coming,
And shut the gates for safety of ourselves,
For now we owe allegiance unto Henry.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
But, master mayor, if Henry be your king,
Yet Edward, at the least, is Duke of York.

speaker: MAYOR
text: True, my good lord, I know you for no less.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Why, and I challenge nothing but my dukedom,
As being well content with that alone.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
But when the fox hath once got in his nose,
He’ll soon find means to make the body follow.

speaker: HASTINGS
text:
Why, master mayor, why stand you in a doubt?
Open the gates. We are King Henry’s friends.

speaker: MAYOR
text: Ay, say you so? The gates shall then be opened.

speaker: RICHARD
text: A wise stout captain, and soon persuaded.

speaker: HASTINGS
text:
The good old man would fain that all were well,
So ’twere not long of him; but being entered,
I doubt not, I, but we shall soon persuade
Both him and all his brothers unto reason.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
So, master mayor, these gates must not be shut
But in the night or in the time of war.
What, fear not, man, but yield me up the keys.
For Edward will defend the town and thee
And all those friends that deign to follow me.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Brother, this is Sir John Montgomery,
Our trusty friend, unless I be deceived.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Welcome, Sir John. But why come you in arms?

speaker: MONTGOMERY
text:
To help King Edward in his time of storm,
As every loyal subject ought to do.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Thanks, good Montgomery. But we now forget
Our title to the crown, and only claim
Our dukedom, till God please to send the rest.

speaker: MONTGOMERY
text:
Then fare you well, for I will hence again.
I came to serve a king and not a duke.—
Drummer, strike up, and let us march away.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Nay, stay, Sir John, a while, and we’ll debate
By what safe means the crown may be recovered.

speaker: MONTGOMERY
text:
What talk you of debating? In few words,
If you’ll not here proclaim yourself our king,
I’ll leave you to your fortune and be gone
To keep them back that come to succor you.
Why shall we fight if you pretend no title?

speaker: RICHARD
text: Why, brother, wherefore stand you on nice points?

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
When we grow stronger, then we’ll make our claim.
Till then ’tis wisdom to conceal our meaning.

speaker: HASTINGS
text: Away with scrupulous wit! Now arms must rule.

speaker: RICHARD
KING EDWARD
text:
Then be it as you will, for ’tis my right,
And Henry but usurps the diadem.

speaker: MONTGOMERY
text:
Ay, now my sovereign speaketh like himself,
And now will I be Edward’s champion.

speaker: HASTINGS
text:
Sound, trumpet! Edward shall be here proclaimed.—
Come, fellow soldier, make thou proclamation.

speaker: SOLDIER
text: Edward the Fourth , by the Grace of God , King of England and France , and Lord of Ireland , &c .

speaker: MONTGOMERY
text:
And whosoe’er gainsays King Edward’s right,
By this I challenge him to single fight.

speaker: ALL
text: Long live Edward the Fourth!

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Thanks, brave Montgomery, and thanks unto you all.
If fortune serve me, I’ll requite this kindness.
Now, for this night let’s harbor here in York,
And when the morning sun shall raise his car
Above the border of this horizon,
We’ll forward towards Warwick and his mates;
For well I wot that Henry is no soldier.
Ah, froward Clarence, how evil it beseems thee
To flatter Henry and forsake thy brother!
Yet, as we may, we’ll meet both thee and Warwick.
Come on, brave soldiers; doubt not of the day;
And that once gotten, doubt not of large pay.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
What counsel, lords? Edward from Belgia,
With hasty Germans and blunt Hollanders,
Hath passed in safety through the Narrow Seas,
And with his troops doth march amain to London,
And many giddy people flock to him.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Let’s levy men and beat him back again.

speaker: CLARENCE
text:
A little fire is quickly trodden out,
Which, being suffered, rivers cannot quench.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
In Warwickshire I have true-hearted friends,
Not mutinous in peace yet bold in war.
Those will I muster up; and thou, son Clarence,
Shalt stir up in Suffolk, Norfolk, and in Kent
The knights and gentlemen to come with thee.—
Thou, brother Montague, in Buckingham,
Northampton, and in Leicestershire shalt find
Men well inclined to hear what thou command’st.—
And thou, brave Oxford, wondrous well beloved,
In Oxfordshire shalt muster up thy friends.—
My sovereign, with the loving citizens,
Like to his island girt in with the ocean,
Or modest Dian circled with her nymphs,
Shall rest in London till we come to him.
Fair lords, take leave, and stand not to reply.—
Farewell, my sovereign.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Farewell, my Hector and my Troy’s true hope.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: In sign of truth, I kiss your Highness’ hand.

speaker: KING HENRY
text: Well-minded Clarence, be thou fortunate.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: Comfort, my lord; and so I take my leave.

speaker: OXFORD
text: And thus I seal my truth, and bid adieu.

speaker: KING HENRY
text:
Sweet Oxford and my loving Montague
And all at once, once more a happy farewell.

speaker: WARWICK
text: Farewell, sweet lords. Let’s meet at Coventry.

speaker: KING HENRY
text:
Here at the palace will I rest awhile.
Cousin of Exeter, what thinks your Lordship?
Methinks the power that Edward hath in field
Should not be able to encounter mine.

speaker: EXETER
text: The doubt is that he will seduce the rest.

speaker: KING HENRY
text:
That’s not my fear. My meed hath got me fame.
I have not stopped mine ears to their demands,
Nor posted off their suits with slow delays.
My pity hath been balm to heal their wounds,
My mildness hath allayed their swelling griefs,
My mercy dried their water-flowing tears.
I have not been desirous of their wealth
Nor much oppressed them with great subsidies,
Nor forward of revenge, though they much erred.
Then why should they love Edward more than me?
No, Exeter, these graces challenge grace;
And when the lion fawns upon the lamb,
The lamb will never cease to follow him.

speaker: EXETER
text: Hark, hark, my lord, what shouts are these?

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Seize on the shamefaced Henry, bear him hence,
And once again proclaim us King of England.—
You are the fount that makes small brooks to flow.
Now stops thy spring; my sea shall suck them dry
And swell so much the higher by their ebb.—
Hence with him to the Tower. Let him not speak.
And, lords, towards Coventry bend we our course,
Where peremptory Warwick now remains.
The sun shines hot, and if we use delay,
Cold biting winter mars our hoped-for hay.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Away betimes, before his forces join,
And take the great-grown traitor unawares.
Brave warriors, march amain towards Coventry.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Where is the post that came from valiant Oxford?—
How far hence is thy lord, mine honest fellow?

speaker: FIRST MESSENGER
text: By this at Dunsmore, marching hitherward.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
How far off is our brother Montague?
Where is the post that came from Montague?

speaker: SECOND MESSENGER
text: By this at Daintry, with a puissant troop.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Say, Somerville, what says my loving son?
And, by thy guess, how nigh is Clarence now?

speaker: SOMERVILLE
text:
At Southam I did leave him with his forces
And do expect him here some two hours hence.

speaker: WARWICK
text: Then Clarence is at hand; I hear his drum.

speaker: SOMERVILLE
text:
It is not his, my lord; here Southam lies.
The drum your Honor hears marcheth from Warwick.

speaker: WARWICK
text: Who should that be? Belike unlooked-for friends.

speaker: SOMERVILLE
text: They are at hand, and you shall quickly know.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Go, Trumpet, to the walls, and sound a parle.

speaker: RICHARD
text: See how the surly Warwick mans the wall.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
O unbid spite, is sportful Edward come?
Where slept our scouts, or how are they seduced,
That we could hear no news of his repair?

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Now, Warwick, wilt thou ope the city gates,
Speak gentle words, and humbly bend thy knee?
Call Edward king, and at his hands beg mercy,
And he shall pardon thee these outrages.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Nay, rather wilt thou draw thy forces hence,
Confess who set thee up and plucked thee down,
Call Warwick patron, and be penitent,
And thou shalt still remain the Duke of York.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
I thought at least he would have said “the King.”
Or did he make the jest against his will?

speaker: WARWICK
text: Is not a dukedom, sir, a goodly gift?

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Ay, by my faith, for a poor earl to give.
I’ll do thee service for so good a gift.

speaker: WARWICK
text: ’Twas I that gave the kingdom to thy brother.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Why, then, ’tis mine, if but by Warwick’s gift.

speaker: WARWICK
KING EDWARD
text:
But Warwick’s king is Edward’s prisoner.
And, gallant Warwick, do but answer this:
What is the body when the head is off?

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Alas, that Warwick had no more forecast,
But whiles he thought to steal the single ten,
The King was slyly fingered from the deck.
You left poor Henry at the Bishop’s palace,
And ten to one you’ll meet him in the Tower.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: ’Tis even so; yet you are Warwick still.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Come, Warwick, take the time; kneel down, kneel down.
Nay, when? Strike now, or else the iron cools.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
I had rather chop this hand off at a blow
And with the other fling it at thy face
Than bear so low a sail to strike to thee.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Sail how thou canst, have wind and tide thy friend,
This hand, fast wound about thy coal-black hair,
Shall, whiles thy head is warm and new cut off,
Write in the dust this sentence with thy blood:
“Wind-changing Warwick now can change no more.”

speaker: WARWICK
text: O, cheerful colors, see where Oxford comes!

speaker: OXFORD
text: Oxford, Oxford for Lancaster!

speaker: RICHARD
text: The gates are open; let us enter too.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
So other foes may set upon our backs.
Stand we in good array, for they no doubt
Will issue out again and bid us battle.
If not, the city being but of small defense,
We’ll quickly rouse the traitors in the same.

speaker: WARWICK
text: O welcome, Oxford, for we want thy help.

speaker: MONTAGUE
text: Montague, Montague for Lancaster!

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Thou and thy brother both shall buy this treason
Even with the dearest blood your bodies bear!

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
The harder matched, the greater victory.
My mind presageth happy gain and conquest.

speaker: SOMERSET
text: Somerset, Somerset for Lancaster!

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Two of thy name, both dukes of Somerset,
Have sold their lives unto the house of York,
And thou shalt be the third, if this sword hold.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
And lo, where George of Clarence sweeps along,
Of force enough to bid his brother battle,
With whom an upright zeal to right prevails
More than the nature of a brother’s love.—
Come, Clarence, come; thou wilt, if Warwick call.

speaker: CLARENCE
text:
Father of Warwick, know you what this means?
Look, here I throw my infamy at thee.
I will not ruinate my father’s house,
Who gave his blood to lime the stones together
And set up Lancaster. Why, trowest thou, Warwick,
That Clarence is so harsh, so blunt, unnatural,
To bend the fatal instruments of war
Against his brother and his lawful king?
Perhaps thou wilt object my holy oath.
To keep that oath were more impiety
Than Jephthah when he sacrificed his daughter.
I am so sorry for my trespass made
That, to deserve well at my brother’s hands,
I here proclaim myself thy mortal foe,
With resolution, wheresoe’er I meet thee—
As I will meet thee if thou stir abroad—
To plague thee for thy foul misleading me.
And so, proud-hearted Warwick, I defy thee
And to my brother turn my blushing cheeks.—
Pardon me, Edward, I will make amends.—
And, Richard, do not frown upon my faults,
For I will henceforth be no more unconstant.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Now, welcome more, and ten times more beloved,
Than if thou never hadst deserved our hate.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Welcome, good Clarence; this is brother-like.

speaker: WARWICK
text: O, passing traitor, perjured and unjust.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
What, Warwick, wilt thou leave the town and fight?
Or shall we beat the stones about thine ears?

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Alas, I am not cooped here for defense.
I will away towards Barnet presently
And bid thee battle, Edward, if thou dar’st.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Yes, Warwick, Edward dares, and leads the way.—
Lords, to the field! Saint George and victory!

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
So, lie thou there. Die thou, and die our fear,
For Warwick was a bug that feared us all.
Now, Montague, sit fast. I seek for thee,
That Warwick’s bones may keep thine company.

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Ah, who is nigh? Come to me, friend or foe,
And tell me who is victor, York or Warwick?
Why ask I that? My mangled body shows,
My blood, my want of strength, my sick heart shows
That I must yield my body to the earth
And, by my fall, the conquest to my foe.
Thus yields the cedar to the axe’s edge,
Whose arms gave shelter to the princely eagle,
Under whose shade the ramping lion slept,
Whose top branch overpeered Jove’s spreading tree
And kept low shrubs from winter’s pow’rful wind.
These eyes, that now are dimmed with death’s black veil,
Have been as piercing as the midday sun
To search the secret treasons of the world.
The wrinkles in my brows, now filled with blood,
Were likened oft to kingly sepulchers,
For who lived king but I could dig his grave?
And who durst smile when Warwick bent his brow?
Lo, now my glory smeared in dust and blood!
My parks, my walks, my manors that I had
Even now forsake me; and of all my lands
Is nothing left me but my body’s length.
Why, what is pomp, rule, reign, but earth and dust?
And live we how we can, yet die we must.

speaker: SOMERSET
text:
Ah, Warwick, Warwick, wert thou as we are,
We might recover all our loss again.
The Queen from France hath brought a puissant power;
Even now we heard the news. Ah, could’st thou fly—

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Why, then, I would not fly. Ah, Montague,
If thou be there, sweet brother, take my hand
And with thy lips keep in my soul awhile.
Thou lov’st me not, for, brother, if thou didst,
Thy tears would wash this cold congealèd blood
That glues my lips and will not let me speak.
Come quickly, Montague, or I am dead.

speaker: SOMERSET
text:
Ah, Warwick, Montague hath breathed his last,
And to the latest gasp cried out for Warwick,
And said “Commend me to my valiant brother.”
And more he would have said, and more he spoke,
Which sounded like a cannon in a vault,
That mought not be distinguished, but at last
I well might hear, delivered with a groan,
“O, farewell, Warwick.”

speaker: WARWICK
text:
Sweet rest his soul! Fly, lords, and save yourselves,
For Warwick bids you all farewell to meet in heaven.

speaker: OXFORD
text: Away, away, to meet the Queen’s great power!

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Thus far our fortune keeps an upward course,
And we are graced with wreaths of victory.
But in the midst of this bright-shining day,
I spy a black suspicious threat’ning cloud
That will encounter with our glorious sun
Ere he attain his easeful western bed.
I mean, my lords, those powers that the Queen
Hath raised in Gallia have arrived our coast
And, as we hear, march on to fight with us.

speaker: CLARENCE
text:
A little gale will soon disperse that cloud
And blow it to the source from whence it came;
Thy very beams will dry those vapors up,
For every cloud engenders not a storm.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
The Queen is valued thirty thousand strong,
And Somerset, with Oxford, fled to her.
If she have time to breathe, be well assured
Her faction will be full as strong as ours.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
We are advertised by our loving friends
That they do hold their course toward Tewkesbury.
We having now the best at Barnet Field
Will thither straight, for willingness rids way,
And, as we march, our strength will be augmented
In every county as we go along.
Strike up the drum, cry “Courage!” and away.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
Great lords, wise men ne’er sit and wail their loss
But cheerly seek how to redress their harms.
What though the mast be now blown overboard,
The cable broke, the holding-anchor lost,
And half our sailors swallowed in the flood?
Yet lives our pilot still. Is ’t meet that he
Should leave the helm and, like a fearful lad,
With tearful eyes add water to the sea
And give more strength to that which hath too much,
Whiles in his moan the ship splits on the rock,
Which industry and courage might have saved?
Ah, what a shame, ah, what a fault were this!
Say Warwick was our anchor; what of that?
And Montague our topmast; what of him?
Our slaughtered friends the tackles; what of these?
Why, is not Oxford here another anchor?
And Somerset another goodly mast?
The friends of France our shrouds and tacklings?
And, though unskillful, why not Ned and I
For once allowed the skillful pilot’s charge?
We will not from the helm to sit and weep,
But keep our course, though the rough wind say no,
From shelves and rocks that threaten us with wrack.
As good to chide the waves as speak them fair.
And what is Edward but a ruthless sea?
What Clarence but a quicksand of deceit?
And Richard but a ragged fatal rock—
All these the enemies to our poor bark?
Say you can swim: alas, ’tis but awhile;
Tread on the sand: why, there you quickly sink;
Bestride the rock: the tide will wash you off
Or else you famish; that’s a threefold death.
This speak I, lords, to let you understand,
If case some one of you would fly from us,
That there’s no hoped-for mercy with the brothers
More than with ruthless waves, with sands and rocks.
Why, courage then! What cannot be avoided
’Twere childish weakness to lament or fear.

speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
text:
Methinks a woman of this valiant spirit
Should, if a coward heard her speak these words,
Infuse his breast with magnanimity
And make him, naked, foil a man-at-arms.
I speak not this as doubting any here,
For did I but suspect a fearful man,
He should have leave to go away betimes,
Lest in our need he might infect another
And make him of like spirit to himself.
If any such be here, as God forbid,
Let him depart before we need his help.

speaker: OXFORD
text:
Women and children of so high a courage,
And warriors faint? Why, ’twere perpetual shame!
O, brave young prince, thy famous grandfather
Doth live again in thee. Long mayst thou live
To bear his image and renew his glories!

speaker: SOMERSET
text:
And he that will not fight for such a hope,
Go home to bed and, like the owl by day,
If he arise, be mocked and wondered at.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: Thanks, gentle Somerset.—Sweet Oxford, thanks.

speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
text: And take his thanks that yet hath nothing else.

speaker: MESSENGER
text:
Prepare you, lords, for Edward is at hand,
Ready to fight. Therefore be resolute.

speaker: OXFORD
text:
I thought no less. It is his policy
To haste thus fast to find us unprovided.

speaker: SOMERSET
text: But he’s deceived. We are in readiness.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: This cheers my heart to see your forwardness.

speaker: OXFORD
text: Here pitch our battle; hence we will not budge.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Brave followers, yonder stands the thorny wood
Which by the heavens’ assistance and your strength
Must by the roots be hewn up yet ere night.
I need not add more fuel to your fire,
For, well I wot, you blaze to burn them out.
Give signal to the fight, and to it, lords!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
Lords, knights, and gentlemen, what I should say
My tears gainsay, for every word I speak
You see I drink the water of my eye.
Therefore, no more but this: Henry, your sovereign,
Is prisoner to the foe, his state usurped,
His realm a slaughterhouse, his subjects slain,
His statutes cancelled and his treasure spent,
And yonder is the wolf that makes this spoil.
You fight in justice. Then, in God’s name, lords,
Be valiant, and give signal to the fight!

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Now here a period of tumultuous broils.
Away with Oxford to Hames Castle straight.
For Somerset, off with his guilty head.
Go bear them hence. I will not hear them speak.

speaker: OXFORD
text: For my part, I’ll not trouble thee with words.

speaker: SOMERSET
text: Nor I, but stoop with patience to my fortune.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
So part we sadly in this troublous world
To meet with joy in sweet Jerusalem.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Is proclamation made that who finds Edward
Shall have a high reward, and he his life?

speaker: RICHARD
text: It is, and lo where youthful Edward comes.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Bring forth the gallant; let us hear him speak.
What, can so young a thorn begin to prick?—
Edward, what satisfaction canst thou make
For bearing arms, for stirring up my subjects,
And all the trouble thou hast turned me to?

speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
text:
Speak like a subject, proud ambitious York.
Suppose that I am now my father’s mouth:
Resign thy chair, and where I stand, kneel thou,
Whilst I propose the selfsame words to thee
Which, traitor, thou wouldst have me answer to.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: Ah, that thy father had been so resolved!

speaker: RICHARD
text:
That you might still have worn the petticoat
And ne’er have stol’n the breech from Lancaster.

speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
text:
Let Aesop fable in a winter’s night;
His currish riddles sorts not with this place.

speaker: RICHARD
text: By heaven, brat, I’ll plague you for that word.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: Ay, thou wast born to be a plague to men.

speaker: RICHARD
text: For God’s sake, take away this captive scold.

speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
text: Nay, take away this scolding crookback, rather.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Peace, willful boy, or I will charm your tongue.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Untutored lad, thou art too malapert.

speaker: PRINCE EDWARD
text:
I know my duty. You are all undutiful.
Lascivious Edward, and thou perjured George,
And thou misshapen Dick, I tell you all
I am your better, traitors as you are,
And thou usurp’st my father’s right and mine.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Take that, the likeness of this railer here!

speaker: RICHARD
text: Sprawl’st thou? Take that to end thy agony!

speaker: CLARENCE
text: And there’s for twitting me with perjury.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: O, kill me too!

speaker: RICHARD
text: Marry, and shall.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Hold, Richard, hold, for we have done too much.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Why should she live to fill the world with words?

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: What, doth she swoon? Use means for her recovery.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Clarence, excuse me to the King my brother.
I’ll hence to London on a serious matter.
Ere you come there, be sure to hear some news.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: What? What?

speaker: RICHARD
text: The Tower, the Tower!

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
O Ned, sweet Ned, speak to thy mother, boy.
Canst thou not speak? O traitors, murderers!
They that stabbed Caesar shed no blood at all,
Did not offend, nor were not worthy blame,
If this foul deed were by to equal it.
He was a man; this, in respect, a child,
And men ne’er spend their fury on a child.
What’s worse than murderer, that I may name it?
No, no, my heart will burst an if I speak,
And I will speak, that so my heart may burst.
Butchers and villains, bloody cannibals,
How sweet a plant have you untimely cropped!
You have no children, butchers. If you had,
The thought of them would have stirred up remorse.
But if you ever chance to have a child,
Look in his youth to have him so cut off
As, deathsmen, you have rid this sweet young prince.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Away with her. Go bear her hence perforce.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
Nay, never bear me hence! Dispatch me here.
Here sheathe thy sword; I’ll pardon thee my death.
What, wilt thou not?—Then, Clarence, do it thou.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: By heaven, I will not do thee so much ease.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: Good Clarence, do! Sweet Clarence, do thou do it.

speaker: CLARENCE
text: Didst thou not hear me swear I would not do it?

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text:
Ay, but thou usest to forswear thyself.
’Twas sin before, but now ’tis charity.
What, wilt thou not? Where is that devil’s butcher, Richard,
Hard-favored Richard? Richard, where art thou?
Thou art not here. Murder is thy alms-deed;
Petitioners for blood thou ne’er putt’st back.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Away, I say! I charge you bear her hence.

speaker: QUEEN MARGARET
text: So come to you and yours as to this prince!

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Where’s Richard gone?

speaker: CLARENCE
text:
To London all in post, and, as I guess,
To make a bloody supper in the Tower.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
He’s sudden if a thing comes in his head.
Now march we hence. Discharge the common sort
With pay and thanks, and let’s away to London
And see our gentle queen how well she fares.
By this I hope she hath a son for me.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Good day, my lord. What, at your book so hard?

speaker: KING HENRY
text:
Ay, my good lord—“my lord,” I should say rather.
’Tis sin to flatter; “good” was little better:
“Good Gloucester” and “good devil” were alike,
And both preposterous: therefore, not “good lord.”

speaker: RICHARD
text: Sirrah, leave us to ourselves; we must confer.

speaker: KING HENRY
text:
So flies the reckless shepherd from the wolf;
So first the harmless sheep doth yield his fleece
And next his throat unto the butcher’s knife.
What scene of death hath Roscius now to act?

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Suspicion always haunts the guilty mind;
The thief doth fear each bush an officer.

speaker: KING HENRY
text:
The bird that hath been limèd in a bush,
With trembling wings misdoubteth every bush;
And I, the hapless male to one sweet bird,
Have now the fatal object in my eye
Where my poor young was limed, was caught, and killed.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
Why, what a peevish fool was that of Crete
That taught his son the office of a fowl!
And yet, for all his wings, the fool was drowned.

speaker: KING HENRY
text:
I Daedalus, my poor boy Icarus,
Thy father Minos, that denied our course;
The sun that seared the wings of my sweet boy
Thy brother Edward, and thyself the sea
Whose envious gulf did swallow up his life.
Ah, kill me with thy weapon, not with words!
My breast can better brook thy dagger’s point
Than can my ears that tragic history.
But wherefore dost thou come? Is ’t for my life?

speaker: RICHARD
text: Think’st thou I am an executioner?

speaker: KING HENRY
text:
A persecutor I am sure thou art.
If murdering innocents be executing,
Why, then, thou art an executioner.

speaker: RICHARD
text: Thy son I killed for his presumption.

speaker: KING HENRY
text:
Hadst thou been killed when first thou didst presume,
Thou hadst not lived to kill a son of mine.
And thus I prophesy: that many a thousand
Which now mistrust no parcel of my fear,
And many an old man’s sigh, and many a widow’s
And many an orphan’s water-standing eye,
Men for their sons, wives for their husbands,
Orphans for their parents’ timeless death,
Shall rue the hour that ever thou wast born.
The owl shrieked at thy birth, an evil sign;
The night-crow cried, aboding luckless time;
Dogs howled, and hideous tempest shook down trees;
The raven rooked her on the chimney’s top;
And chatt’ring pies in dismal discords sung;
Thy mother felt more than a mother’s pain,
And yet brought forth less than a mother’s hope:
To wit, an indigested and deformèd lump,
Not like the fruit of such a goodly tree.
Teeth hadst thou in thy head when thou wast born
To signify thou cam’st to bite the world.
And if the rest be true which I have heard,
Thou cam’st—

speaker: RICHARD
text:
I’ll hear no more. Die, prophet, in thy speech;
For this amongst the rest was I ordained.

speaker: KING HENRY
text:
Ay, and for much more slaughter after this.
O God, forgive my sins, and pardon thee.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
What, will the aspiring blood of Lancaster
Sink in the ground? I thought it would have mounted.
See how my sword weeps for the poor king’s death.
O, may such purple tears be always shed
From those that wish the downfall of our house.
If any spark of life be yet remaining,
Down, down to hell, and say I sent thee thither—
I that have neither pity, love, nor fear.
Indeed, ’tis true that Henry told me of,
For I have often heard my mother say
I came into the world with my legs forward.
Had I not reason, think you, to make haste
And seek their ruin that usurped our right?
The midwife wondered, and the women cried
“O Jesus bless us, he is born with teeth!”
And so I was, which plainly signified
That I should snarl, and bite, and play the dog.
Then, since the heavens have shaped my body so,
Let hell make crook’d my mind to answer it.
I have no brother, I am like no brother;
And this word “love,” which graybeards call divine,
Be resident in men like one another
And not in me. I am myself alone.
Clarence, beware; thou keep’st me from the light,
But I will sort a pitchy day for thee;
For I will buzz abroad such prophecies
That Edward shall be fearful of his life;
And then to purge his fear, I’ll be thy death.
King Henry and the Prince his son are gone.
Clarence, thy turn is next, and then the rest,
Counting myself but bad till I be best.
I’ll throw thy body in another room,
And triumph, Henry, in thy day of doom.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Once more we sit in England’s royal throne,
Repurchased with the blood of enemies.
What valiant foemen, like to autumn’s corn,
Have we mowed down in tops of all their pride!
Three dukes of Somerset, threefold renowned
For hardy and undoubted champions;
Two Cliffords, as the father and the son;
And two Northumberlands; two braver men
Ne’er spurred their coursers at the trumpet’s sound.
With them the two brave bears, Warwick and Montague,
That in their chains fettered the kingly lion
And made the forest tremble when they roared.
Thus have we swept suspicion from our seat
And made our footstool of security.—
Come hither, Bess, and let me kiss my boy.—
Young Ned, for thee, thine uncles and myself
Have in our armors watched the winter’s night,
Went all afoot in summer’s scalding heat,
That thou mightst repossess the crown in peace,
And of our labors thou shalt reap the gain.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
I’ll blast his harvest, if your head were laid;
For yet I am not looked on in the world.
This shoulder was ordained so thick to heave,
And heave it shall some weight or break my back.
Work thou the way and that shalt execute.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Clarence and Gloucester, love my lovely queen,
And kiss your princely nephew, brothers both.

speaker: CLARENCE
text:
The duty that I owe unto your Majesty
I seal upon the lips of this sweet babe.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text: Thanks, noble Clarence; worthy brother, thanks.

speaker: RICHARD
text:
And that I love the tree from whence thou sprang’st,
Witness the loving kiss I give the fruit.
To say the truth, so Judas kissed his master
And cried “All hail!” whenas he meant all harm.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Now am I seated as my soul delights,
Having my country’s peace and brothers’ loves.

speaker: CLARENCE
text:
What will your Grace have done with Margaret?
Reignier, her father, to the King of France
Hath pawned the Sicils and Jerusalem,
And hither have they sent it for her ransom.

speaker: KING EDWARD
text:
Away with her, and waft her hence to France.
And now what rests but that we spend the time
With stately triumphs, mirthful comic shows,
Such as befits the pleasure of the court?
Sound drums and trumpets! Farewell, sour annoy,
For here I hope begins our lasting joy.

speaker: PROLOGUE
text:
I come no more to make you laugh. Things now
That bear a weighty and a serious brow,
Sad, high, and working, full of state and woe,
Such noble scenes as draw the eye to flow,
We now present. Those that can pity here
May, if they think it well, let fall a tear;
The subject will deserve it. Such as give
Their money out of hope they may believe
May here find truth too. Those that come to see
Only a show or two, and so agree
The play may pass, if they be still and willing,
I’ll undertake may see away their shilling
Richly in two short hours. Only they
That come to hear a merry, bawdy play,
A noise of targets, or to see a fellow
In a long motley coat guarded with yellow,
Will be deceived. For, gentle hearers, know
To rank our chosen truth with such a show
As fool and fight is, besides forfeiting
Our own brains and the opinion that we bring
To make that only true we now intend,
Will leave us never an understanding friend.
Therefore, for goodness’ sake, and as you are known
The first and happiest hearers of the town,
Be sad, as we would make you. Think you see
The very persons of our noble story
As they were living. Think you see them great,
And followed with the general throng and sweat
Of thousand friends. Then, in a moment, see
How soon this mightiness meets misery.
And if you can be merry then, I’ll say
A man may weep upon his wedding day.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text:
Good morrow, and well met. How have you done
Since last we saw in France?

speaker: NORFOLK
text:
I thank your Grace,
Healthful, and ever since a fresh admirer
Of what I saw there.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text:
An untimely ague
Stayed me a prisoner in my chamber when
Those suns of glory, those two lights of men,
Met in the vale of Andren.

speaker: NORFOLK
text:
’Twixt Guynes and Arde.
I was then present, saw them salute on horseback,
Beheld them when they lighted, how they clung
In their embracement, as they grew together—
Which had they, what four throned ones could have weighed
Such a compounded one?

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text:
All the whole time
I was my chamber’s prisoner.

speaker: NORFOLK
text:
Then you lost
The view of earthly glory. Men might say
Till this time pomp was single, but now married
To one above itself. Each following day
Became the next day’s master, till the last
Made former wonders its. Today the French,
All clinquant, all in gold, like heathen gods,
Shone down the English, and tomorrow they
Made Britain India: every man that stood
Showed like a mine. Their dwarfish pages were
As cherubins, all gilt. The madams too,
Not used to toil, did almost sweat to bear
The pride upon them, that their very labor
Was to them as a painting. Now this masque
Was cried incomparable; and th’ ensuing night
Made it a fool and beggar. The two kings,
Equal in luster, were now best, now worst,
As presence did present them: him in eye
Still him in praise; and being present both,
’Twas said they saw but one, and no discerner
Durst wag his tongue in censure. When these suns—
For so they phrase ’em—by their heralds challenged
The noble spirits to arms, they did perform
Beyond thought’s compass, that former fabulous story,
Being now seen possible enough, got credit
That Bevis was believed.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text: O, you go far.

speaker: NORFOLK
text:
As I belong to worship, and affect
In honor honesty, the tract of everything
Would by a good discourser lose some life
Which action’s self was tongue to. All was royal;
To the disposing of it naught rebelled.
Order gave each thing view. The office did
Distinctly his full function.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text:
Who did guide,
I mean who set the body and the limbs
Of this great sport together, as you guess?

speaker: NORFOLK
text:
One, certes, that promises no element
In such a business.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text: I pray you who, my lord?

speaker: NORFOLK
text:
All this was ordered by the good discretion
Of the right reverend Cardinal of York.

speaker: BUCKINGHAM
text:
The devil speed him! No man’s pie is freed
From his ambitious finger. What had he
To do in these fierce vanities? I wonder
That such a keech can with his very bulk
Take up the rays o’ th’ beneficial sun
And keep it from the Earth.

speaker: NORFOLK
text:
Surely, sir,
