If wolves had at thy gate howled that stern time,
Thou shouldst have said “Good porter, turn the key.”
All cruels else subscribe. But I shall see
The wingèd vengeance overtake such children.

speaker: CORNWALL
text:
See ’t shalt thou never.—Fellows, hold the chair.—
Upon these eyes of thine I’ll set my foot.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
He that will think to live till he be old,
Give me some help!
O cruel! O you gods!

speaker: REGAN
text: One side will mock another. Th’ other too.

speaker: CORNWALL
text: If you see vengeance—

speaker: FIRST SERVANT
text:
Hold your hand, my lord.
I have served you ever since I was a child,
But better service have I never done you
Than now to bid you hold.

speaker: REGAN
text: How now, you dog?

speaker: FIRST SERVANT
text:
If you did wear a beard upon your chin,
I’d shake it on this quarrel. What do you mean?

speaker: CORNWALL
text: My villain?

speaker: FIRST SERVANT
text: Nay, then, come on, and take the chance of anger.

speaker: REGAN
text: Give me thy sword. A peasant stand up thus?

speaker: FIRST SERVANT
text:
O, I am slain! My lord, you have one eye left
To see some mischief on him. O!

speaker: CORNWALL
text:
Lest it see more, prevent it. Out, vile jelly!
Where is thy luster now?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
All dark and comfortless! Where’s my son Edmund?—
Edmund, enkindle all the sparks of nature
To quit this horrid act.

speaker: REGAN
text:
Out, treacherous villain!
Thou call’st on him that hates thee. It was he
That made the overture of thy treasons to us,
Who is too good to pity thee.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
O my follies! Then Edgar was abused.
Kind gods, forgive me that, and prosper him.

speaker: REGAN
text:
Go thrust him out at gates, and let him smell
His way to Dover.
How is ’t, my lord? How look you?

speaker: CORNWALL
text:
I have received a hurt. Follow me, lady.—
Turn out that eyeless villain. Throw this slave
Upon the dunghill.—Regan, I bleed apace.
Untimely comes this hurt. Give me your arm.

speaker: SECOND SERVANT
text:
I’ll never care what wickedness I do
If this man come to good.

speaker: THIRD SERVANT
text:
If she live long
And in the end meet the old course of death,
Women will all turn monsters.

speaker: SECOND SERVANT
text:
Let’s follow the old earl and get the Bedlam
To lead him where he would. His roguish madness
Allows itself to anything.

speaker: THIRD SERVANT
text:
Go thou. I’ll fetch some flax and whites of eggs
To apply to his bleeding face. Now heaven help him!

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Yet better thus, and known to be contemned,
Than still contemned and flattered. To be worst,
The lowest and most dejected thing of Fortune,
Stands still in esperance, lives not in fear.
The lamentable change is from the best;
The worst returns to laughter. Welcome, then,
Thou unsubstantial air that I embrace.
The wretch that thou hast blown unto the worst
Owes nothing to thy blasts. But who comes here?
My father, poorly led? World, world, O world,
But that thy strange mutations make us hate thee,
Life would not yield to age.

speaker: OLD MAN
text:
O my good lord, I have been your tenant
And your father’s tenant these fourscore years.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
OLD MAN
text: You cannot see your way.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
I have no way and therefore want no eyes.
I stumbled when I saw. Full oft ’tis seen
Our means secure us, and our mere defects
Prove our commodities. O dear son Edgar,
The food of thy abusèd father’s wrath,
Might I but live to see thee in my touch,
I’d say I had eyes again.

speaker: OLD MAN
text: How now? Who’s there?

speaker: EDGAR
text:
O gods, who is ’t can say “I am at the worst”?
I am worse than e’er I was.

speaker: OLD MAN
text: ’Tis poor mad Tom.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
And worse I may be yet. The worst is not
So long as we can say “This is the worst.”

speaker: OLD MAN
text: Fellow, where goest?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Is it a beggar-man?

speaker: OLD MAN
text: Madman and beggar too.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
He has some reason, else he could not beg.
I’ th’ last night’s storm, I such a fellow saw,
Which made me think a man a worm. My son
Came then into my mind, and yet my mind
Was then scarce friends with him. I have heard more since.
As flies to wanton boys are we to th’ gods;
They kill us for their sport.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
How should this be?
Bad is the trade that must play fool to sorrow,
Ang’ring itself and others.—Bless thee, master.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Is that the naked fellow?

speaker: OLD MAN
text: Ay, my lord.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
Then, prithee, get thee away. If for my sake
Thou wilt o’ertake us hence a mile or twain
I’ th’ way toward Dover, do it for ancient love,
And bring some covering for this naked soul,
Which I’ll entreat to lead me.

speaker: OLD MAN
text: Alack, sir, he is mad.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
’Tis the time’s plague when madmen lead the blind.
Do as I bid thee, or rather do thy pleasure.
Above the rest, begone.

speaker: OLD MAN
text:
I’ll bring him the best ’parel that I have,
Come on ’t what will.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Sirrah, naked fellow—

speaker: EDGAR
text: Poor Tom’s a-cold. I cannot daub it further.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Come hither, fellow.

speaker: EDGAR
text: And yet I must.—Bless thy sweet eyes, they bleed.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Know’st thou the way to Dover?

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Both stile and gate, horseway and footpath.
Poor Tom hath been scared out of his good wits.
Bless thee, good man’s son, from the foul fiend.
Five fiends have been in Poor Tom at once: of lust,
as Obidicut; Hobbididance, prince of dumbness;
Mahu, of stealing; Modo, of murder; Flibbertigibbet,
of mopping and mowing, who since possesses
chambermaids and waiting women. So, bless
thee, master.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
Here, take this purse, thou whom the heavens’ plagues
Have humbled to all strokes. That I am wretched
Makes thee the happier. Heavens, deal so still:
Let the superfluous and lust-dieted man,
That slaves your ordinance, that will not see
Because he does not feel, feel your power quickly.
So distribution should undo excess
And each man have enough. Dost thou know Dover?

speaker: EDGAR
text: Ay, master.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
There is a cliff, whose high and bending head
Looks fearfully in the confinèd deep.
Bring me but to the very brim of it,
And I’ll repair the misery thou dost bear
With something rich about me. From that place
I shall no leading need.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Give me thy arm.
Poor Tom shall lead thee.

speaker: GONERIL
text:
Welcome, my lord. I marvel our mild husband
Not met us on the way.
Now, where’s your master?

speaker: OSWALD
GONERIL
text:
Then shall you go no further.
It is the cowish terror of his spirit,
That dares not undertake. He’ll not feel wrongs
Which tie him to an answer. Our wishes on the way
May prove effects. Back, Edmund, to my brother.
Hasten his musters and conduct his powers.
I must change names at home and give the distaff
Into my husband’s hands. This trusty servant
Shall pass between us. Ere long you are like to hear—
If you dare venture in your own behalf—
A mistress’s command. Wear this; spare speech.
Decline your head. This kiss, if it durst speak,
Would stretch thy spirits up into the air.
Conceive, and fare thee well.

speaker: EDMUND
text: Yours in the ranks of death.

speaker: GONERIL
text:
My most dear Gloucester!
O, the difference of man and man!
To thee a woman’s services are due;
My fool usurps my body.

speaker: OSWALD
text: Madam, here comes my lord.

speaker: GONERIL
text: I have been worth the whistle.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
O Goneril,
You are not worth the dust which the rude wind
Blows in your face. I fear your disposition.
That nature which contemns its origin
Cannot be bordered certain in itself.
She that herself will sliver and disbranch
From her material sap perforce must wither
And come to deadly use.

speaker: GONERIL
text: No more. The text is foolish.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Wisdom and goodness to the vile seem vile.
Filths savor but themselves. What have you done?
Tigers, not daughters, what have you performed?
A father, and a gracious agèd man,
Whose reverence even the head-lugged bear would lick,
Most barbarous, most degenerate, have you madded.
Could my good brother suffer you to do it?
A man, a prince, by him so benefited!
If that the heavens do not their visible spirits
Send quickly down to tame these vile offenses,
It will come:
Humanity must perforce prey on itself,
Like monsters of the deep.

speaker: GONERIL
text:
Milk-livered man,
That bear’st a cheek for blows, a head for wrongs;
Who hast not in thy brows an eye discerning
Thine honor from thy suffering; that not know’st
Fools do those villains pity who are punished
Ere they have done their mischief. Where’s thy drum?
France spreads his banners in our noiseless land,
With plumèd helm thy state begins to threat,
Whilst thou, a moral fool, sits still and cries
“Alack, why does he so?”

speaker: ALBANY
text:
See thyself, devil!
Proper deformity shows not in the fiend
So horrid as in woman.

speaker: GONERIL
text: O vain fool!

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Thou changèd and self-covered thing, for shame
Bemonster not thy feature. Were ’t my fitness
To let these hands obey my blood,
They are apt enough to dislocate and tear
Thy flesh and bones. Howe’er thou art a fiend,
A woman’s shape doth shield thee.

speaker: GONERIL
text: Marry, your manhood, mew—

speaker: ALBANY
text: What news?

speaker: MESSENGER
text:
O, my good lord, the Duke of Cornwall’s dead,
Slain by his servant, going to put out
The other eye of Gloucester.

speaker: ALBANY
text: Gloucester’s eyes?

speaker: MESSENGER
text:
A servant that he bred, thrilled with remorse,
Opposed against the act, bending his sword
To his great master, who, thereat enraged,
Flew on him and amongst them felled him dead,
But not without that harmful stroke which since
Hath plucked him after.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
This shows you are above,
You justicers, that these our nether crimes
So speedily can venge. But, O poor Gloucester,
Lost he his other eye?

speaker: MESSENGER
text:
Both, both, my lord.—
This letter, madam, craves a speedy answer.
’Tis from your sister.

speaker: GONERIL
text:
One way I like this well.
But being widow and my Gloucester with her
May all the building in my fancy pluck
Upon my hateful life. Another way
The news is not so tart.—I’ll read, and answer.

speaker: ALBANY
text: Where was his son when they did take his eyes?

speaker: MESSENGER
text: Come with my lady hither.

speaker: ALBANY
text: He is not here.

speaker: MESSENGER
text: No, my good lord. I met him back again.

speaker: ALBANY
text: Knows he the wickedness?

speaker: MESSENGER
text:
Ay, my good lord. ’Twas he informed against him
And quit the house on purpose, that their punishment
Might have the freer course.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Gloucester, I live
To thank thee for the love thou show’d’st the King,
And to revenge thine eyes.—Come hither, friend.
Tell me what more thou know’st.

speaker: KENT
text:
Why the King of France is so suddenly gone
back know you no reason?

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text:
Something he left imperfect in the state,
which since his coming forth is thought of, which
imports to the kingdom so much fear and danger
that his personal return was most required and
necessary.

speaker: KENT
text: Who hath he left behind him general?

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text: The Marshal of France, Monsieur La Far.

speaker: KENT
text:
Did your letters pierce the Queen to any demonstration
of grief?

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text:
Ay, sir, she took them, read them in my presence,
And now and then an ample tear trilled down
Her delicate cheek. It seemed she was a queen
Over her passion, who, most rebel-like,
Fought to be king o’er her.

speaker: KENT
text: O, then it moved her.

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text:
Not to a rage. Patience and sorrow strove
Who should express her goodliest. You have seen
Sunshine and rain at once; her smiles and tears
Were like a better way. Those happy smilets
That played on her ripe lip seemed not to know
What guests were in her eyes, which parted thence
As pearls from diamonds dropped. In brief,
Sorrow would be a rarity most beloved
If all could so become it.

speaker: KENT
text: Made she no verbal question?

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text:
Faith, once or twice she heaved the name of “father”
Pantingly forth, as if it pressed her heart;
Cried “Sisters, sisters, shame of ladies, sisters!
Kent, father, sisters! What, i’ th’ storm, i’ th’ night?
Let pity not be believed!” There she shook
The holy water from her heavenly eyes,
And clamor moistened. Then away she started,
To deal with grief alone.

speaker: KENT
text:
It is the stars.
The stars above us govern our conditions,
Else one self mate and make could not beget
Such different issues. You spoke not with her since?

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text: No.

speaker: KENT
text: Was this before the King returned?

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text: No, since.

speaker: KENT
text:
Well, sir, the poor distressèd Lear’s i’ th’ town,
Who sometime in his better tune remembers
What we are come about, and by no means
Will yield to see his daughter.

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text: Why, good sir?

speaker: KENT
text:
A sovereign shame so elbows him—his own unkindness,
That stripped her from his benediction, turned her
To foreign casualties, gave her dear rights
To his dog-hearted daughters—these things sting
His mind so venomously that burning shame
Detains him from Cordelia.

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text: Alack, poor gentleman!

speaker: KENT
text: Of Albany’s and Cornwall’s powers you heard not?

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text: ’Tis so. They are afoot.

speaker: KENT
text:
Well, sir, I’ll bring you to our master Lear
And leave you to attend him. Some dear cause
Will in concealment wrap me up awhile.
When I am known aright, you shall not grieve
Lending me this acquaintance. I pray you, go
Along with me.

speaker: CORDELIA
text:
Alack, ’tis he! Why, he was met even now
As mad as the vexed sea, singing aloud,
Crowned with rank fumiter and furrow-weeds,
With hardocks, hemlock, nettles, cuckooflowers,
Darnel, and all the idle weeds that grow
In our sustaining corn. A century send forth.
Search every acre in the high-grown field
And bring him to our eye.
What can man’s wisdom
In the restoring his bereavèd sense?
He that helps him take all my outward worth.

speaker: DOCTOR
text:
There is means, madam.
Our foster nurse of nature is repose,
The which he lacks. That to provoke in him
Are many simples operative, whose power
Will close the eye of anguish.

speaker: CORDELIA
text:
All blest secrets,
All you unpublished virtues of the earth,
Spring with my tears. Be aidant and remediate
In the good man’s distress. Seek, seek for him,
Lest his ungoverned rage dissolve the life
That wants the means to lead it.

speaker: MESSENGER
text:
News, madam.
The British powers are marching hitherward.

speaker: CORDELIA
text:
’Tis known before. Our preparation stands
In expectation of them.—O dear father,
It is thy business that I go about.
Therefore great France
My mourning and importuned tears hath pitied.
No blown ambition doth our arms incite,
But love, dear love, and our aged father’s right.
Soon may I hear and see him.

speaker: REGAN
text: But are my brother’s powers set forth?

speaker: OSWALD
text: Ay, madam.

speaker: REGAN
text: Himself in person there?

speaker: OSWALD
text:
Madam, with much ado.
Your sister is the better soldier.

speaker: REGAN
text: Lord Edmund spake not with your lord at home?

speaker: OSWALD
text: No, madam.

speaker: REGAN
text: What might import my sister’s letter to him?

speaker: OSWALD
text: I know not, lady.

speaker: REGAN
text:
Faith, he is posted hence on serious matter.
It was great ignorance, Gloucester’s eyes being out,
To let him live. Where he arrives he moves
All hearts against us. Edmund, I think, is gone,
In pity of his misery, to dispatch
His nighted life; moreover to descry
The strength o’ th’ enemy.

speaker: OSWALD
text: I must needs after him, madam, with my letter.

speaker: REGAN
text:
Our troops set forth tomorrow. Stay with us.
The ways are dangerous.

speaker: OSWALD
text:
I may not, madam.
My lady charged my duty in this business.

speaker: REGAN
text:
Why should she write to Edmund? Might not you
Transport her purposes by word? Belike,
Some things—I know not what. I’ll love thee much—
Let me unseal the letter.

speaker: OSWALD
text: Madam, I had rather—

speaker: REGAN
text:
I know your lady does not love her husband;
I am sure of that; and at her late being here,
She gave strange eliads and most speaking looks
To noble Edmund. I know you are of her bosom.

speaker: OSWALD
text: I, madam?

speaker: REGAN
text:
I speak in understanding. Y’ are; I know ’t.
Therefore I do advise you take this note:
My lord is dead; Edmund and I have talked,
And more convenient is he for my hand
Than for your lady’s. You may gather more.
If you do find him, pray you, give him this,
And when your mistress hears thus much from you,
I pray, desire her call her wisdom to her.
So, fare you well.
If you do chance to hear of that blind traitor,
Preferment falls on him that cuts him off.

speaker: OSWALD
text:
Would I could meet him, madam. I should show
What party I do follow.

speaker: REGAN
text: Fare thee well.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: When shall I come to th’ top of that same hill?

speaker: EDGAR
text: You do climb up it now. Look how we labor.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Methinks the ground is even.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Horrible steep.
Hark, do you hear the sea?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: No, truly.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Why then, your other senses grow imperfect
By your eyes’ anguish.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
So may it be indeed.
Methinks thy voice is altered and thou speak’st
In better phrase and matter than thou didst.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
You’re much deceived; in nothing am I changed
But in my garments.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Methinks you’re better spoken.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Come on, sir. Here’s the place. Stand still. How fearful
And dizzy ’tis to cast one’s eyes so low!
The crows and choughs that wing the midway air
Show scarce so gross as beetles. Halfway down
Hangs one that gathers samphire—dreadful trade;
Methinks he seems no bigger than his head.
The fishermen that walk upon the beach
Appear like mice, and yond tall anchoring bark
Diminished to her cock, her cock a buoy
Almost too small for sight. The murmuring surge
That on th’ unnumbered idle pebble chafes
Cannot be heard so high. I’ll look no more
Lest my brain turn and the deficient sight
Topple down headlong.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Set me where you stand.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Give me your hand. You are now within a foot
Of th’ extreme verge. For all beneath the moon
Would I not leap upright.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
Let go my hand.
Here, friend, ’s another purse; in it a jewel
Well worth a poor man’s taking. Fairies and gods
Prosper it with thee.
Go thou further off.
Bid me farewell, and let me hear thee going.

speaker: EDGAR
text: Now fare you well, good sir.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: With all my heart.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Why I do trifle thus with his despair
Is done to cure it.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
O you mighty gods!
This world I do renounce, and in your sights
Shake patiently my great affliction off.
If I could bear it longer, and not fall
To quarrel with your great opposeless wills,
My snuff and loathèd part of nature should
Burn itself out. If Edgar live, O, bless him!—
Now, fellow, fare thee well.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Gone, sir. Farewell.—
And yet I know not how conceit may rob
The treasury of life, when life itself
Yields to the theft. Had he been where he thought,
By this had thought been past. Alive or dead?—
Ho you, sir! Friend, hear you. Sir, speak.—
Thus might he pass indeed. Yet he revives.—
What are you, sir?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Away, and let me die.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Hadst thou been aught but gossamer, feathers, air,
So many fathom down precipitating,
Thou ’dst shivered like an egg; but thou dost breathe,
Hast heavy substance, bleed’st not, speak’st, art sound.
Ten masts at each make not the altitude
Which thou hast perpendicularly fell.
Thy life’s a miracle. Speak yet again.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: But have I fall’n or no?

speaker: EDGAR
text:
From the dread summit of this chalky bourn.
Look up a-height. The shrill-gorged lark so far
Cannot be seen or heard. Do but look up.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
Alack, I have no eyes.
Is wretchedness deprived that benefit
To end itself by death? ’Twas yet some comfort
When misery could beguile the tyrant’s rage
And frustrate his proud will.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Give me your arm.
Up. So, how is ’t? Feel you your legs? You stand.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Too well, too well.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
This is above all strangeness.
Upon the crown o’ th’ cliff, what thing was that
Which parted from you?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: A poor unfortunate beggar.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
As I stood here below, methought his eyes
Were two full moons; he had a thousand noses,
Horns whelked and waved like the enragèd sea.
It was some fiend. Therefore, thou happy father,
Think that the clearest gods, who make them honors
Of men’s impossibilities, have preserved thee.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
I do remember now. Henceforth I’ll bear
Affliction till it do cry out itself
“Enough, enough!” and die. That thing you speak of,
I took it for a man. Often ’twould say
“The fiend, the fiend!” He led me to that place.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Bear free and patient thoughts.
But who comes here?
The safer sense will ne’er accommodate
His master thus.

speaker: LEAR
text:
No, they cannot touch me for coining. I am the
King himself.

speaker: EDGAR
text: O, thou side-piercing sight!

speaker: LEAR
text:
Nature’s above art in that respect. There’s your
press-money. That fellow handles his bow like a
crowkeeper. Draw me a clothier’s yard. Look, look,
a mouse! Peace, peace! This piece of toasted cheese
will do ’t. There’s my gauntlet; I’ll prove it on a
giant. Bring up the brown bills. O, well flown, bird!
I’ th’ clout, i’ th’ clout! Hewgh! Give the word.

speaker: EDGAR
text: Sweet marjoram.

speaker: LEAR
text: Pass.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: I know that voice.

speaker: LEAR
text:
Ha! Goneril with a white beard? They flattered
me like a dog and told me I had the white hairs in
my beard ere the black ones were there. To say “ay”
and “no” to everything that I said “ay” and “no” to
was no good divinity. When the rain came to wet me
once and the wind to make me chatter, when the
thunder would not peace at my bidding, there I
found ’em, there I smelt ’em out. Go to. They are
not men o’ their words; they told me I was everything.
’Tis a lie. I am not ague-proof.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
The trick of that voice I do well remember.
Is ’t not the King?

speaker: LEAR
text:
Ay, every inch a king.
When I do stare, see how the subject quakes.
I pardon that man’s life. What was thy cause?
Adultery? Thou shalt not die. Die for adultery? No.
The wren goes to ’t, and the small gilded fly does
lecher in my sight. Let copulation thrive, for
Gloucester’s bastard son was kinder to his father
than my daughters got ’tween the lawful sheets. To
’t, luxury, pell-mell, for I lack soldiers. Behold yond
simp’ring dame, whose face between her forks
presages snow, that minces virtue and does shake
the head to hear of pleasure’s name. The fitchew
nor the soiled horse goes to ’t with a more riotous
appetite. Down from the waist they are centaurs,
though women all above. But to the girdle do the
gods inherit; beneath is all the fiend’s. There’s hell,
there’s darkness, there is the sulphurous pit; burning,
scalding, stench, consumption! Fie, fie, fie, pah,
pah! Give me an ounce of civet, good apothecary;
sweeten my imagination. There’s money for thee.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: O, let me kiss that hand!

speaker: LEAR
text: Let me wipe it first; it smells of mortality.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
O ruined piece of nature! This great world
Shall so wear out to naught. Dost thou know me?

speaker: LEAR
text:
I remember thine eyes well enough. Dost thou
squinny at me? No, do thy worst, blind Cupid, I’ll
not love. Read thou this challenge. Mark but the
penning of it.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Were all thy letters suns, I could not see.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
I would not take this from report. It is,
And my heart breaks at it.

speaker: LEAR
text: Read.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: What, with the case of eyes?

speaker: LEAR
text:
O ho, are you there with me? No eyes in your
head, nor no money in your purse? Your eyes are in
a heavy case, your purse in a light, yet you see how
this world goes.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: I see it feelingly.

speaker: LEAR
text:
What, art mad? A man may see how this world
goes with no eyes. Look with thine ears. See how
yond justice rails upon yond simple thief. Hark in
thine ear. Change places and, handy-dandy, which
is the justice, which is the thief? Thou hast seen a
farmer’s dog bark at a beggar?

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Ay, sir.

speaker: LEAR
text:
And the creature run from the cur? There thou
might’st behold the great image of authority: a
dog’s obeyed in office.
Thou rascal beadle, hold thy bloody hand!
Why dost thou lash that whore? Strip thy own back.
Thou hotly lusts to use her in that kind
For which thou whipp’st her. The usurer hangs the cozener.
Through tattered clothes small vices do appear.
Robes and furred gowns hide all. Plate sin with gold,
And the strong lance of justice hurtless breaks.
Arm it in rags, a pygmy’s straw does pierce it.
None does offend, none, I say, none; I’ll able ’em.
Take that of me, my friend, who have the power
To seal th’ accuser’s lips. Get thee glass eyes,
And like a scurvy politician
Seem to see the things thou dost not. Now, now, now, now.
Pull off my boots. Harder, harder. So.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
O, matter and impertinency mixed,
Reason in madness!

speaker: LEAR
text:
If thou wilt weep my fortunes, take my eyes.
I know thee well enough; thy name is Gloucester.
Thou must be patient. We came crying hither;
Thou know’st the first time that we smell the air
We wawl and cry. I will preach to thee. Mark.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Alack, alack the day!

speaker: LEAR
text:
When we are born, we cry that we are come
To this great stage of fools.—This’ a good block.
It were a delicate stratagem to shoe
A troop of horse with felt. I’ll put ’t in proof,
And when I have stol’n upon these son-in-laws,
Then kill, kill, kill, kill, kill, kill!

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text:
O, here he is. Lay hand upon him.—Sir,
Your most dear daughter—

speaker: LEAR
text:
No rescue? What, a prisoner? I am even
The natural fool of Fortune. Use me well.
You shall have ransom. Let me have surgeons;
I am cut to th’ brains.

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text: You shall have anything.

speaker: LEAR
text:
No seconds? All myself?
Why, this would make a man a man of salt,
To use his eyes for garden waterpots,
Ay, and laying autumn’s dust.
I will die bravely like a smug bridegroom. What?
I will be jovial. Come, come, I am a king,
Masters, know you that?

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text: You are a royal one, and we obey you.

speaker: LEAR
text:
Then there’s life in ’t. Come, an you get it, you
shall get it by running. Sa, sa, sa, sa.

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text:
A sight most pitiful in the meanest wretch,
Past speaking of in a king. Thou hast a daughter
Who redeems nature from the general curse
Which twain have brought her to.

speaker: EDGAR
text: Hail, gentle sir.

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text: Sir, speed you. What’s your will?

speaker: EDGAR
text: Do you hear aught, sir, of a battle toward?

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text:
Most sure and vulgar. Everyone hears that,
Which can distinguish sound.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
But, by your favor,
How near’s the other army?

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text:
Near and on speedy foot. The main descry
Stands on the hourly thought.

speaker: EDGAR
text: I thank you, sir. That’s all.

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text:
Though that the Queen on special cause is here,
Her army is moved on.

speaker: EDGAR
text: I thank you, sir.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
EDGAR
text: Well pray you, father.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Now, good sir, what are you?

speaker: EDGAR
text:
A most poor man, made tame to Fortune’s blows,
Who, by the art of known and feeling sorrows,
Am pregnant to good pity. Give me your hand;
I’ll lead you to some biding.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
Hearty thanks.
The bounty and the benison of heaven
To boot, and boot.

speaker: OSWALD
text:
A proclaimed prize! Most happy!
That eyeless head of thine was first framed flesh
To raise my fortunes. Thou old unhappy traitor,
Briefly thyself remember; the sword is out
That must destroy thee.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
Now let thy friendly hand
Put strength enough to ’t.

speaker: OSWALD
text:
Wherefore, bold peasant,
Dar’st thou support a published traitor? Hence,
Lest that th’ infection of his fortune take
Like hold on thee. Let go his arm.

speaker: EDGAR
text: Chill not let go, zir, without vurther ’casion.

speaker: OSWALD
text: Let go, slave, or thou diest!

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Good gentleman, go your gait, and let poor
volk pass. An ’chud ha’ bin zwaggered out of my
life, ’twould not ha’ bin zo long as ’tis by a vortnight.
Nay, come not near th’ old man. Keep out,
che vor’ ye, or Ise try whether your costard or my
ballow be the harder. Chill be plain with you.

speaker: OSWALD
text: Out, dunghill.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Chill pick your teeth, zir. Come, no matter vor
your foins.

speaker: OSWALD
text:
Slave, thou hast slain me. Villain, take my purse.
If ever thou wilt thrive, bury my body,
And give the letters which thou find’st about me
To Edmund, Earl of Gloucester. Seek him out
Upon the English party. O, untimely death! Death!

speaker: EDGAR
text:
I know thee well, a serviceable villain,
As duteous to the vices of thy mistress
As badness would desire.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: What, is he dead?

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Sit you down, father; rest you.
Let’s see these pockets. The letters that he speaks of
May be my friends. He’s dead; I am only sorry
He had no other deathsman. Let us see.
Leave, gentle wax, and, manners, blame us not.
To know our enemies’ minds, we rip their hearts.
Their papers is more lawful.
O indistinguished space of woman’s will!
A plot upon her virtuous husband’s life,
And the exchange my brother.—Here, in the sands
Thee I’ll rake up, the post unsanctified
Of murderous lechers; and in the mature time
With this ungracious paper strike the sight
Of the death-practiced duke. For him ’tis well
That of thy death and business I can tell.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text:
The King is mad. How stiff is my vile sense
That I stand up and have ingenious feeling
Of my huge sorrows! Better I were distract.
So should my thoughts be severed from my griefs,
And woes, by wrong imaginations, lose
The knowledge of themselves.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Give me your hand.
Far off methinks I hear the beaten drum.
Come, father, I’ll bestow you with a friend.

speaker: CORDELIA
text:
O, thou good Kent, how shall I live and work
To match thy goodness? My life will be too short,
And every measure fail me.

speaker: KENT
text:
To be acknowledged, madam, is o’erpaid.
All my reports go with the modest truth,
Nor more, nor clipped, but so.

speaker: CORDELIA
text:
Be better suited.
These weeds are memories of those worser hours.
I prithee put them off.

speaker: KENT
text:
Pardon, dear madam.
Yet to be known shortens my made intent.
My boon I make it that you know me not
Till time and I think meet.

speaker: CORDELIA
text: Then be ’t so, my good lord.—How does the King?

speaker: DOCTOR
text: Madam, sleeps still.

speaker: CORDELIA
text:
O, you kind gods,
Cure this great breach in his abusèd nature!
Th’ untuned and jarring senses, O, wind up,
Of this child-changèd father!

speaker: DOCTOR
text:
So please your Majesty
That we may wake the King? He hath slept long.

speaker: CORDELIA
text:
Be governed by your knowledge, and proceed
I’ th’ sway of your own will. Is he arrayed?

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text:
Ay, madam. In the heaviness of sleep,
We put fresh garments on him.

speaker: DOCTOR
text:
Be by, good madam, when we do awake him.
I doubt not of his temperance.

speaker: CORDELIA
text: Very well.

speaker: DOCTOR
text: Please you, draw near.—Louder the music there.

speaker: CORDELIA
text:
O, my dear father, restoration hang
Thy medicine on my lips, and let this kiss
Repair those violent harms that my two sisters
Have in thy reverence made.

speaker: KENT
text: Kind and dear princess.

speaker: CORDELIA
text:
Had you not been their father, these white flakes
Did challenge pity of them. Was this a face
To be opposed against the jarring winds?
To stand against the deep dread-bolted thunder,
In the most terrible and nimble stroke
Of quick cross-lightning? To watch, poor perdu,
With this thin helm? Mine enemy’s dog,
Though he had bit me, should have stood that night
Against my fire. And wast thou fain, poor father,
To hovel thee with swine and rogues forlorn
In short and musty straw? Alack, alack,
’Tis wonder that thy life and wits at once
Had not concluded all.—He wakes. Speak to him.

speaker: DOCTOR
text: Madam, do you; ’tis fittest.

speaker: CORDELIA
text: How does my royal lord? How fares your Majesty?

speaker: LEAR
text:
You do me wrong to take me out o’ th’ grave.
Thou art a soul in bliss, but I am bound
Upon a wheel of fire, that mine own tears
Do scald like molten lead.

speaker: CORDELIA
text: Sir, do you know me?

speaker: LEAR
text: You are a spirit, I know. Where did you die?

speaker: CORDELIA
text: Still, still, far wide.

speaker: DOCTOR
text: He’s scarce awake. Let him alone awhile.

speaker: LEAR
text:
Where have I been? Where am I? Fair daylight?
I am mightily abused; I should e’en die with pity
To see another thus. I know not what to say.
I will not swear these are my hands. Let’s see.
I feel this pinprick. Would I were assured
Of my condition!

speaker: CORDELIA
text:
O, look upon me, sir,
And hold your hand in benediction o’er me.
No, sir, you must not kneel.

speaker: LEAR
text:
Pray do not mock:
I am a very foolish fond old man,
Fourscore and upward, not an hour more nor less,
And to deal plainly,
I fear I am not in my perfect mind.
Methinks I should know you and know this man,
Yet I am doubtful, for I am mainly ignorant
What place this is, and all the skill I have
Remembers not these garments; nor I know not
Where I did lodge last night. Do not laugh at me,
For, as I am a man, I think this lady
To be my child Cordelia.

speaker: CORDELIA
text: And so I am; I am.

speaker: LEAR
text:
Be your tears wet? Yes, faith. I pray, weep not.
If you have poison for me, I will drink it.
I know you do not love me, for your sisters
Have, as I do remember, done me wrong.
You have some cause; they have not.

speaker: CORDELIA
text: No cause, no cause.

speaker: LEAR
text: Am I in France?

speaker: KENT
text: In your own kingdom, sir.

speaker: LEAR
text: Do not abuse me.

speaker: DOCTOR
text:
Be comforted, good madam. The great rage,
You see, is killed in him, and yet it is danger
To make him even o’er the time he has lost.
Desire him to go in. Trouble him no more
Till further settling.

speaker: CORDELIA
text: Will ’t please your Highness walk?

speaker: LEAR
text:
You must bear with me.
Pray you now, forget, and forgive. I am old and foolish.

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text:
Holds it true, sir, that the Duke of Cornwall
was so slain?

speaker: KENT
text: Most certain, sir.

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text: Who is conductor of his people?

speaker: KENT
text: As ’tis said, the bastard son of Gloucester.

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text:
They say Edgar, his banished son, is with
the Earl of Kent in Germany.

speaker: KENT
text:
Report is changeable. ’Tis time to look about.
The powers of the kingdom approach apace.

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text:
The arbitrament is like to be bloody. Fare
you well, sir.

speaker: KENT
text:
My point and period will be throughly wrought,
Or well, or ill, as this day’s battle’s fought.

speaker: EDMUND
text:
Know of the Duke if his last purpose hold,
Or whether since he is advised by aught
To change the course. He’s full of alteration
And self-reproving. Bring his constant pleasure.

speaker: REGAN
text: Our sister’s man is certainly miscarried.

speaker: EDMUND
text: ’Tis to be doubted, madam.

speaker: REGAN
text:
Now, sweet lord,
You know the goodness I intend upon you;
Tell me but truly, but then speak the truth,
Do you not love my sister?

speaker: EDMUND
text: In honored love.

speaker: REGAN
text:
But have you never found my brother’s way
To the forfended place?

speaker: EDMUND
text: That thought abuses you.

speaker: REGAN
text:
I am doubtful that you have been conjunct
And bosomed with her as far as we call hers.

speaker: EDMUND
text: No, by mine honor, madam.

speaker: REGAN
text:
I never shall endure her. Dear my lord,
Be not familiar with her.

speaker: EDMUND
text: Fear me not. She and the Duke, her husband.

speaker: GONERIL
text:
I had rather lose the battle than that sister
Should loosen him and me.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Our very loving sister, well bemet.—
Sir, this I heard: the King is come to his daughter,
With others whom the rigor of our state
Forced to cry out. Where I could not be honest,
I never yet was valiant. For this business,
It touches us as France invades our land,
Not bolds the King, with others whom, I fear,
Most just and heavy causes make oppose.

speaker: EDMUND
text: Sir, you speak nobly.

speaker: REGAN
text: Why is this reasoned?

speaker: GONERIL
text:
Combine together ’gainst the enemy,
For these domestic and particular broils
Are not the question here.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Let’s then determine
With th’ ancient of war on our proceeding.

speaker: EDMUND
text: I shall attend you presently at your tent.

speaker: REGAN
text: Sister, you’ll go with us?

speaker: GONERIL
text: No.

speaker: REGAN
text: ’Tis most convenient. Pray, go with us.

speaker: GONERIL
text: Oho, I know the riddle.—I will go.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
If e’er your Grace had speech with man so poor,
Hear me one word.

speaker: ALBANY
text: I’ll overtake you.—Speak.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Before you fight the battle, ope this letter.
If you have victory, let the trumpet sound
For him that brought it. Wretched though I seem,
I can produce a champion that will prove
What is avouchèd there. If you miscarry,
Your business of the world hath so an end,
And machination ceases. Fortune love you.

speaker: ALBANY
text: Stay till I have read the letter.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
I was forbid it.
When time shall serve, let but the herald cry
And I’ll appear again.

speaker: ALBANY
text: Why, fare thee well. I will o’erlook thy paper.

speaker: EDMUND
text:
The enemy’s in view. Draw up your powers.
Here is the guess of their true strength and forces
By diligent discovery. But your haste
Is now urged on you.

speaker: ALBANY
text: We will greet the time.

speaker: EDMUND
text:
To both these sisters have I sworn my love,
Each jealous of the other as the stung
Are of the adder. Which of them shall I take?
Both? One? Or neither? Neither can be enjoyed
If both remain alive. To take the widow
Exasperates, makes mad her sister Goneril,
And hardly shall I carry out my side,
Her husband being alive. Now, then, we’ll use
His countenance for the battle, which, being done,
Let her who would be rid of him devise
His speedy taking off. As for the mercy
Which he intends to Lear and to Cordelia,
The battle done and they within our power,
Shall never see his pardon, for my state
Stands on me to defend, not to debate.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Here, father, take the shadow of this tree
For your good host. Pray that the right may thrive.
If ever I return to you again,
I’ll bring you comfort.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: Grace go with you, sir.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Away, old man. Give me thy hand. Away.
King Lear hath lost, he and his daughter ta’en.
Give me thy hand. Come on.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: No further, sir. A man may rot even here.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
What, in ill thoughts again? Men must endure
Their going hence even as their coming hither.
Ripeness is all. Come on.

speaker: GLOUCESTER
text: And that’s true too.

speaker: EDMUND
text:
Some officers take them away. Good guard
Until their greater pleasures first be known
That are to censure them.

speaker: CORDELIA
text:
We are not the first
Who with best meaning have incurred the worst.
For thee, oppressèd king, I am cast down.
Myself could else outfrown false Fortune’s frown.
Shall we not see these daughters and these sisters?

speaker: LEAR
text:
No, no, no, no. Come, let’s away to prison.
We two alone will sing like birds i’ th’ cage.
When thou dost ask me blessing, I’ll kneel down
And ask of thee forgiveness. So we’ll live,
And pray, and sing, and tell old tales, and laugh
At gilded butterflies, and hear poor rogues
Talk of court news, and we’ll talk with them too—
Who loses and who wins; who’s in, who’s out—
And take upon ’s the mystery of things,
As if we were God’s spies. And we’ll wear out,
In a walled prison, packs and sects of great ones
That ebb and flow by th’ moon.

speaker: EDMUND
text: Take them away.

speaker: LEAR
text:
Upon such sacrifices, my Cordelia,
The gods themselves throw incense. Have I caught thee?
He that parts us shall bring a brand from heaven
And fire us hence like foxes. Wipe thine eyes.
The good years shall devour them, flesh and fell,
Ere they shall make us weep. We’ll see ’em starved first.
Come.

speaker: EDMUND
text:
Come hither, captain. Hark.
Take thou this note. Go follow them to prison.
One step I have advanced thee. If thou dost
As this instructs thee, thou dost make thy way
To noble fortunes. Know thou this: that men
Are as the time is; to be tender-minded
Does not become a sword. Thy great employment
Will not bear question. Either say thou ’lt do ’t,
Or thrive by other means.

speaker: CAPTAIN
text: I’ll do ’t, my lord.

speaker: EDMUND
text:
About it, and write “happy” when th’ hast done.
Mark, I say, instantly, and carry it so
As I have set it down.

speaker: CAPTAIN
text:
I cannot draw a cart, nor eat dried oats.
If it be man’s work, I’ll do ’t.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Sir, you have showed today your valiant strain,
And Fortune led you well. You have the captives
Who were the opposites of this day’s strife.
I do require them of you, so to use them
As we shall find their merits and our safety
May equally determine.

speaker: EDMUND
text:
Sir, I thought it fit
To send the old and miserable king
To some retention and appointed guard,
Whose age had charms in it, whose title more,
To pluck the common bosom on his side
And turn our impressed lances in our eyes,
Which do command them. With him I sent the Queen,
My reason all the same, and they are ready
Tomorrow, or at further space, t’ appear
Where you shall hold your session. At this time
We sweat and bleed. The friend hath lost his friend,
And the best quarrels in the heat are cursed
By those that feel their sharpness.
The question of Cordelia and her father
Requires a fitter place.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Sir, by your patience,
I hold you but a subject of this war,
Not as a brother.

speaker: REGAN
text:
That’s as we list to grace him.
Methinks our pleasure might have been demanded
Ere you had spoke so far. He led our powers,
Bore the commission of my place and person,
The which immediacy may well stand up
And call itself your brother.

speaker: GONERIL
text:
Not so hot.
In his own grace he doth exalt himself
More than in your addition.

speaker: REGAN
text:
In my rights,
By me invested, he compeers the best.

speaker: GONERIL
text: That were the most if he should husband you.

speaker: REGAN
text: Jesters do oft prove prophets.

speaker: GONERIL
text:
Holla, holla!
That eye that told you so looked but asquint.

speaker: REGAN
text:
Lady, I am not well, else I should answer
From a full-flowing stomach.
General,
Take thou my soldiers, prisoners, patrimony.
Dispose of them, of me; the walls is thine.
Witness the world that I create thee here
My lord and master.

speaker: GONERIL
text: Mean you to enjoy him?

speaker: ALBANY
text: The let-alone lies not in your goodwill.

speaker: EDMUND
text: Nor in thine, lord.

speaker: ALBANY
text: Half-blooded fellow, yes.

speaker: REGAN
text: Let the drum strike, and prove my title thine.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Stay yet, hear reason.—Edmund, I arrest thee
On capital treason; and, in thine attaint,
This gilded serpent.—For your claim, fair sister,
I bar it in the interest of my wife.
’Tis she is subcontracted to this lord,
And I, her husband, contradict your banns.
If you will marry, make your loves to me.
My lady is bespoke.

speaker: GONERIL
text: An interlude!

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Thou art armed, Gloucester. Let the trumpet sound.
If none appear to prove upon thy person
Thy heinous, manifest, and many treasons,
There is my pledge.
I’ll make it on thy heart,
Ere I taste bread, thou art in nothing less
Than I have here proclaimed thee.

speaker: REGAN
text: Sick, O, sick!

speaker: GONERIL
text: If not, I’ll ne’er trust medicine.

speaker: EDMUND
text:
There’s my exchange.
What in the world he is
That names me traitor, villain-like he lies.
Call by the trumpet. He that dares approach,
On him, on you, who not, I will maintain
My truth and honor firmly.

speaker: ALBANY
text: A herald, ho!

speaker: EDMUND
text: A herald, ho, a herald!

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Trust to thy single virtue, for thy soldiers,
All levied in my name, have in my name
Took their discharge.

speaker: REGAN
text: My sickness grows upon me.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
She is not well. Convey her to my tent.
Come hither, herald. Let the trumpet sound,
And read out this.

speaker: CAPTAIN
text: Sound, trumpet!

speaker: HERALD
text: If any man of quality or degree , within the lists of the army , will maintain upon Edmund , supposed Earl of Gloucester , that he is a manifold traitor , let him appear by the third sound of the trumpet . He is bold in his defense .

speaker: HERALD
text: Again!

speaker: HERALD
text: Again!

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Ask him his purposes, why he appears
Upon this call o’ th’ trumpet.

speaker: HERALD
text:
What are you?
Your name, your quality, and why you answer
This present summons?

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Know my name is lost,
By treason’s tooth bare-gnawn and canker-bit.
Yet am I noble as the adversary
I come to cope.

speaker: ALBANY
text: Which is that adversary?

speaker: EDGAR
text: What’s he that speaks for Edmund, Earl of Gloucester?

speaker: EDMUND
text: Himself. What sayest thou to him?

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Draw thy sword,
That if my speech offend a noble heart,
Thy arm may do thee justice. Here is mine.
Behold, it is my privilege, the privilege of mine honors,
My oath, and my profession. I protest,
Maugre thy strength, place, youth, and eminence,
Despite thy victor-sword and fire-new fortune,
Thy valor, and thy heart, thou art a traitor,
False to thy gods, thy brother, and thy father,
Conspirant ’gainst this high illustrious prince,
And from th’ extremest upward of thy head
To the descent and dust below thy foot,
A most toad-spotted traitor. Say thou “no,”
This sword, this arm, and my best spirits are bent
To prove upon thy heart, whereto I speak,
Thou liest.

speaker: EDMUND
text:
In wisdom I should ask thy name,
But since thy outside looks so fair and warlike,
And that thy tongue some say of breeding breathes,
What safe and nicely I might well delay
By rule of knighthood, I disdain and spurn.
Back do I toss these treasons to thy head,
With the hell-hated lie o’erwhelm thy heart,
Which, for they yet glance by and scarcely bruise,
This sword of mine shall give them instant way,
Where they shall rest forever. Trumpets, speak!

speaker: ALBANY
text: Save him, save him!

speaker: GONERIL
text:
This is practice, Gloucester.
By th’ law of war, thou wast not bound to answer
An unknown opposite. Thou art not vanquished,
But cozened and beguiled.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Shut your mouth, dame,
Or with this paper shall I stopple it.—Hold, sir.—
Thou worse than any name, read thine own evil.
No tearing, lady. I perceive you know it.

speaker: GONERIL
text:
Say if I do; the laws are mine, not thine.
Who can arraign me for ’t?

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Most monstrous! O!
Know’st thou this paper?

speaker: GONERIL
text: Ask me not what I know.

speaker: ALBANY
text: Go after her, she’s desperate. Govern her.

speaker: EDMUND
text:
What you have charged me with, that have I done,
And more, much more. The time will bring it out.
’Tis past, and so am I. But what art thou
That hast this fortune on me? If thou ’rt noble,
I do forgive thee.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Let’s exchange charity.
I am no less in blood than thou art, Edmund;
If more, the more th’ hast wronged me.
My name is Edgar and thy father’s son.
The gods are just, and of our pleasant vices
Make instruments to plague us.
The dark and vicious place where thee he got
Cost him his eyes.

speaker: EDMUND
text:
Th’ hast spoken right. ’Tis true.
The wheel is come full circle; I am here.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Methought thy very gait did prophesy
A royal nobleness. I must embrace thee.
Let sorrow split my heart if ever I
Did hate thee or thy father!

speaker: EDGAR
text: Worthy prince, I know ’t.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Where have you hid yourself?
How have you known the miseries of your father?

speaker: EDGAR
text:
By nursing them, my lord. List a brief tale,
And when ’tis told, O, that my heart would burst!
The bloody proclamation to escape
That followed me so near—O, our lives’ sweetness,
That we the pain of death would hourly die
Rather than die at once!—taught me to shift
Into a madman’s rags, t’ assume a semblance
That very dogs disdained, and in this habit
Met I my father with his bleeding rings,
Their precious stones new lost; became his guide,
Led him, begged for him, saved him from despair.
Never—O fault!—revealed myself unto him
Until some half hour past, when I was armed.
Not sure, though hoping of this good success,
I asked his blessing, and from first to last
Told him our pilgrimage. But his flawed heart
(Alack, too weak the conflict to support)
’Twixt two extremes of passion, joy and grief,
Burst smilingly.

speaker: EDMUND
text:
This speech of yours hath moved me,
And shall perchance do good. But speak you on.
You look as you had something more to say.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
If there be more, more woeful, hold it in,
For I am almost ready to dissolve,
Hearing of this.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
This would have seemed a period
To such as love not sorrow; but another,
To amplify too much, would make much more
And top extremity. Whilst I
Was big in clamor, came there in a man
Who, having seen me in my worst estate,
Shunned my abhorred society; but then, finding
Who ’twas that so endured, with his strong arms
He fastened on my neck and bellowed out
As he’d burst heaven, threw him on my father,
Told the most piteous tale of Lear and him
That ever ear received, which, in recounting,
His grief grew puissant, and the strings of life
Began to crack. Twice then the trumpets sounded,
And there I left him tranced.

speaker: ALBANY
text: But who was this?

speaker: EDGAR
text:
Kent, sir, the banished Kent, who in disguise
Followed his enemy king and did him service
Improper for a slave.

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text: Help, help, O, help!

speaker: EDGAR
text: What kind of help?

speaker: ALBANY
text: Speak, man!

speaker: EDGAR
text: What means this bloody knife?

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text:
’Tis hot, it smokes! It came even from the heart
Of—O, she’s dead!

speaker: ALBANY
text: Who dead? Speak, man.

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text:
Your lady, sir, your lady. And her sister
By her is poisoned. She confesses it.

speaker: EDMUND
text:
I was contracted to them both. All three
Now marry in an instant.

speaker: EDGAR
text: Here comes Kent.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Produce the bodies, be they alive or dead.
This judgment of the heavens, that makes us tremble,
Touches us not with pity. O, is this he?
The time will not allow the compliment
Which very manners urges.

speaker: KENT
text:
I am come
To bid my king and master aye goodnight.
Is he not here?

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Great thing of us forgot!
Speak, Edmund, where’s the King? And where’s Cordelia?
Seest thou this object, Kent?

speaker: KENT
text: Alack, why thus?

speaker: EDMUND
text:
Yet Edmund was beloved.
The one the other poisoned for my sake,
And after slew herself.

speaker: ALBANY
text: Even so.—Cover their faces.

speaker: EDMUND
text:
I pant for life. Some good I mean to do
Despite of mine own nature. Quickly send—
Be brief in it—to th’ castle, for my writ
Is on the life of Lear, and on Cordelia.
Nay, send in time.

speaker: ALBANY
text: Run, run, O, run!

speaker: EDGAR
text:
To who, my lord? Who has the office? Send
Thy token of reprieve.

speaker: EDMUND
text: Well thought on. Take my sword. Give it the Captain.

speaker: EDGAR
text: Haste thee for thy life.

speaker: EDMUND
text:
He hath commission from thy wife and me
To hang Cordelia in the prison, and
To lay the blame upon her own despair,
That she fordid herself.

speaker: ALBANY
text: The gods defend her!—Bear him hence awhile.

speaker: LEAR
text:
Howl, howl, howl! O, you are men of stones!
Had I your tongues and eyes, I’d use them so
That heaven’s vault should crack. She’s gone forever.
I know when one is dead and when one lives.
She’s dead as earth.—Lend me a looking glass.
If that her breath will mist or stain the stone,
Why, then she lives.

speaker: KENT
text: Is this the promised end?

speaker: EDGAR
text: Or image of that horror?

speaker: ALBANY
text: Fall and cease.

speaker: LEAR
text:
This feather stirs. She lives. If it be so,
It is a chance which does redeem all sorrows
That ever I have felt.

speaker: KENT
text: O, my good master—

speaker: LEAR
text: Prithee, away.

speaker: EDGAR
text: ’Tis noble Kent, your friend.

speaker: LEAR
text:
A plague upon you, murderers, traitors all!
I might have saved her. Now she’s gone forever.—
Cordelia, Cordelia, stay a little. Ha!
What is ’t thou sayst?—Her voice was ever soft,
Gentle, and low, an excellent thing in woman.
I killed the slave that was a-hanging thee.

speaker: GENTLEMAN
text: ’Tis true, my lords, he did.

speaker: LEAR
text:
Did I not, fellow?
I have seen the day, with my good biting falchion
I would have made him skip. I am old now,
And these same crosses spoil me. Who are you?
Mine eyes are not o’ th’ best. I’ll tell you straight.

speaker: KENT
text:
If Fortune brag of two she loved and hated,
One of them we behold.

speaker: LEAR
text: This is a dull sight. Are you not Kent?

speaker: KENT
text:
The same,
Your servant Kent. Where is your servant Caius?

speaker: LEAR
text:
He’s a good fellow, I can tell you that.
He’ll strike and quickly too. He’s dead and rotten.

speaker: KENT
text: No, my good lord, I am the very man—

speaker: LEAR
text: I’ll see that straight.

speaker: KENT
text:
That from your first of difference and decay
Have followed your sad steps.

speaker: LEAR
text: You are welcome hither.

speaker: KENT
text:
Nor no man else. All’s cheerless, dark, and deadly.
Your eldest daughters have fordone themselves,
And desperately are dead.

speaker: LEAR
text: Ay, so I think.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
He knows not what he says, and vain is it
That we present us to him.

speaker: EDGAR
text: Very bootless.

speaker: MESSENGER
text: Edmund is dead, my lord.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
That’s but a trifle here.—
You lords and noble friends, know our intent:
What comfort to this great decay may come
Shall be applied. For us, we will resign,
During the life of this old Majesty,
To him our absolute power; you to your rights,
With boot and such addition as your Honors
Have more than merited. All friends shall taste
The wages of their virtue, and all foes
The cup of their deservings. O, see, see!

speaker: LEAR
text:
And my poor fool is hanged. No, no, no life?
Why should a dog, a horse, a rat have life,
And thou no breath at all? Thou ’lt come no more,
Never, never, never, never, never.—
Pray you undo this button. Thank you, sir.
Do you see this? Look on her, look, her lips,
Look there, look there!

speaker: EDGAR
text: He faints. My lord, my lord!

speaker: KENT
text: Break, heart, I prithee, break!

speaker: EDGAR
text: Look up, my lord.

speaker: KENT
text:
Vex not his ghost. O, let him pass! He hates him
That would upon the rack of this tough world
Stretch him out longer.

speaker: EDGAR
text: He is gone indeed.

speaker: KENT
text:
The wonder is he hath endured so long.
He but usurped his life.

speaker: ALBANY
text:
Bear them from hence. Our present business
Is general woe. Friends of my soul, you twain
Rule in this realm, and the gored state sustain.

speaker: KENT
text:
I have a journey, sir, shortly to go;
My master calls me. I must not say no.

speaker: EDGAR
text:
The weight of this sad time we must obey,
Speak what we feel, not what we ought to say.
The oldest hath borne most; we that are young
Shall never see so much nor live so long.

speaker: KING
text:
Let fame, that all hunt after in their lives,
Live registered upon our brazen tombs,
And then grace us in the disgrace of death,
When, spite of cormorant devouring time,
Th’ endeavor of this present breath may buy
That honor which shall bate his scythe’s keen edge
And make us heirs of all eternity.
Therefore, brave conquerors, for so you are
That war against your own affections
And the huge army of the world’s desires,
Our late edict shall strongly stand in force.
Navarre shall be the wonder of the world;
Our court shall be a little academe,
Still and contemplative in living art.
You three, Berowne, Dumaine, and Longaville,
Have sworn for three years’ term to live with me,
My fellow scholars, and to keep those statutes
That are recorded in this schedule here.
Your oaths are passed, and now subscribe your names,
That his own hand may strike his honor down
That violates the smallest branch herein.
If you are armed to do as sworn to do,
Subscribe to your deep oaths, and keep it too.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text:
I am resolved. ’Tis but a three years’ fast.
The mind shall banquet though the body pine.
Fat paunches have lean pates, and dainty bits
Make rich the ribs but bankrout quite the wits.

speaker: DUMAINE
text:
My loving lord, Dumaine is mortified.
The grosser manner of these world’s delights
He throws upon the gross world’s baser slaves.
To love, to wealth, to pomp I pine and die,
With all these living in philosophy.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
I can but say their protestation over.
So much, dear liege, I have already sworn,
That is, to live and study here three years.
But there are other strict observances:
As not to see a woman in that term,
Which I hope well is not enrollèd there;
And one day in a week to touch no food,
And but one meal on every day besides,
The which I hope is not enrollèd there;
And then to sleep but three hours in the night,
And not be seen to wink of all the day—
When I was wont to think no harm all night,
And make a dark night too of half the day—
Which I hope well is not enrollèd there.
O, these are barren tasks, too hard to keep,
Not to see ladies, study, fast, not sleep.

speaker: KING
text: Your oath is passed to pass away from these.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Let me say no, my liege, an if you please.
I only swore to study with your Grace
And stay here in your court for three years’ space.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: You swore to that, Berowne, and to the rest.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
By yea and nay, sir. Then I swore in jest.
What is the end of study, let me know?

speaker: KING
text: Why, that to know which else we should not know.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Things hid and barred, you mean, from common sense.

speaker: KING
text: Ay, that is study’s godlike recompense.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Come on, then, I will swear to study so,
To know the thing I am forbid to know:
As thus—to study where I well may dine,
When I to feast expressly am forbid;
Or study where to meet some mistress fine
When mistresses from common sense are hid;
Or having sworn too hard-a-keeping oath,
Study to break it, and not break my troth.
If study’s gain be thus, and this be so,
Study knows that which yet it doth not know.
Swear me to this, and I will ne’er say no.

speaker: KING
text:
These be the stops that hinder study quite,
And train our intellects to vain delight.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Why, all delights are vain, and that most vain
Which with pain purchased doth inherit pain:
As painfully to pore upon a book
To seek the light of truth, while truth the while
Doth falsely blind the eyesight of his look.
Light seeking light doth light of light beguile.
So, ere you find where light in darkness lies,
Your light grows dark by losing of your eyes.
Study me how to please the eye indeed
By fixing it upon a fairer eye,
Who dazzling so, that eye shall be his heed
And give him light that it was blinded by.
Study is like the heaven’s glorious sun,
That will not be deep-searched with saucy looks.
Small have continual plodders ever won,
Save base authority from others’ books.
These earthly godfathers of heaven’s lights,
That give a name to every fixèd star,
Have no more profit of their shining nights
Than those that walk and wot not what they are.
Too much to know is to know naught but fame,
And every godfather can give a name.

speaker: KING
text: How well he’s read to reason against reading.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: Proceeded well, to stop all good proceeding.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: He weeds the corn, and still lets grow the weeding.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: The spring is near when green geese are a-breeding.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: How follows that?

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Fit in his place and time.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: In reason nothing.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Something then in rhyme.

speaker: KING
text:
Berowne is like an envious sneaping frost
That bites the firstborn infants of the spring.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Well, say I am. Why should proud summer boast
Before the birds have any cause to sing?
Why should I joy in any abortive birth?
At Christmas I no more desire a rose
Than wish a snow in May’s new-fangled shows,
But like of each thing that in season grows.
So you, to study now it is too late,
Climb o’er the house to unlock the little gate.

speaker: KING
text: Well, sit you out. Go home, Berowne. Adieu.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
No, my good lord, I have sworn to stay with you.
And though I have for barbarism spoke more
Than for that angel knowledge you can say,
Yet, confident, I’ll keep what I have sworn
And bide the penance of each three years’ day.
Give me the paper. Let me read the same,
And to the strictest decrees I’ll write my name.

speaker: KING
text: How well this yielding rescues thee from shame.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Item , That no woman shall come within a mile of my court . Hath this been proclaimed?

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: Four days ago.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Let’s see the penalty. On pain of losing her tongue . Who devised this penalty?

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: Marry, that did I.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Sweet lord, and why?

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: To fright them hence with that dread penalty.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
A dangerous law against gentility.
Item , If any man be seen to talk with a woman within the term of three years , he shall endure such public shame as the rest of the court can possible devise .
This article, my liege, yourself must break,
For well you know here comes in embassy
The French king’s daughter with yourself to speak—
A maid of grace and complete majesty—
About surrender up of Aquitaine
To her decrepit, sick, and bedrid father.
Therefore this article is made in vain,
Or vainly comes th’ admirèd princess hither.

speaker: KING
text: What say you, lords? Why, this was quite forgot.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
So study evermore is overshot.
While it doth study to have what it would,
It doth forget to do the thing it should.
And when it hath the thing it hunteth most,
’Tis won as towns with fire—so won, so lost.

speaker: KING
text:
We must of force dispense with this decree.
She must lie here on mere necessity.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Necessity will make us all forsworn
Three thousand times within this three years’ space;
For every man with his affects is born,
Not by might mastered, but by special grace.
If I break faith, this word shall speak for me:
I am forsworn on mere necessity.
So to the laws at large I write my name,
And he that breaks them in the least degree
Stands in attainder of eternal shame.
Suggestions are to other as to me,
But I believe, although I seem so loath,
I am the last that will last keep his oath.
But is there no quick recreation granted?

speaker: KING
text:
Ay, that there is. Our court, you know, is haunted
With a refinèd traveler of Spain,
A man in all the world’s new fashion planted,
That hath a mint of phrases in his brain;
One who the music of his own vain tongue
Doth ravish like enchanting harmony,
A man of compliments, whom right and wrong
Have chose as umpire of their mutiny.
This child of fancy, that Armado hight,
For interim to our studies shall relate
In high-born words the worth of many a knight
From tawny Spain lost in the world’s debate.
How you delight, my lords, I know not, I,
But I protest I love to hear him lie,
And I will use him for my minstrelsy.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Armado is a most illustrious wight,
A man of fire-new words, fashion’s own knight.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text:
Costard the swain and he shall be our sport,
And so to study three years is but short.

speaker: DULL
text: Which is the Duke’s own person?

speaker: BEROWNE
text: This, fellow. What wouldst?

speaker: DULL
text:
I myself reprehend his own person, for I am his
Grace’s farborough. But I would see his own
person in flesh and blood.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: This is he.

speaker: DULL
text:
Signior Arm-, Arm-, commends you.
There’s villainy abroad. This letter will tell you
more.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
Sir, the contempts thereof are as touching
me.

speaker: KING
text: A letter from the magnificent Armado.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
How low soever the matter, I hope in God
for high words.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text:
A high hope for a low heaven. God grant
us patience!

speaker: BEROWNE
text: To hear, or forbear hearing?

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text:
To hear meekly, sir, and to laugh moderately,
or to forbear both.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Well, sir, be it as the style shall give us cause
to climb in the merriness.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
The matter is to me, sir, as concerning
Jaquenetta. The manner of it is, I was taken with
the manner.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: In what manner?

speaker: COSTARD
text:
In manner and form following, sir, all those
three. I was seen with her in the manor house,
sitting with her upon the form, and taken following
her into the park, which, put together, is “in manner
and form following.” Now, sir, for the manner.
It is the manner of a man to speak to a woman. For
the form—in some form.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: For the “following,” sir?

speaker: COSTARD
text:
As it shall follow in my correction, and God
defend the right.

speaker: KING
text: Will you hear this letter with attention?

speaker: BEROWNE
text: As we would hear an oracle.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
Such is the sinplicity of man to hearken after
the flesh.

speaker: KING
text: Great deputy , the welkin’s vicegerent and sole dominator of Navarre , my soul’s earth’s god , and body’s fost’ring patron —

speaker: COSTARD
text: Not a word of Costard yet.

speaker: KING
text: So it is —

speaker: COSTARD
text:
It may be so, but if he say it is so, he is, in
telling true, but so.

speaker: KING
text: Peace.

speaker: COSTARD
text: Be to me, and every man that dares not fight.

speaker: KING
text: No words.

speaker: COSTARD
text: Of other men’s secrets, I beseech you.

speaker: KING
text: So it is , besieged with sable-colored melancholy , I did commend the black oppressing humor to the most wholesome physic of thy health-giving air ; and , as I am a gentleman , betook myself to walk . The time when ? About the sixth hour , when beasts most graze , birds best peck , and men sit down to that nourishment which is called supper . So much for the time when . Now for the ground which — which , I mean , I walked upon . It is yclept thy park . Then for the place where — where , I mean , I did encounter that obscene and most prepost’rous event that draweth from my snow-white pen the ebon-colored ink , which here thou viewest , beholdest , surveyest , or seest . But to the place where . It standeth north-north-east and by east from the west corner of thy curious-knotted garden . There did I see that low-spirited swain , that base minnow of thy mirth , —

speaker: COSTARD
text: Me?

speaker: KING
text: that unlettered , small-knowing soul , —

speaker: COSTARD
text: Me?

speaker: KING
text: that shallow vassal , —

speaker: COSTARD
text: Still me?

speaker: KING
text: which , as I remember , hight Costard , —

speaker: COSTARD
text: O, me!

speaker: KING
text: sorted and consorted , contrary to thy established proclaimed edict and continent canon , which with — O with — but with this I passion to say wherewith —

speaker: COSTARD
text: With a wench.

speaker: KING
text: with a child of our grandmother Eve , a female ; or , for thy more sweet understanding , a woman : him , I , as my ever-esteemed duty pricks me on , have sent to thee , to receive the meed of punishment by thy sweet Grace’s officer , Anthony Dull , a man of good repute , carriage , bearing , and estimation .

speaker: DULL
text: Me, an ’t shall please you. I am Anthony Dull.

speaker: KING
text: For Jaquenetta — so is the weaker vessel called which I apprehended with the aforesaid swain — I keep her as a vessel of thy law’s fury , and shall , at the least of thy sweet notice , bring her to trial . Thine , in all compliments of devoted and heartburning heat of duty , Don Adriano de Armado .

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
This is not so well as I looked for, but the
best that ever I heard.

speaker: KING
text:
Ay, the best, for the worst. But,
sirrah, what say you to this?

speaker: COSTARD
text: Sir, I confess the wench.

speaker: KING
text: Did you hear the proclamation?

speaker: COSTARD
text:
I do confess much of the hearing it, but little
of the marking of it.

speaker: KING
text:
It was proclaimed a year’s imprisonment to be
taken with a wench.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
I was taken with none, sir. I was taken with a
damsel.

speaker: KING
text: Well, it was proclaimed “damsel.”

speaker: COSTARD
text:
This was no damsel neither, sir. She was a
virgin.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
It is so varied too, for it was proclaimed
“virgin.”

speaker: COSTARD
text:
If it were, I deny her virginity. I was taken
with a maid.

speaker: KING
text: This “maid” will not serve your turn, sir.

speaker: COSTARD
text: This maid will serve my turn, sir.

speaker: KING
text:
Sir, I will pronounce your sentence: you shall
fast a week with bran and water.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
I had rather pray a month with mutton and
porridge.

speaker: KING
text:
And Don Armado shall be your keeper.
My Lord Berowne, see him delivered o’er,
And go we, lords, to put in practice that
Which each to other hath so strongly sworn.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
I’ll lay my head to any goodman’s hat,
These oaths and laws will prove an idle scorn.
Sirrah, come on.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
I suffer for the truth, sir; for true it is I was
taken with Jaquenetta, and Jaquenetta is a true
girl. And therefore welcome the sour cup of prosperity.
Affliction may one day smile again, and till
then, sit thee down, sorrow.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Boy, what sign is it when a man of great spirit
grows melancholy?

speaker: BOY
text: A great sign, sir, that he will look sad.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Why, sadness is one and the selfsame thing,
dear imp.

speaker: BOY
text: No, no. O Lord, sir, no!

speaker: ARMADO
text:
How canst thou part sadness and melancholy,
my tender juvenal?

speaker: BOY
text:
By a familiar demonstration of the working, my
tough signior.

speaker: ARMADO
text: Why “tough signior”? Why “tough signior”?

speaker: BOY
text: Why “tender juvenal”? Why “tender juvenal”?

speaker: ARMADO
text:
I spoke it “tender juvenal” as a congruent
epitheton appertaining to thy young days, which
we may nominate “tender.”

speaker: BOY
text:
And I “tough signior” as an appurtenant title to
your old time, which we may name “tough.”

speaker: ARMADO
text: Pretty and apt.

speaker: BOY
text:
How mean you, sir? I pretty and my saying apt, or
I apt and my saying pretty?

speaker: ARMADO
text: Thou pretty because little.

speaker: BOY
text: Little pretty, because little. Wherefore apt?

speaker: ARMADO
text: And therefore apt, because quick.

speaker: BOY
text: Speak you this in my praise, master?

speaker: ARMADO
text: In thy condign praise.

speaker: BOY
text: I will praise an eel with the same praise.

speaker: ARMADO
text: What, that an eel is ingenious?

speaker: BOY
text: That an eel is quick.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
I do say thou art quick in answers. Thou
heat’st my blood.

speaker: BOY
text: I am answered, sir.

speaker: ARMADO
text: I love not to be crossed.

speaker: BOY
text:
He speaks the mere contrary; crosses love
not him.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
I have promised to study three years with the
Duke.

speaker: BOY
text: You may do it in an hour, sir.

speaker: ARMADO
text: Impossible.

speaker: BOY
text: How many is one thrice told?

speaker: ARMADO
text:
I am ill at reckoning. It fitteth the spirit of a
tapster.

speaker: BOY
text: You are a gentleman and a gamester, sir.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
I confess both. They are both the varnish of a
complete man.

speaker: BOY
text:
Then I am sure you know how much the gross
sum of deuce-ace amounts to.

speaker: ARMADO
text: It doth amount to one more than two.

speaker: BOY
text: Which the base vulgar do call “three.”

speaker: ARMADO
text: True.

speaker: BOY
text:
Why, sir, is this such a piece of study? Now here is
“three” studied ere you’ll thrice wink. And how
easy it is to put “years” to the word “three” and
study “three years” in two words, the dancing horse
will tell you.

speaker: ARMADO
text: A most fine figure.

speaker: BOY
text: To prove you a cipher.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
I will hereupon confess I am in love; and as it
is base for a soldier to love, so am I in love with a
base wench. If drawing my sword against the
humor of affection would deliver me from the
reprobate thought of it, I would take desire prisoner
and ransom him to any French courtier for a
new-devised curtsy. I think scorn to sigh; methinks
I should outswear Cupid. Comfort me, boy. What
great men have been in love?

speaker: BOY
text: Hercules, master.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Most sweet Hercules! More authority, dear
boy, name more; and, sweet my child, let them be
men of good repute and carriage.

speaker: BOY
text:
Samson, master; he was a man of good carriage,
great carriage, for he carried the town gates on his
back like a porter, and he was in love.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
O, well-knit Samson, strong-jointed Samson;
I do excel thee in my rapier as much as thou didst
me in carrying gates. I am in love too. Who was
Samson’s love, my dear Mote?

speaker: BOY
text: A woman, master.

speaker: ARMADO
text: Of what complexion?

speaker: BOY
text:
Of all the four, or the three, or the two, or one of
the four.

speaker: ARMADO
text: Tell me precisely of what complexion.

speaker: BOY
text: Of the sea-water green, sir.

speaker: ARMADO
text: Is that one of the four complexions?

speaker: BOY
text: As I have read, sir, and the best of them too.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Green indeed is the color of lovers. But to
have a love of that color, methinks Samson had
small reason for it. He surely affected her for her
wit.

speaker: BOY
text: It was so, sir, for she had a green wit.

speaker: ARMADO
text: My love is most immaculate white and red.

speaker: BOY
text:
Most maculate thoughts, master, are masked
under such colors.

speaker: ARMADO
text: Define, define, well-educated infant.

speaker: BOY
text:
My father’s wit and my mother’s tongue, assist
me.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Sweet invocation of a child, most pretty and
pathetical.

speaker: BOY
text:
If she be made of white and red,
Her faults will ne’er be known,
For blushing cheeks by faults are bred,
And fears by pale white shown.
Then if she fear, or be to blame,
By this you shall not know,
For still her cheeks possess the same
Which native she doth owe.
A dangerous rhyme, master, against the reason of
white and red.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Is there not a ballad, boy, of The King and
the Beggar?

speaker: BOY
text:
The world was very guilty of such a ballad some
three ages since, but I think now ’tis not to be found;
or if it were, it would neither serve for the writing
nor the tune.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
I will have that subject newly writ o’er, that I
may example my digression by some mighty precedent.
Boy, I do love that country girl that I took in
the park with the rational hind Costard. She deserves
well.

speaker: BOY
text:
To be whipped—and yet a better love than
my master.

speaker: ARMADO
text: Sing, boy. My spirit grows heavy in love.

speaker: BOY
text:
And that’s great marvel, loving a light
wench.

speaker: ARMADO
text: I say sing.

speaker: BOY
text: Forbear till this company be past.

speaker: DULL
text:
Sir, the Duke’s pleasure is that you
keep Costard safe, and you must suffer him to take
no delight, nor no penance, but he must fast three
days a week. For this damsel, I must keep her at the
park. She is allowed for the dey-woman. Fare you
well.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
I do betray myself with blushing.—
Maid.

speaker: JAQUENETTA
text: Man.

speaker: ARMADO
text: I will visit thee at the lodge.

speaker: JAQUENETTA
text: That’s hereby.

speaker: ARMADO
text: I know where it is situate.

speaker: JAQUENETTA
text: Lord, how wise you are.

speaker: ARMADO
text: I will tell thee wonders.

speaker: JAQUENETTA
text: With that face?

speaker: ARMADO
text: I love thee.

speaker: JAQUENETTA
text: So I heard you say.

speaker: ARMADO
text: And so, farewell.

speaker: JAQUENETTA
text: Fair weather after you.

speaker: DULL
text: Come, Jaquenetta, away.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Villain, thou shalt fast for thy
offenses ere thou be pardoned.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
Well, sir, I hope when I do it I shall do it on
a full stomach.

speaker: ARMADO
text: Thou shalt be heavily punished.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
I am more bound to you than your fellows,
for they are but lightly rewarded.

speaker: ARMADO
text: Take away this villain. Shut him up.

speaker: BOY
text: Come, you transgressing slave, away.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
Let me not be pent up, sir. I will
fast being loose.

speaker: BOY
text:
No, sir, that were fast and loose. Thou shalt to
prison.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
Well, if ever I do see the merry days of
desolation that I have seen, some shall see.

speaker: BOY
text: What shall some see?

speaker: COSTARD
text:
Nay, nothing, Master Mote, but what they
look upon. It is not for prisoners to be too silent in
their words, and therefore I will say nothing. I thank
God I have as little patience as another man, and
therefore I can be quiet.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
I do affect the very ground (which is base)
where her shoe (which is baser) guided by her foot
(which is basest) doth tread. I shall be forsworn
(which is a great argument of falsehood) if I love.
And how can that be true love which is falsely
attempted? Love is a familiar; love is a devil. There is
no evil angel but love, yet was Samson so tempted,
and he had an excellent strength; yet was Solomon
so seduced, and he had a very good wit. Cupid’s
butt-shaft is too hard for Hercules’ club, and therefore
too much odds for a Spaniard’s rapier. The first
and second cause will not serve my turn; the
