passado he respects not, the duello he regards not.
His disgrace is to be called “boy,” but his glory is to
subdue men. Adieu, valor; rust, rapier; be still,
drum, for your manager is in love. Yea, he loveth.
Assist me, some extemporal god of rhyme, for I am
sure I shall turn sonnet. Devise wit, write pen, for I
am for whole volumes in folio.

speaker: BOYET
text:
Now, madam, summon up your dearest spirits.
Consider who the King your father sends,
To whom he sends, and what’s his embassy.
Yourself, held precious in the world’s esteem,
To parley with the sole inheritor
Of all perfections that a man may owe,
Matchless Navarre; the plea of no less weight
Than Aquitaine, a dowry for a queen.
Be now as prodigal of all dear grace
As nature was in making graces dear
When she did starve the general world besides
And prodigally gave them all to you.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Good Lord Boyet, my beauty, though but mean,
Needs not the painted flourish of your praise.
Beauty is bought by judgment of the eye,
Not uttered by base sale of chapmen’s tongues.
I am less proud to hear you tell my worth
Than you much willing to be counted wise
In spending your wit in the praise of mine.
But now to task the tasker: good Boyet,
You are not ignorant all-telling fame
Doth noise abroad Navarre hath made a vow,
Till painful study shall outwear three years,
No woman may approach his silent court.
Therefore to ’s seemeth it a needful course,
Before we enter his forbidden gates,
To know his pleasure, and in that behalf,
Bold of your worthiness, we single you
As our best-moving fair solicitor.
Tell him the daughter of the King of France
On serious business craving quick dispatch,
Importunes personal conference with his Grace.
Haste, signify so much, while we attend,
Like humble-visaged suitors, his high will.

speaker: BOYET
text: Proud of employment, willingly I go.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
All pride is willing pride, and yours is so.
Who are the votaries, my loving lords,
That are vow-fellows with this virtuous duke?

speaker: A LORD
text: Lord Longaville is one.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Know you the man?

speaker: MARIA
text:
I know him, madam. At a marriage feast
Between Lord Perigort and the beauteous heir
Of Jaques Falconbridge, solemnizèd
In Normandy, saw I this Longaville.
A man of sovereign parts he is esteemed,
Well fitted in arts, glorious in arms.
Nothing becomes him ill that he would well.
The only soil of his fair virtue’s gloss,
If virtue’s gloss will stain with any soil,
Is a sharp wit matched with too blunt a will,
Whose edge hath power to cut, whose will still wills
It should none spare that come within his power.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Some merry mocking lord, belike. Is ’t so?

speaker: MARIA
text: They say so most that most his humors know.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Such short-lived wits do wither as they grow.
Who are the rest?

speaker: KATHERINE
text:
The young Dumaine, a well-accomplished youth,
Of all that virtue love for virtue loved.
Most power to do most harm, least knowing ill;
For he hath wit to make an ill shape good,
And shape to win grace though he had no wit.
I saw him at the Duke Alanson’s once,
And much too little of that good I saw
Is my report to his great worthiness.

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
Another of these students at that time
Was there with him, if I have heard a truth.
Berowne they call him, but a merrier man,
Within the limit of becoming mirth,
I never spent an hour’s talk withal.
His eye begets occasion for his wit,
For every object that the one doth catch
The other turns to a mirth-moving jest,
Which his fair tongue, conceit’s expositor,
Delivers in such apt and gracious words
That agèd ears play truant at his tales,
And younger hearings are quite ravishèd,
So sweet and voluble is his discourse.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
God bless my ladies, are they all in love,
That every one her own hath garnishèd
With such bedecking ornaments of praise?

speaker: A LORD
text: Here comes Boyet.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Now, what admittance, lord?

speaker: BOYET
text:
Navarre had notice of your fair approach,
And he and his competitors in oath
Were all addressed to meet you, gentle lady,
Before I came. Marry, thus much I have learned:
He rather means to lodge you in the field,
Like one that comes here to besiege his court,
Than seek a dispensation for his oath
To let you enter his unpeopled house.
Here comes Navarre.

speaker: KING
text: Fair Princess, welcome to the court of Navarre.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
“Fair” I give you back again, and “welcome”
I have not yet. The roof of this court is too
high to be yours, and welcome to the wide fields too
base to be mine.

speaker: KING
text: You shall be welcome, madam, to my court.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: I will be welcome, then. Conduct me thither.

speaker: KING
text: Hear me, dear lady. I have sworn an oath.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Our Lady help my lord! He’ll be forsworn.

speaker: KING
text: Not for the world, fair madam, by my will.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Why, will shall break it, will and nothing else.

speaker: KING
text: Your Ladyship is ignorant what it is.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Were my lord so, his ignorance were wise,
Where now his knowledge must prove ignorance.
I hear your Grace hath sworn out housekeeping.
’Tis deadly sin to keep that oath, my lord,
And sin to break it.
But pardon me, I am too sudden bold.
To teach a teacher ill beseemeth me.
Vouchsafe to read the purpose of my coming,
And suddenly resolve me in my suit.

speaker: KING
text: Madam, I will, if suddenly I may.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
You will the sooner that I were away,
For you’ll prove perjured if you make me stay.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Did not I dance with you in Brabant once?

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Did not I dance with you in Brabant once?

speaker: BEROWNE
text: I know you did.

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
How needless was it then
To ask the question.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: You must not be so quick.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: ’Tis long of you that spur me with such questions.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Your wit’s too hot, it speeds too fast; ’twill tire.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Not till it leave the rider in the mire.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: What time o’ day?

speaker: ROSALINE
text: The hour that fools should ask.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Now fair befall your mask.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Fair fall the face it covers.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: And send you many lovers.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Amen, so you be none.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Nay, then, will I be gone.

speaker: KING
text:
Madam, your father here doth intimate
The payment of a hundred thousand crowns,
Being but the one half of an entire sum
Disbursèd by my father in his wars.
But say that he or we, as neither have,
Received that sum, yet there remains unpaid
A hundred thousand more, in surety of the which
One part of Aquitaine is bound to us,
Although not valued to the money’s worth.
If then the King your father will restore
But that one half which is unsatisfied,
We will give up our right in Aquitaine,
And hold fair friendship with his Majesty.
But that, it seems, he little purposeth;
For here he doth demand to have repaid
A hundred thousand crowns, and not demands,
On payment of a hundred thousand crowns,
To have his title live in Aquitaine—
Which we much rather had depart withal,
And have the money by our father lent,
Than Aquitaine, so gelded as it is.
Dear Princess, were not his requests so far
From reason’s yielding, your fair self should make
A yielding ’gainst some reason in my breast,
And go well satisfied to France again.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
You do the King my father too much wrong,
And wrong the reputation of your name,
In so unseeming to confess receipt
Of that which hath so faithfully been paid.

speaker: KING
PRINCESS
text:
We arrest your word.—
Boyet, you can produce acquittances
For such a sum from special officers
Of Charles his father.

speaker: KING
text: Satisfy me so.

speaker: BOYET
text:
So please your Grace, the packet is not come
Where that and other specialties are bound.
Tomorrow you shall have a sight of them.

speaker: KING
text:
It shall suffice me; at which interview
All liberal reason I will yield unto.
Meantime receive such welcome at my hand
As honor (without breach of honor) may
Make tender of to thy true worthiness.
You may not come, fair princess, within my gates,
But here without you shall be so received
As you shall deem yourself lodged in my heart,
Though so denied fair harbor in my house.
Your own good thoughts excuse me, and farewell.
Tomorrow shall we visit you again.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Sweet health and fair desires consort your Grace.

speaker: KING
text: Thy own wish wish I thee in every place.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Lady, I will commend you to
my own heart.

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
Pray you, do my commendations. I would
be glad to see it.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: I would you heard it groan.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Is the fool sick?

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Sick at the heart.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Alack, let it blood.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Would that do it good?

speaker: ROSALINE
text: My physic says “ay.”

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Will you prick ’t with your eye?

speaker: ROSALINE
text: No point, with my knife.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Now God save thy life.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: And yours from long living.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: I cannot stay thanksgiving.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: Sir, I pray you, a word. What lady is that same?

speaker: BOYET
text: The heir of Alanson, Katherine her name.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: A gallant lady, monsieur. Fare you well.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: I beseech you, a word. What is she in the white?

speaker: BOYET
text: A woman sometimes, an you saw her in the light.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: Perchance light in the light. I desire her name.

speaker: BOYET
text: She hath but one for herself; to desire that were a shame.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: Pray you, sir, whose daughter?

speaker: BOYET
text: Her mother’s, I have heard.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: God’s blessing on your beard!

speaker: BOYET
text:
Good sir, be not offended. She is an heir of
Falconbridge.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text:
Nay, my choler is ended. She is a most
sweet lady.

speaker: BOYET
text: Not unlike, sir, that may be.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: What’s her name in the cap?

speaker: BOYET
text: Rosaline, by good hap.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Is she wedded or no?

speaker: BOYET
text: To her will, sir, or so.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: You are welcome, sir. Adieu.

speaker: BOYET
text: Farewell to me, sir, and welcome to you.

speaker: MARIA
text:
That last is Berowne, the merry madcap lord.
Not a word with him but a jest.

speaker: BOYET
text: And every jest but a word.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: It was well done of you to take him at his word.

speaker: BOYET
text: I was as willing to grapple as he was to board.

speaker: KATHERINE
text: Two hot sheeps, marry.

speaker: BOYET
text:
And wherefore not ships?
No sheep, sweet lamb, unless we feed on your lips.

speaker: KATHERINE
text: You sheep and I pasture. Shall that finish the jest?

speaker: BOYET
text: So you grant pasture for me.

speaker: KATHERINE
text:
Not so, gentle beast,
My lips are no common, though several they be.

speaker: BOYET
text: Belonging to whom?

speaker: KATHERINE
text: To my fortunes and me.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Good wits will be jangling; but, gentles, agree,
This civil war of wits were much better used
On Navarre and his bookmen, for here ’tis abused.

speaker: BOYET
text:
If my observation, which very seldom lies,
By the heart’s still rhetoric, disclosèd wi’ th’ eyes,
Deceive me not now, Navarre is infected.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: With what?

speaker: BOYET
text: With that which we lovers entitle “affected.”

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Your reason?

speaker: BOYET
text:
Why, all his behaviors did make their retire
To the court of his eye, peeping thorough desire.
His heart like an agate with your print impressed,
Proud with his form, in his eye pride expressed.
His tongue, all impatient to speak and not see,
Did stumble with haste in his eyesight to be;
All senses to that sense did make their repair,
To feel only looking on fairest of fair.
Methought all his senses were locked in his eye,
As jewels in crystal for some prince to buy,
Who, tend’ring their own worth from where they were glassed,
Did point you to buy them along as you passed.
His face’s own margent did quote such amazes
That all eyes saw his eyes enchanted with gazes.
I’ll give you Aquitaine, and all that is his,
An you give him for my sake but one loving kiss.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Come, to our pavilion. Boyet is disposed.

speaker: BOYET
text:
But to speak that in words which his eye hath disclosed.
I only have made a mouth of his eye
By adding a tongue which I know will not lie.

speaker: MARIA
text: Thou art an old lovemonger and speakest skillfully.

speaker: KATHERINE
text: He is Cupid’s grandfather, and learns news of him.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Then was Venus like her mother, for her father is but grim.

speaker: BOYET
text: Do you hear, my mad wenches?

speaker: MARIA
text: No.

speaker: BOYET
text: What then, do you see?

speaker: MARIA
text: Ay, our way to be gone.

speaker: BOYET
text: You are too hard for me.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Warble, child, make passionate my sense of
hearing.

speaker: BOY
text: Concolinel.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Sweet air. Go, tenderness of years.
Take this key, give enlargement to the
swain, bring him festinately hither. I must employ
him in a letter to my love.

speaker: BOY
text:
Master, will you win your love with a French
brawl?

speaker: ARMADO
text: How meanest thou? Brawling in French?

speaker: BOY
text:
No, my complete master, but to jig off a tune at the
tongue’s end, canary to it with your feet, humor it
with turning up your eyelids, sigh a note and sing a
note, sometimes through the throat as if you
swallowed love with singing love, sometimes
through the nose as if you snuffed up love by
smelling love; with your hat penthouse-like o’er the
shop of your eyes, with your arms crossed on your
thin-belly doublet like a rabbit on a spit; or your
hands in your pocket like a man after the old
painting; and keep not too long in one tune, but a
snip and away. These are compliments, these are
humors; these betray nice wenches that would be
betrayed without these, and make them men of
note—do you note me?—that most are affected
to these.

speaker: ARMADO
text: How hast thou purchased this experience?

speaker: BOY
text: By my penny of observation.

speaker: ARMADO
text: But O— but O—.

speaker: BOY
text: “The hobby-horse is forgot.”

speaker: ARMADO
text: Call’st thou my love “hobby-horse”?

speaker: BOY
text:
No, master. The hobby-horse is but a colt,
and your love perhaps a hackney.—But have you
forgot your love?

speaker: ARMADO
text: Almost I had.

speaker: BOY
text: Negligent student, learn her by heart.

speaker: ARMADO
text: By heart and in heart, boy.

speaker: BOY
text:
And out of heart, master. All those three I will
prove.

speaker: ARMADO
text: What wilt thou prove?

speaker: BOY
text:
A man, if I live; and this “by, in, and without,”
upon the instant: “by” heart you love her, because
your heart cannot come by her; “in” heart you love
her, because your heart is in love with her; and
“out” of heart you love her, being out of heart that
you cannot enjoy her.

speaker: ARMADO
text: I am all these three.

speaker: BOY
text:
And three times as much more, and yet
nothing at all.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Fetch hither the swain. He must carry me a
letter.

speaker: BOY
text:
A message well sympathized—a horse to be ambassador
for an ass.

speaker: ARMADO
text: Ha? Ha? What sayest thou?

speaker: BOY
text:
Marry, sir, you must send the ass upon the horse,
for he is very slow-gaited. But I go.

speaker: ARMADO
text: The way is but short. Away!

speaker: BOY
text: As swift as lead, sir.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Thy meaning, pretty ingenious?
Is not lead a metal heavy, dull, and slow?

speaker: BOY
text: Minime, honest master, or rather, master, no.

speaker: ARMADO
text: I say lead is slow.

speaker: BOY
text:
You are too swift, sir, to say so.
Is that lead slow which is fired from a gun?

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Sweet smoke of rhetoric!
He reputes me a cannon, and the bullet, that’s he.—
I shoot thee at the swain.

speaker: BOY
text: Thump, then, and I flee.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
A most acute juvenal, voluble and free of grace.
By thy favor, sweet welkin, I must sigh in thy face.
Most rude melancholy, valor gives thee place.
My herald is returned.

speaker: BOY
text:
A wonder, master!
Here’s a costard broken in a shin.

speaker: ARMADO
text: Some enigma, some riddle. Come, thy l’envoi begin.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
No egma, no riddle, no l’envoi, no salve in
the mail, sir. O, sir, plantain, a plain plantain! No
l’envoi, no l’envoi, no salve, sir, but a plantain.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
By virtue, thou enforcest laughter; thy silly
thought, my spleen. The heaving of my lungs
provokes me to ridiculous smiling. O pardon me,
my stars! Doth the inconsiderate take salve for
l’envoi, and the word l’envoi for a salve?

speaker: BOY
text: Do the wise think them other? Is not l’envoi a salve?

speaker: ARMADO
text:
No, page, it is an epilogue or discourse to make plain
Some obscure precedence that hath tofore been sain.
I will example it:
The fox, the ape, and the humble-bee
Were still at odds, being but three.
There’s the moral. Now the l’envoi.

speaker: BOY
text: I will add the l’envoi. Say the moral again.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
The fox, the ape, and the humble-bee
Were still at odds, being but three.

speaker: BOY
text:
Until the goose came out of door
And stayed the odds by adding four.
Now will I begin your moral, and do you follow with
my l’envoi.
The fox, the ape, and the humble-bee
Were still at odds, being but three.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Until the goose came out of door,
Staying the odds by adding four.

speaker: BOY
text:
A good l’envoi, ending in the goose. Would you
desire more?

speaker: COSTARD
text:
The boy hath sold him a bargain—a goose, that’s flat.—
Sir, your pennyworth is good, an your goose be fat.
To sell a bargain well is as cunning as fast and loose.
Let me see: a fat l’envoi—ay, that’s a fat goose.

speaker: ARMADO
text: Come hither, come hither. How did this argument begin?

speaker: BOY
text:
By saying that a costard was broken in a shin.
Then called you for the l’envoi.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
True, and I for a plantain. Thus came your
argument in. Then the boy’s fat l’envoi, the goose
that you bought; and he ended the market.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
But tell me, how was there a costard broken
in a shin?

speaker: BOY
text: I will tell you sensibly.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
Thou hast no feeling of it, Mote. I will speak
that l’envoi.
I, Costard, running out, that was safely within,
Fell over the threshold and broke my shin.

speaker: ARMADO
text: We will talk no more of this matter.

speaker: COSTARD
text: Till there be more matter in the shin.

speaker: ARMADO
text: Sirrah Costard, I will enfranchise thee.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
O, marry me to one Frances! I smell some
l’envoi, some goose, in this.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
By my sweet soul, I mean, setting thee at
liberty, enfreedoming thy person. Thou wert immured,
restrained, captivated, bound.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
True, true; and now you will be my purgation,
and let me loose.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
I give thee thy liberty, set thee from durance,
and, in lieu thereof, impose on thee nothing but
this: bear this significant to the country maid
Jaquenetta. There is remuneration
for the best ward of
mine honor is rewarding my dependents.—Mote,
follow.

speaker: BOY
text: Like the sequel, I. Signior Costard, adieu.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
My sweet ounce of man’s flesh, my incony Jew!
Now will I look to his remuneration.
“Remuneration”! O, that’s the Latin word for
three farthings. Three farthings—remuneration.
“What’s the price of this inkle?” “One penny.” “No,
I’ll give you a remuneration.” Why, it carries it!
Remuneration. Why, it is a fairer name than “French
crown.” I will never buy and sell out of this word.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
My good knave Costard, exceedingly well
met.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
Pray you, sir, how much carnation ribbon
may a man buy for a remuneration?

speaker: BEROWNE
text: What is a remuneration?

speaker: COSTARD
text: Marry, sir, halfpenny farthing.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Why then, three farthing worth of silk.

speaker: COSTARD
text: I thank your Worship. God be wi’ you.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Stay, slave, I must employ thee.
As thou wilt win my favor, good my knave,
Do one thing for me that I shall entreat.

speaker: COSTARD
text: When would you have it done, sir?

speaker: BEROWNE
text: This afternoon.

speaker: COSTARD
text: Well, I will do it, sir. Fare you well.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Thou knowest not what it is.

speaker: COSTARD
text: I shall know, sir, when I have done it.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Why, villain, thou must know first.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
I will come to your Worship tomorrow
morning.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
It must be done this afternoon. Hark, slave,
it is but this:
The Princess comes to hunt here in the park,
And in her train there is a gentle lady.
When tongues speak sweetly, then they name her name,
And Rosaline they call her. Ask for her,
And to her white hand see thou do commend
This sealed-up counsel. There’s thy guerdon.
Go.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
Gardon. O sweet
gardon! Better than remuneration, a ’levenpence
farthing better! Most sweet gardon. I will do it, sir,
in print. Gardon! Remuneration!

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
And I forsooth in love! I that have been love’s whip,
A very beadle to a humorous sigh,
A critic, nay, a nightwatch constable,
A domineering pedant o’er the boy,
Than whom no mortal so magnificent.
This wimpled, whining, purblind, wayward boy,
This Signior Junior, giant dwarf, Dan Cupid,
Regent of love rhymes, lord of folded arms,
Th’ anointed sovereign of sighs and groans,
Liege of all loiterers and malcontents,
Dread prince of plackets, king of codpieces,
Sole imperator and great general
Of trotting paritors—O my little heart!
And I to be a corporal of his field
And wear his colors like a tumbler’s hoop!
What? I love, I sue, I seek a wife?
A woman, that is like a German clock,
Still a-repairing, ever out of frame,
And never going aright, being a watch,
But being watched that it may still go right.
Nay, to be perjured, which is worst of all.
And, among three, to love the worst of all,
A whitely wanton with a velvet brow,
With two pitch-balls stuck in her face for eyes.
Ay, and by heaven, one that will do the deed
Though Argus were her eunuch and her guard.
And I to sigh for her, to watch for her,
To pray for her! Go to. It is a plague
That Cupid will impose for my neglect
Of his almighty dreadful little might.
Well, I will love, write, sigh, pray, sue, groan.
Some men must love my lady, and some Joan.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Was that the King that spurred his horse so hard
Against the steep uprising of the hill?

speaker: FORESTER
text: I know not, but I think it was not he.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Whoe’er he was, he showed a mounting mind.—
Well, lords, today we shall have our dispatch.
Or Saturday we will return to France.—
Then, forester, my friend, where is the bush
That we must stand and play the murderer in?

speaker: FORESTER
text:
Hereby, upon the edge of yonder coppice,
A stand where you may make the fairest shoot.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
I thank my beauty, I am fair that shoot,
And thereupon thou speakst “the fairest shoot.”

speaker: FORESTER
text: Pardon me, madam, for I meant not so.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
What, what? First praise me, and again say no?
O short-lived pride. Not fair? Alack, for woe!

speaker: FORESTER
text: Yes, madam, fair.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Nay, never paint me now.
Where fair is not, praise cannot mend the brow.
Here, good my glass, take this for telling true.
Fair payment for foul words is more than due.

speaker: FORESTER
text: Nothing but fair is that which you inherit.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
See, see, my beauty will be saved by merit.
O heresy in fair, fit for these days!
A giving hand, though foul, shall have fair praise.
But come, the bow. Now mercy goes to kill,
And shooting well is then accounted ill.
Thus will I save my credit in the shoot:
Not wounding, pity would not let me do ’t;
If wounding, then it was to show my skill,
That more for praise than purpose meant to kill.
And out of question so it is sometimes:
Glory grows guilty of detested crimes,
When for fame’s sake, for praise, an outward part,
We bend to that the working of the heart;
As I for praise alone now seek to spill
The poor deer’s blood, that my heart means no ill.

speaker: BOYET
text:
Do not curst wives hold that self sovereignty
Only for praise’ sake when they strive to be
Lords o’er their lords?

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Only for praise; and praise we may afford
To any lady that subdues a lord.

speaker: BOYET
text: Here comes a member of the commonwealth.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
God dig-you-den all! Pray you, which is the
head lady?

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Thou shalt know her, fellow, by the rest that
have no heads.

speaker: COSTARD
text: Which is the greatest lady, the highest?

speaker: PRINCESS
text: The thickest and the tallest.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
The thickest and the tallest: it is so, truth is truth.
An your waist, mistress, were as slender as my wit,
One o’ these maids’ girdles for your waist should be fit.
Are not you the chief woman? You are the thickest here.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: What’s your will, sir? What’s your will?

speaker: COSTARD
text:
I have a letter from Monsieur Berowne to
one Lady Rosaline.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
O, thy letter, thy letter! He’s a good friend of mine.
Stand aside, good bearer.—Boyet, you can carve.
Break up this capon.

speaker: BOYET
text:
I am bound to serve.
This letter is mistook; it importeth none here.
It is writ to Jaquenetta.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
We will read it, I swear.
Break the neck of the wax, and everyone give ear.

speaker: BOYET
text:
Thus dost thou hear the Nemean lion roar
’Gainst thee, thou lamb, that standest as his prey.
Submissive fall his princely feet before,
And he from forage will incline to play.
But if thou strive, poor soul, what art thou then?
Food for his rage, repasture for his den.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
What plume of feathers is he that indited this letter?
What vane? What weathercock? Did you ever hear better?

speaker: BOYET
text: I am much deceived but I remember the style.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Else your memory is bad, going o’er it erewhile.

speaker: BOYET
text:
This Armado is a Spaniard that keeps here in court,
A phantasime, a Monarcho, and one that makes sport
To the Prince and his bookmates.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Thou, fellow, a word.
Who gave thee this letter?

speaker: COSTARD
text: I told you: my lord.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: To whom shouldst thou give it?

speaker: COSTARD
text: From my lord to my lady.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: From which lord to which lady?

speaker: COSTARD
text:
From my Lord Berowne, a good master of mine,
To a lady of France that he called Rosaline.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Thou hast mistaken his letter. Come, lords, away.
Here, sweet, put up this; ’twill be thine another day.

speaker: BOYET
text: Who is the shooter? Who is the shooter?

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Shall I teach you to know?

speaker: BOYET
text: Ay, my continent of beauty.

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
Why, she that bears the bow.
Finely put off.

speaker: BOYET
text:
My lady goes to kill horns, but if thou marry,
Hang me by the neck if horns that year miscarry.
Finely put on.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Well, then, I am the shooter.

speaker: BOYET
text: And who is your deer?

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
If we choose by the horns, yourself come not near.
Finely put on, indeed.

speaker: MARIA
text: You still wrangle with her, Boyet, and she strikes at the brow.

speaker: BOYET
text: But she herself is hit lower. Have I hit her now?

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
Shall I come upon thee with an old saying,
that was a man when King Pippen of France was a
little boy, as touching the hit it?

speaker: BOYET
text:
So I may answer thee with one as old, that was a
woman when Queen Guinover of Britain was a little
wench, as touching the hit it.

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
Thou canst not hit it, hit it, hit it,
Thou canst not hit it, my good man.

speaker: BOYET
text:
An I cannot, cannot, cannot,
An I cannot, another can.

speaker: COSTARD
text: By my troth, most pleasant. How both did fit it!

speaker: MARIA
text: A mark marvelous well shot, for they both did hit it.

speaker: BOYET
text:
A mark! O, mark but that mark. “A mark,” says my lady.
Let the mark have a prick in ’t to mete at, if it may be.

speaker: MARIA
text: Wide o’ the bow hand! I’ faith, your hand is out.

speaker: COSTARD
text: Indeed, he must shoot nearer, or he’ll ne’er hit the clout.

speaker: BOYET
text: An if my hand be out, then belike your hand is in.

speaker: COSTARD
text: Then will she get the upshoot by cleaving the pin.

speaker: MARIA
text: Come, come, you talk greasily. Your lips grow foul.

speaker: COSTARD
text: She’s too hard for you at pricks, sir. Challenge her to bowl.

speaker: BOYET
text: I fear too much rubbing. Good night, my good owl.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
By my soul, a swain, a most simple clown.
Lord, Lord, how the ladies and I have put him down.
O’ my troth, most sweet jests, most incony vulgar wit,
When it comes so smoothly off, so obscenely, as it were, so fit.
Armado o’ th’ one side, O, a most dainty man!
To see him walk before a lady and to bear her fan.
To see him kiss his hand, and how most sweetly he will swear.
And his page o’ t’ other side, that handful of wit!
Ah heavens, it is a most pathetical nit.
Sola, sola!

speaker: NATHANIEL
text:
Very reverend sport, truly, and done in the
testimony of a good conscience.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
The deer was, as you know, sanguis, in
blood, ripe as the pomewater, who now hangeth
like a jewel in the ear of caelo, the sky, the welkin,
the heaven, and anon falleth like a crab on the face
of terra, the soil, the land, the earth.

speaker: NATHANIEL
text:
Truly, Master Holofernes, the epithets are
sweetly varied, like a scholar at the least. But, sir, I
assure you, it was a buck of the first head.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text: Sir Nathaniel, haud credo.

speaker: DULL
text: ’Twas not a haud credo, ’twas a pricket.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Most barbarous intimation! Yet a kind of
insinuation, as it were, in via, in way, of explication;
facere, as it were, replication, or rather, ostentare, to
show, as it were, his inclination, after his undressed,
unpolished, uneducated, unpruned, untrained, or
rather unlettered, or ratherest, unconfirmed fashion,
to insert again my haud credo for a deer.

speaker: DULL
text:
I said the deer was not a haud credo, ’twas a
pricket.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Twice-sod simplicity, bis coctus!
O thou monster ignorance, how deformed dost thou look!

speaker: NATHANIEL
text:
Sir, he hath never fed of the dainties that are bred in a book.
He hath not eat paper, as it were; he hath not drunk
ink. His intellect is not replenished. He is only an
animal, only sensible in the duller parts.
And such barren plants are set before us that we thankful should be—
Which we of taste and feeling are—for those parts that do fructify in us more than he.
For as it would ill become me to be vain, indiscreet, or a fool,
So were there a patch set on learning, to see him in a school.
But omne bene, say I, being of an old father’s mind:
Many can brook the weather that love not the wind.

speaker: DULL
text:
You two are bookmen. Can you tell me by your wit
What was a month old at Cain’s birth that’s not five weeks old as yet?

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Dictynna, goodman Dull, Dictynna,
goodman Dull.

speaker: DULL
text: What is “dictima”?

speaker: NATHANIEL
text: A title to Phoebe, to Luna, to the moon.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
The moon was a month old when Adam was no more.
And raught not to five weeks when he came to fivescore.
Th’ allusion holds in the exchange.

speaker: DULL
text:
’Tis true indeed. The collusion holds in the
exchange.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
God comfort thy capacity! I say, th’ allusion
holds in the exchange.

speaker: DULL
text:
And I say the pollution holds in the exchange, for
the moon is never but a month old. And I say besides
that, ’twas a pricket that the Princess killed.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Sir Nathaniel, will you hear an extemporal
epitaph on the death of the deer? And, to humor
the ignorant, call I the deer the Princess killed a
pricket.

speaker: NATHANIEL
text:
Perge, good Master Holofernes, perge, so it
shall please you to abrogate scurrility.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
I will something affect the letter, for it
argues facility.
The preyful princess pierced and pricked a pretty pleasing pricket,
Some say a sore, but not a sore till now made sore with shooting.
The dogs did yell. Put “l” to “sore,” then sorel jumps from thicket,
Or pricket sore, or else sorel. The people fall a-hooting.
If sore be sore, then “L” to “sore” makes fifty sores o’ sorel.
Of one sore I an hundred make by adding but one more “L.”

speaker: NATHANIEL
text: A rare talent.

speaker: DULL
text:
If a talent be a claw, look how he claws
him with a talent.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
This is a gift that I have, simple, simple—
a foolish extravagant spirit, full of forms,
figures, shapes, objects, ideas, apprehensions, motions,
revolutions. These are begot in the ventricle
of memory, nourished in the womb of pia mater,
and delivered upon the mellowing of occasion. But
the gift is good in those in whom it is acute, and I
am thankful for it.

speaker: NATHANIEL
text:
Sir, I praise the Lord for you, and so may
my parishioners, for their sons are well tutored by
you, and their daughters profit very greatly under
you. You are a good member of the
commonwealth.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Mehercle, if their sons be ingenious,
they shall want no instruction; if their daughters be
capable, I will put it to them. But Vir sapis qui pauca
loquitur. A soul feminine saluteth us.

speaker: JAQUENETTA
text:
God give you good morrow,
Master Person.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Master Person, quasi pierce one. And
if one should be pierced, which is the one?

speaker: COSTARD
text:
Marry, Master Schoolmaster, he that is likeliest
to a hogshead.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Of piercing a hogshead! A good luster
of conceit in a turf of earth; fire enough for a flint,
pearl enough for a swine. ’Tis pretty, it is well.

speaker: JAQUENETTA
text:
Good Master Parson, be so
good as read me this letter. It was given me by
Costard, and sent me from Don Armado. I beseech
you, read it.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Facile precor gelida quando peccas omnia sub umbra.
Ruminat—
and so forth. Ah, good old Mantuan! I may speak of
thee as the traveler doth of Venice:
Venetia, Venetia,
Chi non ti vede, non ti pretia.
Old Mantuan, old Mantuan! Who understandeth
thee not, loves thee not. Ut, re, sol, la,
mi, fa. Under pardon, sir, what are
the contents? Or rather, as Horace says in his—
What, my soul, verses?

speaker: NATHANIEL
text: Ay, sir, and very learned.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Let me hear a staff, a stanza, a verse,
Lege, domine.

speaker: NATHANIEL
text:
If love make me forsworn, how shall I swear to love?
Ah, never faith could hold, if not to beauty vowed!
Though to myself forsworn, to thee I’ll faithful prove.
Those thoughts to me were oaks, to thee like osiers bowed.
Study his bias leaves and makes his book thine eyes,
Where all those pleasures live that art would comprehend.
If knowledge be the mark, to know thee shall suffice.
Well-learnèd is that tongue that well can thee commend.
All ignorant that soul that sees thee without wonder;
Which is to me some praise that I thy parts admire.
Thy eye Jove’s lightning bears, thy voice his dreadful thunder,
Which, not to anger bent, is music and sweet fire.
Celestial as thou art, O, pardon love this wrong,
That sings heaven’s praise with such an earthly tongue.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
You find not the apostrophus, and so
miss the accent. Let me supervise the canzonet.
Here are only numbers ratified,
but, for the elegancy, facility, and golden cadence of
poesy—caret. Ovidius Naso was the man. And why
indeed “Naso,” but for smelling out the odoriferous
flowers of fancy, the jerks of invention? Imitari is
nothing: so doth the hound his master, the ape his
keeper, the tired horse his rider.—But damosella
virgin, was this directed to you?

speaker: JAQUENETTA
text:
Ay, sir, from one Monsieur Berowne, one
of the strange queen’s lords.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
I will overglance the superscript: “ To the snow-white hand of the most beauteous Lady Rosaline . ” I will look again on the intellect of the
letter for the nomination of the party writing to
the person written unto: “ Your Ladyship’s in all desired employment , Berowne . ” Sir Nathaniel, this
Berowne is one of the votaries with the King, and
here he hath framed a letter to a sequent of the
stranger queen’s: which accidentally, or by the way
of progression, hath miscarried.
Trip and go, my sweet. Deliver this paper into the
royal hand of the King. It may concern much. Stay
not thy compliment. I forgive thy duty. Adieu.

speaker: JAQUENETTA
text:
Good Costard, go with me.—Sir, God
save your life.

speaker: COSTARD
text: Have with thee, my girl.

speaker: NATHANIEL
text:
Sir, you have done this in the fear of God
very religiously; and, as a certain Father saith—

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Sir, tell not me of the Father. I do fear
colorable colors. But to return to the verses: did
they please you, Sir Nathaniel?

speaker: NATHANIEL
text: Marvelous well for the pen.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
I do dine today at the father’s of a certain
pupil of mine, where if, before repast, it shall
please you to gratify the table with a grace, I will,
on my privilege I have with the parents of the
foresaid child or pupil, undertake your ben venuto;
where I will prove those verses to be very unlearned,
neither savoring of poetry, wit, nor invention.
I beseech your society.

speaker: NATHANIEL
text:
And thank you too; for society, saith the
text, is the happiness of life.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
And certes the text most infallibly concludes
it. Sir, I do invite you too. You shall
not say me nay. Pauca verba. Away! The gentles are
at their game, and we will to our recreation.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
The King, he is hunting the deer; I am
coursing myself. They have pitched a toil; I am
toiling in a pitch—pitch that defiles. Defile! A foul
word. Well, “set thee down, sorrow”; for so they
say the fool said, and so say I, and I the fool. Well
proved, wit. By the Lord, this love is as mad as Ajax.
It kills sheep, it kills me, I a sheep. Well proved
again, o’ my side. I will not love. If I do, hang me. I’
faith, I will not. O, but her eye! By this light, but for
her eye I would not love her; yes, for her two eyes.
Well, I do nothing in the world but lie, and lie in my
throat. By heaven, I do love, and it hath taught me to
rhyme, and to be melancholy. And here is part of my
rhyme, and here my melancholy. Well, she hath one
o’ my sonnets already. The clown bore it, the fool
sent it, and the lady hath it. Sweet clown, sweeter
fool, sweetest lady. By the world, I would not care a
pin, if the other three were in. Here comes one with
a paper. God give him grace to groan.

speaker: KING
text: Ay me!

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Shot, by heaven! Proceed, sweet
Cupid. Thou hast thumped him with thy birdbolt
under the left pap. In faith, secrets!

speaker: KING
text:
So sweet a kiss the golden sun gives not
To those fresh morning drops upon the rose
As thy eyebeams, when their fresh rays have smote
The night of dew that on my cheeks down flows.
Nor shines the silver moon one-half so bright
Through the transparent bosom of the deep
As doth thy face, through tears of mine, give light.
Thou shin’st in every tear that I do weep.
No drop but as a coach doth carry thee;
So ridest thou triumphing in my woe.
Do but behold the tears that swell in me,
And they thy glory through my grief will show.
But do not love thyself; then thou wilt keep
My tears for glasses, and still make me weep.
O queen of queens, how far dost thou excel
No thought can think, nor tongue of mortal tell.
How shall she know my griefs? I’ll drop the paper.
Sweet leaves, shade folly. Who is he comes here?
What, Longaville, and reading! Listen, ear.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Now, in thy likeness, one more fool appear!

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: Ay me! I am forsworn.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Why, he comes in like a perjure, wearing papers!

speaker: KING
text: In love, I hope! Sweet fellowship in shame.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: One drunkard loves another of the name.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: Am I the first that have been perjured so?

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
I could put thee in comfort: not by two that I know.
Thou makest the triumviry, the corner-cap of society,
The shape of love’s Tyburn, that hangs up simplicity.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text:
I fear these stubborn lines lack power to move.
O sweet Maria , empress of my love —
These numbers will I tear and write in prose.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
O, rhymes are guards on wanton Cupid’s hose.
Disfigure not his shop!

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text:
This same shall go.
Did not the heavenly rhetoric of thine eye,
’Gainst whom the world cannot hold argument,
Persuade my heart to this false perjury?
Vows for thee broke deserve not punishment.
A woman I forswore, but I will prove,
Thou being a goddess, I forswore not thee.
My vow was earthly, thou a heavenly love.
Thy grace being gained cures all disgrace in me.
Vows are but breath, and breath a vapor is.
Then thou, fair sun, which on my Earth dost shine,
Exhal’st this vapor-vow; in thee it is.
If broken, then, it is no fault of mine.
If by me broke, what fool is not so wise
To lose an oath to win a paradise?

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
This is the liver vein, which makes flesh a deity,
A green goose a goddess. Pure, pure idolatry.
God amend us, God amend. We are much out o’ th’ way.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: By whom shall I send this?—Company? Stay.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
All hid, all hid—an old infant play.
Like a demigod here sit I in the sky,
And wretched fools’ secrets heedfully o’ereye.
More sacks to the mill. O heavens, I have my wish.
Dumaine transformed! Four woodcocks in a dish.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: O most divine Kate!

speaker: BEROWNE
text: O most profane coxcomb!

speaker: DUMAINE
text: By heaven, the wonder in a mortal eye!

speaker: BEROWNE
text: By Earth, she is not, corporal. There you lie.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: Her amber hairs for foul hath amber quoted.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: An amber-colored raven was well noted.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: As upright as the cedar.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Stoop, I say.
Her shoulder is with child.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: As fair as day.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Ay, as some days, but then no sun must shine.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: O, that I had my wish!

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: And I had mine!

speaker: KING
text: And mine too, good Lord!

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Amen, so I had mine. Is not that a good word?

speaker: DUMAINE
text:
I would forget her, but a fever she
Reigns in my blood, and will remembered be.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
A fever in your blood? Why, then incision
Would let her out in saucers! Sweet misprision.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: Once more I’ll read the ode that I have writ.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Once more I’ll mark how love can vary wit.

speaker: DUMAINE
text:
On a day—alack the day!—
Love, whose month is ever May,
Spied a blossom passing fair,
Playing in the wanton air.
Through the velvet leaves the wind,
All unseen, can passage find;
That the lover, sick to death,
Wished himself the heaven’s breath.
“Air,” quoth he, “thy cheeks may blow.
Air, would I might triumph so!”
But, alack, my hand is sworn
Ne’er to pluck thee from thy thorn.
Vow, alack, for youth unmeet,
Youth so apt to pluck a sweet.
Do not call it sin in me
That I am forsworn for thee—
Thou for whom Jove would swear
Juno but an Ethiope were,
And deny himself for Jove,
Turning mortal for thy love.
This will I send, and something else more plain
That shall express my true love’s fasting pain.
O, would the King, Berowne, and Longaville
Were lovers too! Ill to example ill
Would from my forehead wipe a perjured note,
For none offend where all alike do dote.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text:
Dumaine, thy love is far from charity,
That in love’s grief desir’st society.
You may look pale, but I should blush, I know,
To be o’er-heard and taken napping so.

speaker: KING
text:
Come, sir, you blush! As his, your case is such.
You chide at him, offending twice as much.
You do not love Maria? Longaville
Did never sonnet for her sake compile,
Nor never lay his wreathèd arms athwart
His loving bosom to keep down his heart?
I have been closely shrouded in this bush
And marked you both, and for you both did blush.
I heard your guilty rhymes, observed your fashion,
Saw sighs reek from you, noted well your passion.
“Ay, me!” says one. “O Jove!” the other cries.
One, her hairs were gold, crystal the other’s eyes.
You would for paradise break faith and troth,
And Jove, for your love, would infringe an oath.
What will Berowne say when that he shall hear
Faith infringed, which such zeal did swear?
How will he scorn, how will he spend his wit!
How will he triumph, leap, and laugh at it!
For all the wealth that ever I did see,
I would not have him know so much by me.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Now step I forth to whip hypocrisy.
Ah, good my liege, I pray thee pardon me.
Good heart, what grace hast thou thus to reprove
These worms for loving, that art most in love?
Your eyes do make no coaches; in your tears
There is no certain princess that appears.
You’ll not be perjured, ’tis a hateful thing!
Tush, none but minstrels like of sonneting!
But are you not ashamed? Nay, are you not,
All three of you, to be thus much o’ershot?
You found his mote, the King your mote did see,
But I a beam do find in each of three.
O, what a scene of fool’ry have I seen,
Of sighs, of groans, of sorrow, and of teen!
O me, with what strict patience have I sat,
To see a king transformèd to a gnat!
To see great Hercules whipping a gig,
And profound Solomon to tune a jig,
And Nestor play at pushpin with the boys,
And critic Timon laugh at idle toys.
Where lies thy grief, O tell me, good Dumaine?
And gentle Longaville, where lies thy pain?
And where my liege’s? All about the breast!
A caudle, ho!

speaker: KING
text:
Too bitter is thy jest.
Are we betrayed thus to thy overview?

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Not you to me, but I betrayed by you.
I, that am honest, I, that hold it sin
To break the vow I am engagèd in.
I am betrayed by keeping company
With men like you, men of inconstancy.
When shall you see me write a thing in rhyme?
Or groan for Joan? or spend a minute’s time
In pruning me? When shall you hear that I
Will praise a hand, a foot, a face, an eye,
A gait, a state, a brow, a breast, a waist,
A leg, a limb—

speaker: KING
text:
Soft, whither away so fast?
A true man, or a thief, that gallops so?

speaker: BEROWNE
text: I post from love. Good lover, let me go.

speaker: JAQUENETTA
text: God bless the King.

speaker: KING
text: What present hast thou there?

speaker: COSTARD
text: Some certain treason.

speaker: KING
text: What makes treason here?

speaker: COSTARD
text: Nay, it makes nothing, sir.

speaker: KING
text:
If it mar nothing neither,
The treason and you go in peace away together.

speaker: JAQUENETTA
text:
I beseech your Grace, let this letter be read.
Our person misdoubts it. ’Twas treason, he said.

speaker: KING
text:
Berowne, read it over.
Where hadst thou it?

speaker: JAQUENETTA
text: Of Costard.

speaker: KING
text: Where hadst thou it?

speaker: COSTARD
text: Of Dun Adramadio, Dun Adramadio.

speaker: KING
text: How now, what is in you? Why dost thou tear it?

speaker: BEROWNE
text: A toy, my liege, a toy. Your Grace needs not fear it.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: It did move him to passion, and therefore let’s hear it.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: It is Berowne’s writing, and here is his name.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Ah, you whoreson loggerhead, you were born to do me shame.—
Guilty, my lord, guilty. I confess, I confess.

speaker: KING
text: What?

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
That you three fools lacked me fool to make up the mess.
He, he, and you—and you, my liege—and I
Are pickpurses in love, and we deserve to die.
O, dismiss this audience, and I shall tell you more.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: Now the number is even.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
True, true, we are four.
Will these turtles be gone?

speaker: KING
text: Hence, sirs. Away.

speaker: COSTARD
text: Walk aside the true folk, and let the traitors stay.

speaker: BEROWNE
KING
text: What, did these rent lines show some love of thine?

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Did they, quoth you? Who sees the heavenly Rosaline
That, like a rude and savage man of Ind
At the first op’ning of the gorgeous East,
Bows not his vassal head and, strucken blind,
Kisses the base ground with obedient breast?
What peremptory eagle-sighted eye
Dares look upon the heaven of her brow
That is not blinded by her majesty?

speaker: KING
text:
What zeal, what fury, hath inspired thee now?
My love, her mistress, is a gracious moon,
She an attending star scarce seen a light.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
My eyes are then no eyes, nor I Berowne.
O, but for my love, day would turn to night!
Of all complexions the culled sovereignty
Do meet as at a fair in her fair cheek.
Where several worthies make one dignity,
Where nothing wants that want itself doth seek.
Lend me the flourish of all gentle tongues—
Fie, painted rhetoric! O, she needs it not!
To things of sale a seller’s praise belongs.
She passes praise. Then praise too short doth blot.
A withered hermit, fivescore winters worn,
Might shake off fifty, looking in her eye.
Beauty doth varnish age, as if newborn,
And gives the crutch the cradle’s infancy.
O, ’tis the sun that maketh all things shine!

speaker: KING
text: By heaven, thy love is black as ebony.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Is ebony like her? O word divine!
A wife of such wood were felicity.
O, who can give an oath? Where is a book,
That I may swear beauty doth beauty lack
If that she learn not of her eye to look?
No face is fair that is not full so black.

speaker: KING
text:
O, paradox! Black is the badge of hell,
The hue of dungeons and the school of night,
And beauty’s crest becomes the heavens well.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Devils soonest tempt, resembling spirits of light.
O, if in black my lady’s brows be decked,
It mourns that painting and usurping hair
Should ravish doters with a false aspect:
And therefore is she born to make black fair.
Her favor turns the fashion of the days,
For native blood is counted painting now.
And therefore red, that would avoid dispraise,
Paints itself black to imitate her brow.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: To look like her are chimney-sweepers black.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: And since her time are colliers counted bright.

speaker: KING
text: And Ethiopes of their sweet complexion crack.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: Dark needs no candles now, for dark is light.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Your mistresses dare never come in rain,
For fear their colors should be washed away.

speaker: KING
text:
’Twere good yours did, for, sir, to tell you plain,
I’ll find a fairer face not washed today.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: I’ll prove her fair, or talk till doomsday here.

speaker: KING
text: No devil will fright thee then so much as she.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: I never knew man hold vile stuff so dear.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: Look, here’s thy love; my foot and her face see.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
O, if the streets were pavèd with thine eyes.
Her feet were much too dainty for such tread.

speaker: DUMAINE
text:
O vile! Then as she goes, what upward lies
The street should see as she walked overhead.

speaker: KING
text: But what of this? Are we not all in love?

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Nothing so sure, and thereby all forsworn.

speaker: KING
text:
Then leave this chat, and, good Berowne, now prove
Our loving lawful, and our faith not torn.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: Ay, marry, there, some flattery for this evil.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text:
O, some authority how to proceed,
Some tricks, some quillets, how to cheat the devil.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: Some salve for perjury.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
O, ’tis more than need.
Have at you, then, affection’s men-at-arms!
O, we have made a vow to study, lords,
And in that vow we have forsworn our books.
For when would you, my liege, or you, or you,
In leaden contemplation have found out
Such fiery numbers as the prompting eyes
Of beauty’s tutors have enriched you with?
Other slow arts entirely keep the brain
And therefore, finding barren practicers,
Scarce show a harvest of their heavy toil.
But love, first learnèd in a lady’s eyes,
Lives not alone immurèd in the brain,
But with the motion of all elements
Courses as swift as thought in every power,
And gives to every power a double power,
Above their functions and their offices.
It adds a precious seeing to the eye.
A lover’s eyes will gaze an eagle blind.
A lover’s ear will hear the lowest sound,
When the suspicious head of theft is stopped.
Love’s feeling is more soft and sensible
Than are the tender horns of cockled snails.
Love’s tongue proves dainty Bacchus gross in taste.
For valor, is not love a Hercules,
Still climbing trees in the Hesperides?
Subtle as Sphinx, as sweet and musical
As bright Apollo’s lute strung with his hair.
And when love speaks, the voice of all the gods
Make heaven drowsy with the harmony.
Never durst poet touch a pen to write
Until his ink were tempered with love’s sighs.
O, then his lines would ravish savage ears
And plant in tyrants mild humility.
From women’s eyes this doctrine I derive.
They sparkle still the right Promethean fire.
They are the books, the arts, the academes
That show, contain, and nourish all the world.
Else none at all in ought proves excellent.
Then fools you were these women to forswear,
Or, keeping what is sworn, you will prove fools.
For wisdom’s sake, a word that all men love,
Or for love’s sake, a word that loves all men,
Or for men’s sake, the authors of these women,
Or women’s sake, by whom we men are men,
Let us once lose our oaths to find ourselves,
Or else we lose ourselves to keep our oaths.
It is religion to be thus forsworn,
For charity itself fulfills the law,
And who can sever love from charity?

speaker: KING
text: Saint Cupid, then, and, soldiers, to the field!

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Advance your standards, and upon them, lords.
Pell-mell, down with them. But be first advised
In conflict that you get the sun of them.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text:
Now to plain dealing. Lay these glozes by.
Shall we resolve to woo these girls of France?

speaker: KING
text:
And win them, too. Therefore let us devise
Some entertainment for them in their tents.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
First, from the park let us conduct them thither.
Then homeward every man attach the hand
Of his fair mistress. In the afternoon
We will with some strange pastime solace them,
Such as the shortness of the time can shape;
For revels, dances, masques, and merry hours
Forerun fair love, strewing her way with flowers.

speaker: KING
text:
Away, away! No time shall be omitted
That will betime and may by us be fitted.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Allons! Allons! Sowed cockle reaped no corn,
And justice always whirls in equal measure.
Light wenches may prove plagues to men forsworn;
If so, our copper buys no better treasure.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text: Satis quid sufficit.

speaker: NATHANIEL
text:
I praise God for you, sir. Your reasons at
dinner have been sharp and sententious, pleasant
without scurrility, witty without affection, audacious
without impudency, learned without opinion,
and strange without heresy. I did converse this
quondam day with a companion of the King’s, who
is intituled, nominated, or called Don Adriano de
Armado.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Novi hominem tanquam te. His humor
is lofty, his discourse peremptory, his tongue filed,
his eye ambitious, his gait majestical, and his general
behavior vain, ridiculous, and thrasonical. He is
too picked, too spruce, too affected, too odd, as it
were, too peregrinate, as I may call it.

speaker: NATHANIEL
text: A most singular and choice epithet.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
He draweth out the thread of his verbosity
finer than the staple of his argument. I abhor
such fanatical phantasimes, such insociable and
point-devise companions, such rackers of orthography,
as to speak “dout,” fine, when he should
say “doubt”; “det” when he should pronounce
“debt”—d, e, b, t, not d, e, t. He clepeth a calf
“cauf,” half “hauf,” neighbor vocatur “nebor”;
neigh abbreviated ne. This is abhominable—which
he would call “abominable.” It insinuateth me of
insanie. Ne intelligis, domine? To make frantic,
lunatic.

speaker: NATHANIEL
text: Laus Deo, bone intelligo.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Bone? Bone for bene? Priscian a little
scratched; ’twill serve.

speaker: NATHANIEL
text: Videsne quis venit?

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text: Video, et gaudeo.

speaker: ARMADO
text: Chirrah.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text: Quare “chirrah,” not “sirrah”?

speaker: ARMADO
text: Men of peace, well encountered.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text: Most military sir, salutation.

speaker: BOY
text:
They have been at a great feast
of languages and stolen the scraps.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
O, they have lived long on the
almsbasket of words. I marvel thy master hath not
eaten thee for a word, for thou art not so long by the
head as honorificabilitudinitatibus. Thou art easier
swallowed than a flapdragon.

speaker: BOY
text: Peace, the peal begins.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Monsieur, are you not
lettered?

speaker: BOY
text:
Yes, yes, he teaches boys the hornbook.—What is
a, b spelled backward, with the horn on his head?

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text: Ba, pueritia, with a horn added.

speaker: BOY
text:
Ba, most silly sheep, with a horn.—You hear his
learning.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text: Quis, quis, thou consonant?

speaker: BOY
text:
The last of the five vowels, if you repeat them; or
the fifth, if I.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text: I will repeat them: a, e, i—

speaker: BOY
text: The sheep. The other two concludes it: o, u.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Now by the salt wave of the Mediterraneum,
a sweet touch, a quick venue of wit! Snip, snap,
quick and home. It rejoiceth my intellect. True
wit.

speaker: BOY
text:
Offered by a child to an old man—which is
wit-old.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text: What is the figure? What is the figure?

speaker: BOY
text: Horns.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Thou disputes like an infant. Go whip thy
gig.

speaker: BOY
text:
Lend me your horn to make one, and I will whip
about your infamy—unum cita—a gig of a cuckold’s
horn.

speaker: COSTARD
text:
An I had but one penny in the world, thou
shouldst have it to buy gingerbread! Hold, there is
the very remuneration I had of thy master, thou
halfpenny purse of wit, thou pigeon egg of discretion.
O, an the heavens were
so pleased that thou wert but my bastard, what a
joyful father wouldest thou make me! Go to, thou
hast it ad dunghill, at the fingers’ ends, as they say.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Oh, I smell false Latin! Dunghill for
unguem.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Arts-man, preambulate. We will be singuled
from the barbarous. Do you not educate youth at
the charge-house on the top of the mountain?

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text: Or mons, the hill.

speaker: ARMADO
text: At your sweet pleasure, for the mountain.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text: I do, sans question.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Sir, it is the King’s most sweet pleasure and
affection to congratulate the Princess at her pavilion
in the posteriors of this day, which the rude
multitude call the afternoon.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
“The posterior of the day,” most generous
sir, is liable, congruent, and measurable for
“the afternoon”; the word is well culled, chose,
sweet, and apt, I do assure you, sir, I do assure.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Sir, the King is a noble gentleman, and my
familiar, I do assure you, very good friend. For
what is inward between us, let it pass. I do beseech
thee, remember thy courtesy; I beseech thee apparel
thy head. And among other important and most
serious designs, and of great import indeed, too—
but let that pass; for I must tell thee, it will please his
Grace, by the world, sometimes to lean upon my
poor shoulder and with his royal finger thus dally
with my excrement, with my mustachio—but,
sweetheart, let that pass. By the world, I recount no
fable! Some certain special honors it pleaseth his
Greatness to impart to Armado, a soldier, a man of
travel, that hath seen the world—but let that pass.
The very all of all is—but sweetheart, I do implore
secrecy—that the King would have me present the
Princess, sweet chuck, with some delightful ostentation,
or show, or pageant, or antic, or firework.
Now, understanding that the curate and your sweet
self are good at such eruptions and sudden breaking
out of mirth, as it were, I have acquainted you
withal to the end to crave your assistance.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Sir, you shall present before her the Nine
Worthies.—Sir Nathaniel, as concerning some
entertainment of time, some show in the posterior
of this day, to be rendered by our assistance, the
King’s command, and this most gallant, illustrate,
and learned gentleman, before the Princess—I say,
none so fit as to present the Nine Worthies.

speaker: NATHANIEL
text:
Where will you find men worthy enough to
present them?

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Joshua, yourself; myself; and this gallant
gentleman, Judas Maccabaeus. This swain, because
of his great limb or joint, shall pass Pompey
the Great; the page, Hercules—

speaker: ARMADO
text:
Pardon, sir—error. He is not quantity
enough for that Worthy’s thumb; he is not so big as
the end of his club!

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Shall I have audience? He shall present
Hercules in minority. His enter and exit shall be
strangling a snake; and I will have an apology for
that purpose.

speaker: BOY
text:
An excellent device. So, if any of the audience
hiss, you may cry “Well done, Hercules, now thou
crushest the snake.” That is the way to make an
offense gracious, though few have the grace to do it.

speaker: ARMADO
text: For the rest of the Worthies?

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text: I will play three myself.

speaker: BOY
text: Thrice-worthy gentleman!

speaker: ARMADO
text: Shall I tell you a thing?

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text: We attend.

speaker: ARMADO
text:
We will have, if this fadge not, an antic. I
beseech you, follow.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Via, goodman Dull. Thou hast spoken no
word all this while.

speaker: DULL
text: Nor understood none neither, sir.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text: Allons! We will employ thee.

speaker: DULL
text:
I’ll make one in a dance, or so; or I will play on
the tabor to the Worthies and let them dance the
hay.

speaker: HOLOFERNES
text:
Most dull, honest Dull. To our sport!
Away.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Sweethearts, we shall be rich ere we depart,
If fairings come thus plentifully in.
A lady walled about with diamonds!
Look you what I have from the loving king.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Madam, came nothing else along with that?

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Nothing but this? Yes, as much love in rhyme
As would be crammed up in a sheet of paper
Writ o’ both sides the leaf, margent and all,
That he was fain to seal on Cupid’s name.

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
That was the way to make his godhead wax,
For he hath been five thousand year a boy.

speaker: KATHERINE
text: Ay, and a shrewd unhappy gallows, too.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: You’ll ne’er be friends with him. He killed your sister.

speaker: KATHERINE
text:
He made her melancholy, sad, and heavy,
And so she died. Had she been light like you,
Of such a merry, nimble, stirring spirit,
She might ha’ been a grandam ere she died.
And so may you, for a light heart lives long.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: What’s your dark meaning, mouse, of this light word?

speaker: KATHERINE
text: A light condition in a beauty dark.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: We need more light to find your meaning out.

speaker: KATHERINE
text:
You’ll mar the light by taking it in snuff;
Therefore I’ll darkly end the argument.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Look what you do, you do it still i’ th’ dark.

speaker: KATHERINE
text: So do not you, for you are a light wench.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Indeed, I weigh not you, and therefore light.

speaker: KATHERINE
text: You weigh me not? O, that’s you care not for me.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Great reason: for past care is still past cure.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Well bandied both; a set of wit well played.
But, Rosaline, you have a favor too.
Who sent it? And what is it?

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
I would you knew.
An if my face were but as fair as yours,
My favor were as great. Be witness this.
Nay, I have verses too, I thank Berowne;
The numbers true; and were the numb’ring too,
I were the fairest goddess on the ground.
I am compared to twenty thousand fairs.
O, he hath drawn my picture in his letter.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Anything like?

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Much in the letters, nothing in the praise.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Beauteous as ink: a good conclusion.

speaker: KATHERINE
text: Fair as a text B in a copybook.

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
Ware pencils, ho! Let me not die your debtor,
My red dominical, my golden letter.
O, that your face were not so full of O’s!

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
A pox of that jest! And I beshrew all shrows.
But, Katherine, what was sent to you
From fair Dumaine?

speaker: KATHERINE
text: Madam, this glove.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Did he not send you twain?

speaker: KATHERINE
text:
Yes, madam, and moreover,
Some thousand verses of a faithful lover,
A huge translation of hypocrisy,
Vilely compiled, profound simplicity.

speaker: MARIA
text:
This, and these pearls, to me sent Longaville.
The letter is too long by half a mile.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
I think no less. Dost thou not wish in heart
The chain were longer and the letter short?

speaker: MARIA
text: Ay, or I would these hands might never part.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: We are wise girls to mock our lovers so.

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
They are worse fools to purchase mocking so.
That same Berowne I’ll torture ere I go.
O, that I knew he were but in by th’ week,
How I would make him fawn, and beg, and seek,
And wait the season, and observe the times,
And spend his prodigal wits in bootless rhymes,
And shape his service wholly to my hests,
And make him proud to make me proud that jests!
So pair-taunt-like would I o’ersway his state,
That he should be my fool, and I his fate.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
None are so surely caught, when they are catched,
As wit turned fool. Folly in wisdom hatched
Hath wisdom’s warrant and the help of school,
And wit’s own grace to grace a learnèd fool.

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
The blood of youth burns not with such excess
As gravity’s revolt to wantonness.

speaker: MARIA
text:
Folly in fools bears not so strong a note
As fool’ry in the wise, when wit doth dote,
Since all the power thereof it doth apply
To prove, by wit, worth in simplicity.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Here comes Boyet, and mirth is in his face.

speaker: BOYET
text: O, I am stabbed with laughter. Where’s her Grace?

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Thy news, Boyet?

speaker: BOYET
text:
Prepare, madam, prepare.
Arm, wenches, arm. Encounters mounted are
Against your peace. Love doth approach, disguised,
Armèd in arguments. You’ll be surprised.
Muster your wits, stand in your own defense,
Or hide your heads like cowards, and fly hence.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Saint Denis to Saint Cupid! What are they
That charge their breath against us? Say, scout, say.

speaker: BOYET
text:
Under the cool shade of a sycamore,
I thought to close mine eyes some half an hour.
When, lo, to interrupt my purposed rest,
Toward that shade I might behold addressed
The King and his companions. Warily
I stole into a neighbor thicket by,
And overheard what you shall overhear:
That, by and by, disguised, they will be here.
Their herald is a pretty knavish page
That well by heart hath conned his embassage.
Action and accent did they teach him there:
“Thus must thou speak,” and “thus thy body bear.”
And ever and anon they made a doubt
Presence majestical would put him out;
“For,” quoth the King, “an angel shalt thou see;
Yet fear not thou, but speak audaciously.”
The boy replied “An angel is not evil.
I should have feared her had she been a devil.”
With that, all laughed and clapped him on the shoulder,
Making the bold wag by their praises bolder.
One rubbed his elbow thus, and fleered, and swore
A better speech was never spoke before.
Another with his finger and his thumb,
Cried “Via! We will do ’t, come what will come.”
The third he capered and cried “All goes well!”
The fourth turned on the toe, and down he fell.
With that, they all did tumble on the ground
With such a zealous laughter so profound
That in this spleen ridiculous appears,
To check their folly, passion’s solemn tears.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: But what, but what? Come they to visit us?

speaker: BOYET
text:
They do, they do; and are appareled thus,
Like Muscovites, or Russians, as I guess.
Their purpose is to parley, to court, and dance,
And every one his love-feat will advance
Unto his several mistress—which they’ll know
By favors several which they did bestow.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
And will they so? The gallants shall be tasked,
For, ladies, we will every one be masked,
And not a man of them shall have the grace,
Despite of suit, to see a lady’s face.
Hold, Rosaline, this favor thou shalt wear,
And then the King will court thee for his dear.
Hold, take thou this, my sweet, and give me thine.
So shall Berowne take me for Rosaline.
And change you favors too. So shall your loves
Woo contrary, deceived by these removes.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Come on, then, wear the favors most in sight.

speaker: KATHERINE
text: But in this changing, what is your intent?

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
The effect of my intent is to cross theirs.
They do it but in mockery merriment,
And mock for mock is only my intent.
Their several counsels they unbosom shall
To loves mistook, and so be mocked withal
Upon the next occasion that we meet,
With visages displayed, to talk and greet.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: But shall we dance, if they desire us to ’t?

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
No, to the death we will not move a foot,
Nor to their penned speech render we no grace,
But while ’tis spoke each turn away her face.

speaker: BOYET
text:
Why, that contempt will kill the speaker’s heart,
And quite divorce his memory from his part.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Therefore I do it, and I make no doubt
The rest will ne’er come in if he be out.
There’s no such sport as sport by sport o’erthrown,
To make theirs ours and ours none but our own.
So shall we stay, mocking intended game,
And they, well mocked, depart away with shame.

speaker: BOYET
text: The trumpet sounds. Be masked; the maskers come.

speaker: BOY
text: All hail, the richest beauties on the Earth!

speaker: BOYET
text: Beauties no richer than rich taffeta.

speaker: BOY
text:
A holy parcel of the fairest dames
That ever turned their—backs—to mortal views.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Their eyes, villain, their eyes!

speaker: BOY
text:
That ever turned their eyes to mortal views.
Out—

speaker: BOYET
text: True; out indeed.

speaker: BOY
text:
Out of your favors, heavenly spirits, vouchsafe
Not to behold—

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Once to behold, rogue!

speaker: BOY
text:
Once to behold with your sun-beamèd eyes—
With your sun-beamèd eyes—

speaker: BOYET
text:
They will not answer to that epithet.
You were best call it “daughter-beamèd eyes.”

speaker: BOY
text: They do not mark me, and that brings me out.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Is this your perfectness? Begone, you rogue!

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
What would these strangers? Know their minds, Boyet.
If they do speak our language, ’tis our will
That some plain man recount their purposes.
Know what they would.

speaker: BOYET
text: What would you with the Princess?

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Nothing but peace and gentle visitation.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: What would they, say they?

speaker: BOYET
text: Nothing but peace and gentle visitation.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Why, that they have, and bid them so be gone.

speaker: BOYET
text: She says you have it, and you may be gone.

speaker: KING
text:
Say to her we have measured many miles
To tread a measure with her on this grass.

speaker: BOYET
text:
They say that they have measured many a mile
To tread a measure with you on this grass.

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
It is not so. Ask them how many inches
Is in one mile. If they have measured many,
The measure then of one is eas’ly told.

speaker: BOYET
text:
If to come hither you have measured miles,
And many miles, the Princess bids you tell
How many inches doth fill up one mile.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Tell her we measure them by weary steps.

speaker: BOYET
text: She hears herself.

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
How many weary steps
Of many weary miles you have o’ergone
Are numbered in the travel of one mile?

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
We number nothing that we spend for you.
Our duty is so rich, so infinite,
That we may do it still without account.
Vouchsafe to show the sunshine of your face
That we, like savages, may worship it.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: My face is but a moon, and clouded too.

speaker: KING
text:
Blessèd are clouds, to do as such clouds do!
Vouchsafe, bright moon, and these thy stars, to shine,
Those clouds removed, upon our watery eyne.

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
O vain petitioner, beg a greater matter!
Thou now requests but moonshine in the water.

speaker: KING
text:
Then in our measure do but vouchsafe one change.
Thou bidd’st me beg; this begging is not strange.

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
Play music, then. Nay, you must do it soon.
Not yet? No dance! Thus change I like the moon.

speaker: KING
text: Will you not dance? How come you thus estranged?

speaker: ROSALINE
text: You took the moon at full, but now she’s changed.

speaker: KING
text:
Yet still she is the moon, and I the man.
The music plays. Vouchsafe some motion to it.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Our ears vouchsafe it.

speaker: KING
text: But your legs should do it.

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
Since you are strangers and come here by chance,
We’ll not be nice. Take hands. We will not dance.

speaker: KING
text: Why take we hands then?

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
Only to part friends.—
Curtsy, sweethearts—and so the measure ends.

speaker: KING
text: More measure of this measure! Be not nice.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: We can afford no more at such a price.

speaker: KING
text: Prize you yourselves. What buys your company?

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Your absence only.

speaker: KING
text: That can never be.

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
Then cannot we be bought. And so adieu—
Twice to your visor, and half once to you.

speaker: KING
text: If you deny to dance, let’s hold more chat.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: In private, then.

speaker: KING
text: I am best pleased with that.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: White-handed mistress, one sweet word with thee.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Honey, and milk, and sugar—there is three.

speaker: BEROWNE
text:
Nay then, two treys, an if you grow so nice,
Metheglin, wort, and malmsey. Well run, dice!
There’s half a dozen sweets.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Seventh sweet, adieu.
Since you can cog, I’ll play no more with you.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: One word in secret.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Let it not be sweet.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Thou grievest my gall.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Gall! Bitter.

speaker: BEROWNE
text: Therefore meet.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: Will you vouchsafe with me to change a word?

speaker: MARIA
text: Name it.

speaker: DUMAINE
text: Fair lady—

speaker: MARIA
text:
Say you so? Fair lord!
Take that for your “fair lady.”

speaker: DUMAINE
text:
Please it you
As much in private, and I’ll bid adieu.

speaker: KATHERINE
text: What, was your vizard made without a tongue?

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: I know the reason, lady, why you ask.

speaker: KATHERINE
text: O, for your reason! Quickly, sir, I long.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text:
You have a double tongue within your mask,
And would afford my speechless vizard half.

speaker: KATHERINE
text: Veal, quoth the Dutchman. Is not veal a calf?

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: A calf, fair lady?

speaker: KATHERINE
text: No, a fair Lord Calf.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: Let’s part the word.

speaker: KATHERINE
text:
No, I’ll not be your half.
Take all and wean it. It may prove an ox.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text:
Look how you butt yourself in these sharp mocks.
Will you give horns, chaste lady? Do not so.

speaker: KATHERINE
text: Then die a calf before your horns do grow.

speaker: LONGAVILLE
text: One word in private with you ere I die.

speaker: KATHERINE
text: Bleat softly, then. The butcher hears you cry.

speaker: BOYET
text:
The tongues of mocking wenches are as keen
As is the razor’s edge invisible,
Cutting a smaller hair than may be seen;
Above the sense of sense, so sensible
Seemeth their conference. Their conceits have wings
Fleeter than arrows, bullets, wind, thought, swifter things.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Not one word more, my maids. Break off, break off!

speaker: BEROWNE
text: By heaven, all dry-beaten with pure scoff!

speaker: KING
text: Farewell, mad wenches. You have simple wits.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
Twenty adieus, my frozen Muskovits.—
Are these the breed of wits so wondered at?

speaker: BOYET
text: Tapers they are, with your sweet breaths puffed out.

speaker: ROSALINE
text: Well-liking wits they have; gross, gross; fat, fat.

speaker: PRINCESS
text:
O poverty in wit, kingly-poor flout!
Will they not, think you, hang themselves tonight?
Or ever but in vizards show their faces?
This pert Berowne was out of count’nance quite.

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
They were all in lamentable cases.
The King was weeping ripe for a good word.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Berowne did swear himself out of all suit.

speaker: MARIA
text:
Dumaine was at my service, and his sword.
“No point,” quoth I. My servant straight was mute.

speaker: KATHERINE
text:
Lord Longaville said I came o’er his heart.
And trow you what he called me?

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Qualm, perhaps.

speaker: KATHERINE
text: Yes, in good faith.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Go, sickness as thou art!

speaker: ROSALINE
text:
Well, better wits have worn plain statute-caps.
But will you hear? The King is my love sworn.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: And quick Berowne hath plighted faith to me.

speaker: KATHERINE
text: And Longaville was for my service born.

speaker: MARIA
text: Dumaine is mine as sure as bark on tree.

speaker: BOYET
text:
Madam, and pretty mistresses, give ear.
Immediately they will again be here
In their own shapes, for it can never be
They will digest this harsh indignity.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: Will they return?

speaker: BOYET
text:
They will, they will, God knows,
And leap for joy, though they are lame with blows.
Therefore change favors, and when they repair,
Blow like sweet roses in this summer air.

speaker: PRINCESS
text: How “blow”? How “blow”? Speak to be understood.

speaker: BOYET
text:
Fair ladies masked are roses in their bud.
Dismasked, their damask sweet commixture shown,
