Set on thy wife to observe. Leave me, Iago.

speaker: IAGO
text: My lord, I take my leave.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Why did I marry? This honest creature doubtless
Sees and knows more, much more, than he unfolds.

speaker: IAGO
text:
My lord, I would I might entreat your Honor
To scan this thing no farther. Leave it to time.
Although ’tis fit that Cassio have his place—
For sure he fills it up with great ability—
Yet, if you please to hold him off awhile,
You shall by that perceive him and his means.
Note if your lady strain his entertainment
With any strong or vehement importunity.
Much will be seen in that. In the meantime,
Let me be thought too busy in my fears—
As worthy cause I have to fear I am—
And hold her free, I do beseech your Honor.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Fear not my government.

speaker: IAGO
text: I once more take my leave.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
This fellow’s of exceeding honesty,
And knows all qualities with a learnèd spirit
Of human dealings. If I do prove her haggard,
Though that her jesses were my dear heartstrings,
I’d whistle her off and let her down the wind
To prey at fortune. Haply, for I am black
And have not those soft parts of conversation
That chamberers have, or for I am declined
Into the vale of years—yet that’s not much—
She’s gone, I am abused, and my relief
Must be to loathe her. O curse of marriage,
That we can call these delicate creatures ours
And not their appetites! I had rather be a toad
And live upon the vapor of a dungeon
Than keep a corner in the thing I love
For others’ uses. Yet ’tis the plague of great ones;
Prerogatived are they less than the base.
’Tis destiny unshunnable, like death.
Even then this forkèd plague is fated to us
When we do quicken. Look where she comes.
If she be false, heaven mocks itself!
I’ll not believe ’t.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
How now, my dear Othello?
Your dinner, and the generous islanders
By you invited, do attend your presence.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: I am to blame.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Why do you speak so faintly? Are you not well?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: I have a pain upon my forehead, here.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
Faith, that’s with watching. ’Twill away again.
Let me but bind it hard; within this hour
It will be well.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Your napkin is too little.
Let it alone.
Come, I’ll go in with you.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I am very sorry that you are not well.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
I am glad I have found this napkin.
This was her first remembrance from the Moor.
My wayward husband hath a hundred times
Wooed me to steal it. But she so loves the token
(For he conjured her she should ever keep it)
That she reserves it evermore about her
To kiss and talk to. I’ll have the work ta’en out
And give ’t Iago. What he will do with it
Heaven knows, not I.
I nothing but to please his fantasy.

speaker: IAGO
text: How now? What do you here alone?

speaker: EMILIA
text: Do not you chide. I have a thing for you.

speaker: IAGO
text: You have a thing for me? It is a common thing—

speaker: EMILIA
text: Ha?

speaker: IAGO
text: To have a foolish wife.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
O, is that all? What will you give me now
For that same handkerchief?

speaker: IAGO
text: What handkerchief?

speaker: EMILIA
text:
What handkerchief?
Why, that the Moor first gave to Desdemona,
That which so often you did bid me steal.

speaker: IAGO
text: Hast stol’n it from her?

speaker: EMILIA
text:
No, faith, she let it drop by negligence,
And to th’ advantage I, being here, took ’t up.
Look, here ’tis.

speaker: IAGO
text: A good wench! Give it me.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
What will you do with ’t, that you have been so earnest
To have me filch it?

speaker: IAGO
text: Why, what is that to you?

speaker: EMILIA
text:
If it be not for some purpose of import,
Give ’t me again. Poor lady, she’ll run mad
When she shall lack it.

speaker: IAGO
text:
Be not acknown on ’t.
I have use for it. Go, leave me.
I will in Cassio’s lodging lose this napkin
And let him find it. Trifles light as air
Are to the jealous confirmations strong
As proofs of holy writ. This may do something.
The Moor already changes with my poison;
Dangerous conceits are in their natures poisons,
Which at the first are scarce found to distaste,
But with a little act upon the blood
Burn like the mines of sulfur.
I did say so.
Look where he comes. Not poppy nor mandragora
Nor all the drowsy syrups of the world
Shall ever medicine thee to that sweet sleep
Which thou owedst yesterday.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Ha, ha, false to me?

speaker: IAGO
text: Why, how now, general? No more of that!

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Avaunt! Begone! Thou hast set me on the rack.
I swear ’tis better to be much abused
Than but to know ’t a little.

speaker: IAGO
text: How now, my lord?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
What sense had I of her stol’n hours of lust?
I saw ’t not, thought it not; it harmed not me.
I slept the next night well, fed well, was free and merry.
I found not Cassio’s kisses on her lips.
He that is robbed, not wanting what is stol’n,
Let him not know ’t, and he’s not robbed at all.

speaker: IAGO
text: I am sorry to hear this.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
I had been happy if the general camp,
Pioners and all, had tasted her sweet body,
So I had nothing known. O, now, forever
Farewell the tranquil mind! Farewell content!
Farewell the plumèd troops and the big wars
That makes ambition virtue! O, farewell!
Farewell the neighing steed and the shrill trump,
The spirit-stirring drum, th’ ear-piercing fife,
The royal banner, and all quality,
Pride, pomp, and circumstance of glorious war!
And O you mortal engines, whose rude throats
Th’ immortal Jove’s dread clamors counterfeit,
Farewell! Othello’s occupation’s gone!

speaker: IAGO
text: Is ’t possible, my lord?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Villain, be sure thou prove my love a whore!
Be sure of it. Give me the ocular proof,
Or, by the worth of mine eternal soul,
Thou hadst been better have been born a dog
Than answer my waked wrath.

speaker: IAGO
text: Is ’t come to this?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Make me to see ’t, or at the least so prove it
That the probation bear no hinge nor loop
To hang a doubt on, or woe upon thy life!

speaker: IAGO
text: My noble lord—

speaker: OTHELLO
IAGO
text:
O grace! O heaven forgive me!
Are you a man? Have you a soul or sense?
God b’ wi’ you. Take mine office.—O wretched fool,
That liv’st to make thine honesty a vice!—
O monstrous world! Take note, take note, O world:
To be direct and honest is not safe.—
I thank you for this profit, and from hence
I’ll love no friend, sith love breeds such offense.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Nay, stay. Thou shouldst be honest.

speaker: IAGO
text:
I should be wise; for honesty’s a fool
And loses that it works for.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
By the world,
I think my wife be honest and think she is not.
I think that thou art just and think thou art not.
I’ll have some proof! Her name, that was as fresh
As Dian’s visage, is now begrimed and black
As mine own face. If there be cords, or knives,
Poison, or fire, or suffocating streams,
I’ll not endure it. Would I were satisfied!

speaker: IAGO
text:
I see you are eaten up with passion.
I do repent me that I put it to you.
You would be satisfied?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Would? Nay, and I will.

speaker: IAGO
text:
And may; but how? How satisfied, my lord?
Would you, the supervisor, grossly gape on,
Behold her topped?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Death and damnation! O!

speaker: IAGO
text:
It were a tedious difficulty, I think,
To bring them to that prospect. Damn them then
If ever mortal eyes do see them bolster
More than their own! What then? How then?
What shall I say? Where’s satisfaction?
It is impossible you should see this,
Were they as prime as goats, as hot as monkeys,
As salt as wolves in pride, and fools as gross
As ignorance made drunk. But yet I say,
If imputation and strong circumstances
Which lead directly to the door of truth
Will give you satisfaction, you might have ’t.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Give me a living reason she’s disloyal.

speaker: IAGO
text:
I do not like the office,
But sith I am entered in this cause so far,
Pricked to ’t by foolish honesty and love,
I will go on. I lay with Cassio lately,
And being troubled with a raging tooth
I could not sleep. There are a kind of men
So loose of soul that in their sleeps will mutter
Their affairs. One of this kind is Cassio.
In sleep I heard him say “Sweet Desdemona,
Let us be wary, let us hide our loves.”
And then, sir, would he gripe and wring my hand,
Cry “O sweet creature!” then kiss me hard,
As if he plucked up kisses by the roots
That grew upon my lips; then laid his leg
O’er my thigh, and sighed, and kissed, and then
Cried “Cursèd fate that gave thee to the Moor!”

speaker: OTHELLO
text: O monstrous! Monstrous!

speaker: IAGO
text: Nay, this was but his dream.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
But this denoted a foregone conclusion.
’Tis a shrewd doubt, though it be but a dream.

speaker: IAGO
text:
And this may help to thicken other proofs
That do demonstrate thinly.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: I’ll tear her all to pieces.

speaker: IAGO
text:
Nay, but be wise. Yet we see nothing done.
She may be honest yet. Tell me but this:
Have you not sometimes seen a handkerchief
Spotted with strawberries in your wife’s hand?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: I gave her such a one. ’Twas my first gift.

speaker: IAGO
text:
I know not that; but such a handkerchief—
I am sure it was your wife’s—did I today
See Cassio wipe his beard with.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: If it be that—

speaker: IAGO
text:
If it be that, or any that was hers,
It speaks against her with the other proofs.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
O, that the slave had forty thousand lives!
One is too poor, too weak for my revenge.
Now do I see ’tis true. Look here, Iago,
All my fond love thus do I blow to heaven.
’Tis gone.
Arise, black vengeance, from the hollow hell!
Yield up, O love, thy crown and hearted throne
To tyrannous hate! Swell, bosom, with thy fraught,
For ’tis of aspics’ tongues!

speaker: IAGO
text: Yet be content.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: O, blood, blood, blood!

speaker: IAGO
text: Patience, I say. Your mind perhaps may change.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Never, Iago. Like to the Pontic Sea,
Whose icy current and compulsive course
Ne’er feels retiring ebb, but keeps due on
To the Propontic and the Hellespont,
Even so my bloody thoughts, with violent pace
Shall ne’er look back, ne’er ebb to humble love,
Till that a capable and wide revenge
Swallow them up. Now by yond marble heaven,
In the due reverence of a sacred vow,
I here engage my words.

speaker: IAGO
text:
Do not rise yet.
Witness, you ever-burning lights above,
You elements that clip us round about,
Witness that here Iago doth give up
The execution of his wit, hands, heart
To wronged Othello’s service! Let him command,
And to obey shall be in me remorse,
What bloody business ever.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
I greet thy love
Not with vain thanks but with acceptance bounteous,
And will upon the instant put thee to ’t.
Within these three days let me hear thee say
That Cassio’s not alive.

speaker: IAGO
text:
My friend is dead.
’Tis done at your request. But let her live.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Damn her, lewd minx! O, damn her, damn her!
Come, go with me apart. I will withdraw
To furnish me with some swift means of death
For the fair devil. Now art thou my lieutenant.

speaker: IAGO
text: I am your own forever.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
Do you know, sirrah, where Lieutenant
Cassio lies?

speaker: CLOWN
text: I dare not say he lies anywhere.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Why, man?

speaker: CLOWN
text:
He’s a soldier, and for me to say a soldier lies,
’tis stabbing.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Go to! Where lodges he?

speaker: CLOWN
text:
To tell you where he lodges is to tell you
where I lie.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Can anything be made of this?

speaker: CLOWN
text:
I know not where he lodges; and for me to
devise a lodging and say he lies here, or he lies
there, were to lie in mine own throat.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
Can you inquire him out, and be edified
by report?

speaker: CLOWN
text:
I will catechize the world for him—that is,
make questions, and by them answer.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
Seek him, bid him come hither. Tell him I
have moved my lord on his behalf and hope all will
be well.

speaker: CLOWN
text:
To do this is within the compass of man’s wit,
and therefore I will attempt the doing it.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Where should I lose that handkerchief, Emilia?

speaker: EMILIA
text: I know not, madam.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
Believe me, I had rather have lost my purse
Full of crusadoes. And but my noble Moor
Is true of mind and made of no such baseness
As jealous creatures are, it were enough
To put him to ill thinking.

speaker: EMILIA
text: Is he not jealous?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
Who, he? I think the sun where he was born
Drew all such humors from him.

speaker: EMILIA
text: Look where he comes.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
I will not leave him now till Cassio
Be called to him.—How is ’t with you, my lord?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Well, my good lady. O, hardness to dissemble!—
How do you, Desdemona?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Well, my good lord.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Give me your hand. This hand is moist, my lady.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: It yet has felt no age nor known no sorrow.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
This argues fruitfulness and liberal heart.
Hot, hot, and moist. This hand of yours requires
A sequester from liberty, fasting and prayer,
Much castigation, exercise devout;
For here’s a young and sweating devil here
That commonly rebels. ’Tis a good hand,
A frank one.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
You may indeed say so,
For ’twas that hand that gave away my heart.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
A liberal hand! The hearts of old gave hands,
But our new heraldry is hands, not hearts.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I cannot speak of this. Come now, your promise.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: What promise, chuck?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I have sent to bid Cassio come speak with you.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
I have a salt and sorry rheum offends me.
Lend me thy handkerchief.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Here, my lord.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: That which I gave you.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I have it not about me.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Not?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: No, faith, my lord.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
That’s a fault. That handkerchief
Did an Egyptian to my mother give.
She was a charmer, and could almost read
The thoughts of people. She told her, while she kept it,
’Twould make her amiable and subdue my father
Entirely to her love. But if she lost it,
Or made a gift of it, my father’s eye
Should hold her loathèd, and his spirits should hunt
After new fancies. She, dying, gave it me,
And bid me, when my fate would have me wived,
To give it her. I did so; and take heed on ’t,
Make it a darling like your precious eye.
To lose ’t or give ’t away were such perdition
As nothing else could match.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Is ’t possible?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
’Tis true. There’s magic in the web of it.
A sybil that had numbered in the world
The sun to course two hundred compasses,
In her prophetic fury sewed the work.
The worms were hallowed that did breed the silk,
And it was dyed in mummy, which the skillful
Conserved of maidens’ hearts.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I’ faith, is ’t true?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Most veritable. Therefore, look to ’t well.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Then would to God that I had never seen ’t!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Ha? Wherefore?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Why do you speak so startingly and rash?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Is ’t lost? Is ’t gone? Speak, is ’t out o’ th’ way?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Heaven bless us!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Say you?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: It is not lost, but what an if it were?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: How?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I say it is not lost.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Fetch ’t. Let me see ’t!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
Why, so I can. But I will not now.
This is a trick to put me from my suit.
Pray you, let Cassio be received again.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Fetch me the handkerchief! My mind misgives.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
Come, come.
You’ll never meet a more sufficient man.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: The handkerchief!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I pray, talk me of Cassio.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: The handkerchief!

speaker: DESDEMONA
OTHELLO
text: The handkerchief!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I’ faith, you are to blame.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Zounds!

speaker: EMILIA
text: Is not this man jealous?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
I ne’er saw this before.
Sure, there’s some wonder in this handkerchief!
I am most unhappy in the loss of it.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
’Tis not a year or two shows us a man.
They are all but stomachs, and we all but food;
They eat us hungerly, and when they are full
They belch us.
Look you—Cassio and my husband.

speaker: IAGO
text:
There is no other way; ’tis she must do ’t,
And, lo, the happiness! Go and importune her.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: How now, good Cassio, what’s the news with you?

speaker: CASSIO
text:
Madam, my former suit. I do beseech you
That by your virtuous means I may again
Exist, and be a member of his love
Whom I with all the office of my heart
Entirely honor. I would not be delayed.
If my offense be of such mortal kind
That nor my service past nor present sorrows
Nor purposed merit in futurity
Can ransom me into his love again,
But to know so must be my benefit.
So shall I clothe me in a forced content,
And shut myself up in some other course
To fortune’s alms.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
Alas, thrice-gentle Cassio,
My advocation is not now in tune.
My lord is not my lord; nor should I know him
Were he in favor as in humor altered.
So help me every spirit sanctified
As I have spoken for you all my best,
And stood within the blank of his displeasure
For my free speech! You must awhile be patient.
What I can do I will; and more I will
Than for myself I dare. Let that suffice you.

speaker: IAGO
text: Is my lord angry?

speaker: EMILIA
text:
He went hence but now,
And certainly in strange unquietness.

speaker: IAGO
text:
Can he be angry? I have seen the cannon
When it hath blown his ranks into the air
And, like the devil, from his very arm
Puffed his own brother—and is he angry?
Something of moment then. I will go meet him.
There’s matter in ’t indeed if he be angry.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
I prithee do so.
Something, sure, of state,
Either from Venice, or some unhatched practice
Made demonstrable here in Cyprus to him,
Hath puddled his clear spirit; and in such cases
Men’s natures wrangle with inferior things,
Though great ones are their object. ’Tis even so.
For let our finger ache, and it endues
Our other healthful members even to a sense
Of pain. Nay, we must think men are not gods,
Nor of them look for such observancy
As fits the bridal. Beshrew me much, Emilia,
I was—unhandsome warrior as I am!—
Arraigning his unkindness with my soul.
But now I find I had suborned the witness,
And he’s indicted falsely.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
Pray heaven it be
State matters, as you think, and no conception
Nor no jealous toy concerning you.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Alas the day, I never gave him cause!

speaker: EMILIA
text:
But jealous souls will not be answered so.
They are not ever jealous for the cause,
But jealous for they’re jealous. It is a monster
Begot upon itself, born on itself.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Heaven keep that monster from Othello’s mind!

speaker: EMILIA
text: Lady, amen.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
I will go seek him.—Cassio, walk hereabout.
If I do find him fit, I’ll move your suit
And seek to effect it to my uttermost.

speaker: CASSIO
text: I humbly thank your Ladyship.

speaker: BIANCA
text: ’Save you, friend Cassio!

speaker: CASSIO
text:
What make you from home?
How is ’t with you, my most fair Bianca?
I’ faith, sweet love, I was coming to your house.

speaker: BIANCA
text:
And I was going to your lodging, Cassio.
What, keep a week away? Seven days and nights,
Eightscore eight hours, and lovers’ absent hours
More tedious than the dial eightscore times?
O weary reck’ning!

speaker: CASSIO
text:
Pardon me, Bianca.
I have this while with leaden thoughts been pressed,
But I shall in a more continuate time
Strike off this score of absence. Sweet Bianca,
Take me this work out.

speaker: BIANCA
text:
O, Cassio, whence came this?
This is some token from a newer friend.
To the felt absence now I feel a cause.
Is ’t come to this? Well, well.

speaker: CASSIO
text:
Go to, woman!
Throw your vile guesses in the devil’s teeth,
From whence you have them. You are jealous now
That this is from some mistress, some remembrance.
No, by my faith, Bianca.

speaker: BIANCA
text: Why, whose is it?

speaker: CASSIO
text:
I know not neither. I found it in my chamber.
I like the work well. Ere it be demanded,
As like enough it will, I would have it copied.
Take it, and do ’t, and leave me for this time.

speaker: BIANCA
text: Leave you? Wherefore?

speaker: CASSIO
text:
I do attend here on the General,
And think it no addition, nor my wish,
To have him see me womaned.

speaker: BIANCA
text: Why, I pray you?

speaker: CASSIO
text: Not that I love you not.

speaker: BIANCA
text:
But that you do not love me!
I pray you bring me on the way a little,
And say if I shall see you soon at night.

speaker: CASSIO
text:
’Tis but a little way that I can bring you,
For I attend here. But I’ll see you soon.

speaker: BIANCA
text: ’Tis very good. I must be circumstanced.

speaker: IAGO
text: Will you think so?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Think so, Iago?

speaker: IAGO
text:
What,
To kiss in private?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: An unauthorized kiss!

speaker: IAGO
text:
Or to be naked with her friend in bed
An hour or more, not meaning any harm?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Naked in bed, Iago, and not mean harm?
It is hypocrisy against the devil!
They that mean virtuously, and yet do so,
The devil their virtue tempts, and they tempt heaven.

speaker: IAGO
text:
If they do nothing, ’tis a venial slip.
But if I give my wife a handkerchief—

speaker: OTHELLO
text: What then?

speaker: IAGO
text:
Why then, ’tis hers, my lord, and being hers,
She may, I think, bestow ’t on any man.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
She is protectress of her honor, too.
May she give that?

speaker: IAGO
OTHELLO
text:
By heaven, I would most gladly have forgot it.
Thou saidst—O, it comes o’er my memory
As doth the raven o’er the infectious house,
Boding to all—he had my handkerchief.

speaker: IAGO
text: Ay, what of that?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: That’s not so good now.

speaker: IAGO
text:
What
If I had said I had seen him do you wrong?
Or heard him say (as knaves be such abroad,
Who having, by their own importunate suit
Or voluntary dotage of some mistress,
Convincèd or supplied them, cannot choose
But they must blab)—

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Hath he said anything?

speaker: IAGO
text:
He hath, my lord, but be you well assured,
No more than he’ll unswear.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: What hath he said?

speaker: IAGO
text: Faith, that he did—I know not what he did.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: What? What?

speaker: IAGO
text: Lie—

speaker: OTHELLO
text: With her?

speaker: IAGO
text: With her—on her—what you will.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Lie with her? Lie on her? We say “lie on her”
when they belie her. Lie with her—Zounds, that’s
fulsome! Handkerchief—confessions—handkerchief.
To confess and be hanged for his labor.
First to be hanged and then to confess—I tremble
at it. Nature would not invest herself in such shadowing
passion without some instruction. It is not
words that shakes me thus. Pish! Noses, ears, and
lips—is ’t possible? Confess—handkerchief—O,
devil!

speaker: IAGO
text:
Work on,
My medicine, work! Thus credulous fools are caught,
And many worthy and chaste dames even thus,
All guiltless, meet reproach.—What ho! My lord!
My lord, I say. Othello!
How now, Cassio?

speaker: CASSIO
text: What’s the matter?

speaker: IAGO
text:
My lord is fall’n into an epilepsy.
This is his second fit. He had one yesterday.

speaker: CASSIO
text: Rub him about the temples.

speaker: IAGO
text:
No, forbear.
The lethargy must have his quiet course.
If not, he foams at mouth, and by and by
Breaks out to savage madness. Look, he stirs.
Do you withdraw yourself a little while.
He will recover straight. When he is gone,
I would on great occasion speak with you.
How is it, general? Have you not hurt your head?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Dost thou mock me?

speaker: IAGO
text:
I mock you not, by heaven!
Would you would bear your fortune like a man!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: A hornèd man’s a monster and a beast.

speaker: IAGO
text:
There’s many a beast, then, in a populous city,
And many a civil monster.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Did he confess it?

speaker: IAGO
text:
Good sir, be a man!
Think every bearded fellow that’s but yoked
May draw with you. There’s millions now alive
That nightly lie in those unproper beds
Which they dare swear peculiar. Your case is better.
O, ’tis the spite of hell, the fiend’s arch-mock,
To lip a wanton in a secure couch
And to suppose her chaste! No, let me know,
And knowing what I am, I know what she shall be.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: O, thou art wise, ’tis certain.

speaker: IAGO
text:
Stand you awhile apart.
Confine yourself but in a patient list.
Whilst you were here, o’erwhelmèd with your grief—
A passion most unsuiting such a man—
Cassio came hither. I shifted him away
And laid good ’scuses upon your ecstasy,
Bade him anon return and here speak with me,
The which he promised. Do but encave yourself,
And mark the fleers, the gibes, and notable scorns
That dwell in every region of his face.
For I will make him tell the tale anew—
Where, how, how oft, how long ago, and when
He hath and is again to cope your wife.
I say but mark his gesture. Marry, patience,
Or I shall say you’re all in all in spleen,
And nothing of a man.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Dost thou hear, Iago,
I will be found most cunning in my patience,
But (dost thou hear?) most bloody.

speaker: IAGO
text:
That’s not amiss.
But yet keep time in all. Will you withdraw?
Now will I question Cassio of Bianca,
A huswife that by selling her desires
Buys herself bread and clothes. It is a creature
That dotes on Cassio—as ’tis the strumpet’s plague
To beguile many and be beguiled by one.
He, when he hears of her, cannot restrain
From the excess of laughter. Here he comes.
As he shall smile, Othello shall go mad,
And his unbookish jealousy must construe
Poor Cassio’s smiles, gestures, and light behaviors
Quite in the wrong.—How do you, lieutenant?

speaker: CASSIO
text:
The worser that you give me the addition
Whose want even kills me.

speaker: IAGO
text:
Ply Desdemona well, and you are sure on ’t.
Now, if this suit lay in Bianca’s power,
How quickly should you speed!

speaker: CASSIO
text: Alas, poor caitiff!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Look how he laughs already!

speaker: IAGO
text: I never knew woman love man so.

speaker: CASSIO
text: Alas, poor rogue, I think i’ faith she loves me.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Now he denies it faintly and laughs it out.

speaker: IAGO
text: Do you hear, Cassio?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Now he importunes him
To tell it o’er. Go to, well said, well said.

speaker: IAGO
text:
She gives it out that you shall marry her.
Do you intend it?

speaker: CASSIO
text: Ha, ha, ha!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Do you triumph, Roman? Do you triumph?

speaker: CASSIO
text:
I marry her? What, a customer? Prithee bear
some charity to my wit! Do not think it so unwholesome.
Ha, ha, ha!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: So, so, so, so. They laugh that wins.

speaker: IAGO
text: Faith, the cry goes that you marry her.

speaker: CASSIO
text: Prithee say true!

speaker: IAGO
text: I am a very villain else.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Have you scored me? Well.

speaker: CASSIO
text:
This is the monkey’s own giving out. She is
persuaded I will marry her out of her own love and
flattery, not out of my promise.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Iago beckons me. Now he begins the story.

speaker: CASSIO
text:
She was here even now. She haunts me in
every place. I was the other day talking on the
sea-bank with certain Venetians, and thither comes
the bauble. By this hand, she falls thus about my
neck!

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Crying, “O dear Cassio,” as it were; his
gesture imports it.

speaker: CASSIO
text:
So hangs and lolls and weeps upon me, so
shakes and pulls me. Ha, ha, ha!

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Now he tells how she plucked him to my
chamber.—O, I see that nose of yours, but not that
dog I shall throw it to.

speaker: CASSIO
text: Well, I must leave her company.

speaker: IAGO
text: Before me, look where she comes.

speaker: CASSIO
text:
’Tis such another fitchew—marry, a perfumed
one!—What do you mean by this haunting
of me?

speaker: BIANCA
text:
Let the devil and his dam haunt you! What did
you mean by that same handkerchief you gave me
even now? I was a fine fool to take it! I must take
out the work? A likely piece of work, that you
should find it in your chamber and know not who
left it there! This is some minx’s token, and I must
take out the work! There, give it your hobbyhorse.
Wheresoever you had it, I’ll take out no work on ’t.

speaker: CASSIO
text: How now, my sweet Bianca? How now? How now?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: By heaven, that should be my handkerchief!

speaker: BIANCA
text:
If you’ll come to supper tonight you may. If
you will not, come when you are next prepared
for.

speaker: IAGO
text: After her, after her!

speaker: CASSIO
text: Faith, I must. She’ll rail in the streets else.

speaker: IAGO
text: Will you sup there?

speaker: CASSIO
text: Faith, I intend so.

speaker: IAGO
text:
Well, I may chance to see you, for I would very
fain speak with you.

speaker: CASSIO
text: Prithee come. Will you?

speaker: IAGO
text: Go to; say no more.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
How shall I murder him,
Iago?

speaker: IAGO
text: Did you perceive how he laughed at his vice?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: O Iago!

speaker: IAGO
text: And did you see the handkerchief?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Was that mine?

speaker: IAGO
text:
Yours, by this hand! And to see how he prizes
the foolish woman your wife! She gave it him, and
he hath giv’n it his whore.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
I would have him nine years a-killing! A fine
woman, a fair woman, a sweet woman!

speaker: IAGO
text: Nay, you must forget that.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Ay, let her rot and perish and be damned
tonight, for she shall not live. No, my heart is turned
to stone. I strike it, and it hurts my hand. O, the
world hath not a sweeter creature! She might lie by
an emperor’s side and command him tasks.

speaker: IAGO
text: Nay, that’s not your way.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Hang her, I do but say what she is! So
delicate with her needle, an admirable musician—
O, she will sing the savageness out of a bear!
Of so high and plenteous wit and invention!

speaker: IAGO
text: She’s the worse for all this.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
O, a thousand, a thousand times!—And then
of so gentle a condition!

speaker: IAGO
text: Ay, too gentle.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Nay, that’s certain. But yet the pity of it,
Iago! O, Iago, the pity of it, Iago!

speaker: IAGO
text:
If you are so fond over her iniquity, give her
patent to offend, for if it touch not you, it comes
near nobody.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: I will chop her into messes! Cuckold me?

speaker: IAGO
text: O, ’tis foul in her.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: With mine officer!

speaker: IAGO
text: That’s fouler.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Get me some poison, Iago, this night. I’ll not
expostulate with her lest her body and beauty
unprovide my mind again. This night, Iago.

speaker: IAGO
text:
Do it not with poison. Strangle her in her bed,
even the bed she hath contaminated.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Good, good. The justice of it pleases. Very
good.

speaker: IAGO
text:
And for Cassio, let me be his undertaker. You
shall hear more by midnight.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Excellent good.
What trumpet is that same?

speaker: IAGO
text:
I warrant something from Venice.
’Tis Lodovico. This comes from the Duke.
See, your wife’s with him.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: God save you, worthy general.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: With all my heart, sir.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: The Duke and the Senators of Venice greet you.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: I kiss the instrument of their pleasures.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: And what’s the news, good cousin Lodovico?

speaker: IAGO
text:
I am very glad to see you, signior.
Welcome to Cyprus.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: I thank you. How does Lieutenant Cassio?

speaker: IAGO
text: Lives, sir.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
Cousin, there’s fall’n between him and my lord
An unkind breach, but you shall make all well.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Are you sure of that?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: My lord?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
“This fail you not to do, as you
will”—

speaker: LODOVICO
text:
He did not call; he’s busy in the paper.
Is there division ’twixt my lord and Cassio?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
A most unhappy one. I would do much
T’ atone them, for the love I bear to Cassio.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Fire and brimstone!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: My lord?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Are you wise?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: What, is he angry?

speaker: LODOVICO
text:
May be the letter moved him.
For, as I think, they do command him home,
Deputing Cassio in his government.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: By my troth, I am glad on ’t.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Indeed?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: My lord?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: I am glad to see you mad.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Why, sweet Othello!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Devil!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I have not deserved this.

speaker: LODOVICO
text:
My lord, this would not be believed in Venice,
Though I should swear I saw ’t. ’Tis very much.
Make her amends. She weeps.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
O, devil, devil!
If that the Earth could teem with woman’s tears,
Each drop she falls would prove a crocodile.
Out of my sight!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I will not stay to offend you.

speaker: LODOVICO
text:
Truly an obedient lady.
I do beseech your Lordship call her back.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Mistress.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: My lord?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: What would you with her, sir?

speaker: LODOVICO
text: Who, I, my lord?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Ay, you did wish that I would make her turn.
Sir, she can turn, and turn, and yet go on,
And turn again. And she can weep, sir, weep.
And she’s obedient, as you say, obedient.
Very obedient.—Proceed you in your tears.—
Concerning this, sir—O, well-painted passion!—
I am commanded home.—Get you away.
I’ll send for you anon.—Sir, I obey the mandate
And will return to Venice.—Hence, avaunt!
Cassio shall have my place. And, sir, tonight
I do entreat that we may sup together.
You are welcome, sir, to Cyprus. Goats and monkeys!

speaker: LODOVICO
text:
Is this the noble Moor, whom our full senate
Call all in all sufficient? Is this the nature
Whom passion could not shake, whose solid virtue
The shot of accident nor dart of chance
Could neither graze nor pierce?

speaker: IAGO
text: He is much changed.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: Are his wits safe? Is he not light of brain?

speaker: IAGO
text:
He’s that he is. I may not breathe my censure
What he might be. If what he might he is not,
I would to heaven he were.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: What? Strike his wife?

speaker: IAGO
text:
’Faith, that was not so well. Yet would I knew
That stroke would prove the worst.

speaker: LODOVICO
text:
Is it his use?
Or did the letters work upon his blood
And new-create this fault?

speaker: IAGO
text:
Alas, alas!
It is not honesty in me to speak
What I have seen and known. You shall observe him,
And his own courses will denote him so
That I may save my speech. Do but go after
And mark how he continues.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: I am sorry that I am deceived in him.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: You have seen nothing then?

speaker: EMILIA
text: Nor ever heard, nor ever did suspect.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Yes, you have seen Cassio and she together.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
But then I saw no harm, and then I heard
Each syllable that breath made up between them.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: What, did they never whisper?

speaker: EMILIA
text: Never, my lord.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Nor send you out o’ th’ way?

speaker: EMILIA
text: Never.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: To fetch her fan, her gloves, her mask, nor nothing?

speaker: EMILIA
text: Never, my lord.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: That’s strange.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
I durst, my lord, to wager she is honest,
Lay down my soul at stake. If you think other,
Remove your thought. It doth abuse your bosom.
If any wretch have put this in your head,
Let heaven requite it with the serpent’s curse,
For if she be not honest, chaste, and true,
There’s no man happy. The purest of their wives
Is foul as slander.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Bid her come hither. Go.
She says enough. Yet she’s a simple bawd
That cannot say as much. This is a subtle whore,
A closet lock and key of villainous secrets.
And yet she’ll kneel and pray. I have seen her do ’t.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: My lord, what is your will?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Pray you, chuck, come hither.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: What is your pleasure?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Let me see your eyes. Look in my face.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: What horrible fancy’s this?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Some of your function, mistress.
Leave procreants alone, and shut the door.
Cough, or cry “hem,” if anybody come.
Your mystery, your mystery! Nay, dispatch.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
Upon my knees, what doth your speech import?
I understand a fury in your words,
But not the words.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Why? What art thou?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Your wife, my lord, your true and loyal wife.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Come, swear it. Damn thyself,
Lest, being like one of heaven, the devils themselves
Should fear to seize thee. Therefore be double damned.
Swear thou art honest.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Heaven doth truly know it.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Heaven truly knows that thou art false as hell.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: To whom, my lord? With whom? How am I false?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Ah, Desdemon, away, away, away!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
Alas the heavy day, why do you weep?
Am I the motive of these tears, my lord?
If haply you my father do suspect
An instrument of this your calling back,
Lay not your blame on me. If you have lost him,
I have lost him too.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Had it pleased heaven
To try me with affliction, had they rained
All kind of sores and shames on my bare head,
Steeped me in poverty to the very lips,
Given to captivity me and my utmost hopes,
I should have found in some place of my soul
A drop of patience. But alas, to make me
A fixèd figure for the time of scorn
To point his slow unmoving finger at—
Yet could I bear that too, well, very well.
But there where I have garnered up my heart,
Where either I must live or bear no life,
The fountain from the which my current runs
Or else dries up—to be discarded thence,
Or keep it as a cistern for foul toads
To knot and gender in—turn thy complexion there,
Patience, thou young and rose-lipped cherubin,
Ay, there look grim as hell.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I hope my noble lord esteems me honest.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
O, ay, as summer flies are in the shambles,
That quicken even with blowing! O thou weed,
Who art so lovely fair, and smell’st so sweet
That the sense aches at thee, would thou hadst ne’er been born!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Alas, what ignorant sin have I committed?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Was this fair paper, this most goodly book,
Made to write “whore” upon? What committed?
Committed? O thou public commoner,
I should make very forges of my cheeks
That would to cinders burn up modesty,
Did I but speak thy deeds. What committed?
Heaven stops the nose at it, and the moon winks;
The bawdy wind that kisses all it meets
Is hushed within the hollow mine of earth
And will not hear ’t. What committed?
Impudent strumpet!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: By heaven, you do me wrong!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Are not you a strumpet?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
No, as I am a Christian!
If to preserve this vessel for my lord
From any other foul unlawful touch
Be not to be a strumpet, I am none.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: What, not a whore?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: No, as I shall be saved.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Is ’t possible?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: O, heaven forgive us!

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
I cry you mercy, then.
I took you for that cunning whore of Venice
That married with Othello.—You, mistress,
That have the office opposite to Saint Peter
And keeps the gate of hell—you, you, ay, you!
We have done our course. There’s money for your pains.
I pray you turn the key and keep our counsel.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
Alas, what does this gentleman conceive?
How do you, madam? How do you, my good lady?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Faith, half asleep.

speaker: EMILIA
text: Good madam, what’s the matter with my lord?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: With who?

speaker: EMILIA
text: Why, with my lord, madam.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Who is thy lord?

speaker: EMILIA
text: He that is yours, sweet lady.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
I have none. Do not talk to me, Emilia.
I cannot weep, nor answers have I none
But what should go by water. Prithee, tonight
Lay on my bed my wedding sheets. Remember.
And call thy husband hither.

speaker: EMILIA
text: Here’s a change indeed.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
’Tis meet I should be used so, very meet.
How have I been behaved that he might stick
The small’st opinion on my least misuse?

speaker: IAGO
text: What is your pleasure, madam? How is ’t with you?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
I cannot tell. Those that do teach young babes
Do it with gentle means and easy tasks.
He might have chid me so, for, in good faith,
I am a child to chiding.

speaker: IAGO
text: What is the matter, lady?

speaker: EMILIA
text:
Alas, Iago, my lord hath so bewhored her,
Thrown such despite and heavy terms upon her
As true hearts cannot bear.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Am I that name, Iago?

speaker: IAGO
text: What name, fair lady?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Such as she said my lord did say I was.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
He called her “whore.” A beggar in his drink
Could not have laid such terms upon his callet.

speaker: IAGO
text: Why did he so?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I do not know. I am sure I am none such.

speaker: IAGO
text: Do not weep, do not weep! Alas the day!

speaker: EMILIA
text:
Hath she forsook so many noble matches,
Her father and her country and her friends,
To be called “whore”? Would it not make one weep?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: It is my wretched fortune.

speaker: IAGO
text: Beshrew him for ’t! How comes this trick upon him?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Nay, heaven doth know.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
I will be hanged if some eternal villain,
Some busy and insinuating rogue,
Some cogging, cozening slave, to get some office,
Have not devised this slander. I will be hanged else.

speaker: IAGO
text: Fie, there is no such man. It is impossible.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: If any such there be, heaven pardon him.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
A halter pardon him, and hell gnaw his bones!
Why should he call her “whore”? Who keeps her company?
What place? What time? What form? What likelihood?
The Moor’s abused by some most villainous knave,
Some base notorious knave, some scurvy fellow.
O heaven, that such companions thou ’dst unfold,
And put in every honest hand a whip
To lash the rascals naked through the world,
Even from the east to th’ west!

speaker: IAGO
text: Speak within door.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
O, fie upon them! Some such squire he was
That turned your wit the seamy side without
And made you to suspect me with the Moor.

speaker: IAGO
text: You are a fool. Go to!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
Alas, Iago,
What shall I do to win my lord again?
Good friend, go to him. For by this light of heaven,
I know not how I lost him. Here I kneel.
If e’er my will did trespass ’gainst his love,
Either in discourse of thought or actual deed,
Or that mine eyes, mine ears, or any sense
Delighted them in any other form,
Or that I do not yet, and ever did,
And ever will—though he do shake me off
To beggarly divorcement—love him dearly,
Comfort forswear me! Unkindness may do much,
And his unkindness may defeat my life,
But never taint my love. I cannot say “whore”—
It does abhor me now I speak the word.
To do the act that might the addition earn,
Not the world’s mass of vanity could make me.

speaker: IAGO
text:
I pray you be content. ’Tis but his humor.
The business of the state does him offense,
And he does chide with you.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: If ’twere no other—

speaker: IAGO
text:
It is but so, I warrant.
Hark how these instruments summon to supper.
The messengers of Venice stays the meat.
Go in and weep not. All things shall be well.
How now, Roderigo?

speaker: RODERIGO
text:
I do not find
That thou deal’st justly with me.

speaker: IAGO
text: What in the contrary?

speaker: RODERIGO
text:
Every day thou daff’st me with some device,
Iago, and rather, as it seems to me now,
keep’st from me all conveniency than suppliest me
with the least advantage of hope. I will indeed no
longer endure it. Nor am I yet persuaded to put up
in peace what already I have foolishly suffered.

speaker: IAGO
text: Will you hear me, Roderigo?

speaker: RODERIGO
text:
Faith, I have heard too much, and your
words and performances are no kin together.

speaker: IAGO
text: You charge me most unjustly.

speaker: RODERIGO
text:
With naught but truth. I have wasted myself
out of my means. The jewels you have had
from me to deliver to Desdemona would half have
corrupted a votaress. You have told me she hath
received them, and returned me expectations and
comforts of sudden respect and acquaintance, but I
find none.

speaker: IAGO
text: Well, go to! Very well.

speaker: RODERIGO
text:
“Very well.” “Go to!” I cannot go to, man,
nor ’tis not very well! By this hand, I say ’tis very
scurvy, and begin to find myself fopped in it.

speaker: IAGO
text: Very well.

speaker: RODERIGO
text:
I tell you ’tis not very well! I will make
myself known to Desdemona. If she will return me
my jewels, I will give over my suit and repent my
unlawful solicitation. If not, assure yourself I will
seek satisfaction of you.

speaker: IAGO
text: You have said now.

speaker: RODERIGO
text:
Ay, and said nothing but what I protest
intendment of doing.

speaker: IAGO
text:
Why, now I see there’s mettle in thee, and even
from this instant do build on thee a better opinion
than ever before. Give me thy hand, Roderigo.
Thou hast taken against me a most just exception,
but yet I protest I have dealt most directly in thy
affair.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: It hath not appeared.

speaker: IAGO
text:
I grant indeed it hath not appeared, and your
suspicion is not without wit and judgment. But,
Roderigo, if thou hast that in thee indeed which I
have greater reason to believe now than ever—I
mean purpose, courage, and valor—this night show
it. If thou the next night following enjoy not Desdemona,
take me from this world with treachery and
devise engines for my life.

speaker: RODERIGO
text:
Well, what is it? Is it within reason and
compass?

speaker: IAGO
text:
Sir, there is especial commission come from
Venice to depute Cassio in Othello’s place.

speaker: RODERIGO
text:
Is that true? Why, then, Othello and Desdemona
return again to Venice.

speaker: IAGO
text:
O, no. He goes into Mauritania and takes away
with him the fair Desdemona, unless his abode be
lingered here by some accident—wherein none
can be so determinate as the removing of Cassio.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: How do you mean, removing him?

speaker: IAGO
text:
Why, by making him uncapable of Othello’s
place: knocking out his brains.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: And that you would have me to do?

speaker: IAGO
text:
Ay, if you dare do yourself a profit and a right. He
sups tonight with a harlotry, and thither will I go to
him. He knows not yet of his honorable fortune. If
you will watch his going thence (which I will
fashion to fall out between twelve and one), you may
take him at your pleasure. I will be near to second
your attempt, and he shall fall between us. Come,
stand not amazed at it, but go along with me. I will
show you such a necessity in his death that you shall
think yourself bound to put it on him. It is now high
supper time, and the night grows to waste. About it!

speaker: RODERIGO
text: I will hear further reason for this.

speaker: IAGO
text: And you shall be satisfied.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: I do beseech you, sir, trouble yourself no further.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: O, pardon me, ’twill do me good to walk.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: Madam, good night. I humbly thank your Ladyship.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Your Honor is most welcome.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Will you walk, sir?—O, Desdemona—

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: My lord?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Get you to bed on th’ instant. I will be
returned forthwith. Dismiss your attendant there.
Look ’t be done.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I will, my lord.

speaker: EMILIA
text: How goes it now? He looks gentler than he did.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
He says he will return incontinent,
And hath commanded me to go to bed,
And bade me to dismiss you.

speaker: EMILIA
text: Dismiss me?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
It was his bidding. Therefore, good Emilia,
Give me my nightly wearing, and adieu.
We must not now displease him.

speaker: EMILIA
text: I would you had never seen him.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
So would not I. My love doth so approve him
That even his stubbornness, his checks, his frowns—
Prithee, unpin me—have grace and favor in them.

speaker: EMILIA
text: I have laid those sheets you bade me on the bed.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
All’s one. Good faith, how foolish are our minds!
If I do die before thee, prithee, shroud me
In one of those same sheets.

speaker: EMILIA
text: Come, come, you talk!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
My mother had a maid called Barbary.
She was in love, and he she loved proved mad
And did forsake her. She had a song of willow,
An old thing ’twas, but it expressed her fortune,
And she died singing it. That song tonight
Will not go from my mind. I have much to do
But to go hang my head all at one side
And sing it like poor Barbary. Prithee, dispatch.

speaker: EMILIA
text: Shall I go fetch your nightgown?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
No, unpin me here.
This Lodovico is a proper man.

speaker: EMILIA
text: A very handsome man.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: He speaks well.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
I know a lady in Venice would have walked
barefoot to Palestine for a touch of his nether lip.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
The poor soul sat sighing by a sycamore tree,
Sing all a green willow.
Her hand on her bosom, her head on her knee,
Sing willow, willow, willow.
The fresh streams ran by her and murmured her moans,
Sing willow, willow, willow;
Her salt tears fell from her, and softened the stones—
Lay by these.
Sing willow, willow, willow.
Prithee hie thee! He’ll come anon.
Sing all a green willow must be my garland.
Let nobody blame him, his scorn I approve.
Nay, that’s not next. Hark, who is ’t that knocks?

speaker: EMILIA
text: It’s the wind.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
I called my love false love, but what said he then?
Sing willow, willow, willow.
If I court more women, you’ll couch with more men.—
So, get thee gone. Good night. Mine eyes do itch;
Doth that bode weeping?

speaker: EMILIA
text: ’Tis neither here nor there.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
I have heard it said so. O these men, these men!
Dost thou in conscience think—tell me, Emilia—
That there be women do abuse their husbands
In such gross kind?

speaker: EMILIA
text: There be some such, no question.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Wouldst thou do such a deed for all the world?

speaker: EMILIA
text: Why, would not you?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: No, by this heavenly light!

speaker: EMILIA
text:
Nor I neither, by this heavenly light.
I might do ’t as well i’ th’ dark.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Wouldst thou do such a deed for all the world?

speaker: EMILIA
text:
The world’s a huge thing. It is a great price
for a small vice.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: In troth, I think thou wouldst not.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
In troth, I think I should, and undo ’t when I
had done it. Marry, I would not do such a thing for
a joint ring, nor for measures of lawn, nor for
gowns, petticoats, nor caps, nor any petty exhibition.
But for the whole world—’Uds pity! Who
would not make her husband a cuckold to make
him a monarch? I should venture purgatory for ’t.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
Beshrew me if I would do such a wrong
for the whole world!

speaker: EMILIA
text:
Why, the wrong is but a wrong i’ th’ world;
and, having the world for your labor, ’tis a wrong in
your own world, and you might quickly make it
right.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I do not think there is any such woman.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
Yes, a dozen; and as many to th’ vantage as
would store the world they played for.
But I do think it is their husbands’ faults
If wives do fall. Say that they slack their duties,
And pour our treasures into foreign laps;
Or else break out in peevish jealousies,
Throwing restraint upon us. Or say they strike us,
Or scant our former having in despite.
Why, we have galls, and though we have some grace,
Yet have we some revenge. Let husbands know
Their wives have sense like them. They see, and smell,
And have their palates both for sweet and sour,
As husbands have. What is it that they do
When they change us for others? Is it sport?
I think it is. And doth affection breed it?
I think it doth. Is ’t frailty that thus errs?
It is so too. And have not we affections,
Desires for sport, and frailty, as men have?
Then let them use us well. Else let them know,
The ills we do, their ills instruct us so.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
Good night, good night. God me such uses send,
Not to pick bad from bad, but by bad mend.

speaker: IAGO
text:
Here, stand behind this bulk. Straight will he come.
Wear thy good rapier bare, and put it home.
Quick, quick! Fear nothing. I’ll be at thy elbow.
It makes us or it mars us—think on that,
And fix most firm thy resolution.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: Be near at hand. I may miscarry in ’t.

speaker: IAGO
text: Here, at thy hand. Be bold and take thy stand.

speaker: RODERIGO
text:
I have no great devotion to the deed,
And yet he hath given me satisfying reasons.
’Tis but a man gone. Forth, my sword! He dies.

speaker: IAGO
text:
I have rubbed this young quat almost to the sense,
And he grows angry. Now, whether he kill Cassio,
Or Cassio him, or each do kill the other,
Every way makes my gain. Live Roderigo,
He calls me to a restitution large
Of gold and jewels that I bobbed from him
As gifts to Desdemona.
It must not be. If Cassio do remain,
He hath a daily beauty in his life
That makes me ugly. And besides, the Moor
May unfold me to him. There stand I in much peril.
No, he must die. Be ’t so. I hear him coming.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: I know his gait. ’Tis he!—Villain, thou diest!

speaker: CASSIO
text:
That thrust had been mine enemy indeed
But that my coat is better than thou know’st.
I will make proof of thine.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: O, I am slain!

speaker: CASSIO
text: I am maimed forever! Help, ho! Murder, murder!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: The voice of Cassio! Iago keeps his word.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: O, villain that I am!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: It is even so.

speaker: CASSIO
text: O, help ho! Light! A surgeon!

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
’Tis he! O brave Iago, honest and just,
That hast such noble sense of thy friend’s wrong!
Thou teachest me.—Minion, your dear lies dead,
And your unblest fate hies. Strumpet, I come.
Forth of my heart those charms, thine eyes, are blotted.
Thy bed, lust-stained, shall with lust’s blood be spotted.

speaker: CASSIO
text: What ho! No watch? No passage? Murder, murder!

speaker: GRATIANO
text: ’Tis some mischance. The voice is very direful.

speaker: CASSIO
text: O, help!

speaker: LODOVICO
text: Hark!

speaker: RODERIGO
text: O wretched villain!

speaker: LODOVICO
text:
Two or three groan. ’Tis heavy night.
These may be counterfeits. Let’s think ’t unsafe
To come in to the cry without more help.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: Nobody come? Then shall I bleed to death.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: Hark!

speaker: GRATIANO
text: Here’s one comes in his shirt, with light and weapons.

speaker: IAGO
text: Who’s there? Whose noise is this that cries on murder?

speaker: LODOVICO
text: We do not know.

speaker: IAGO
text: Did not you hear a cry?

speaker: CASSIO
text: Here, here! For heaven’s sake, help me!

speaker: IAGO
text: What’s the matter?

speaker: GRATIANO
text: This is Othello’s ancient, as I take it.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: The same indeed, a very valiant fellow.

speaker: IAGO
text: What are you here that cry so grievously?

speaker: CASSIO
text:
Iago? O, I am spoiled, undone by villains.
Give me some help!

speaker: IAGO
text: O me, lieutenant! What villains have done this?

speaker: CASSIO
text:
I think that one of them is hereabout
And cannot make away.

speaker: IAGO
text:
O treacherous villains!
What are you there?
Come in, and give some help.

speaker: RODERIGO
text: O, help me here!

speaker: CASSIO
text: That’s one of them.

speaker: IAGO
text: O murd’rous slave! O villain!

speaker: RODERIGO
text: O damned Iago! O inhuman dog!

speaker: IAGO
text:
Kill men i’ th’ dark?—Where be these bloody thieves?
How silent is this town! Ho, murder, murder!—
What may you be? Are you of good or evil?

speaker: LODOVICO
text: As you shall prove us, praise us.

speaker: IAGO
text: Signior Lodovico?

speaker: LODOVICO
text: He, sir.

speaker: IAGO
text: I cry you mercy. Here’s Cassio hurt by villains.

speaker: GRATIANO
text: Cassio?

speaker: IAGO
text: How is ’t, brother?

speaker: CASSIO
text: My leg is cut in two.

speaker: IAGO
text:
Marry, heaven forbid!
Light, gentlemen. I’ll bind it with my shirt.

speaker: BIANCA
text: What is the matter, ho? Who is ’t that cried?

speaker: IAGO
text: Who is ’t that cried?

speaker: BIANCA
text:
O, my dear Cassio,
My sweet Cassio! O Cassio, Cassio, Cassio!

speaker: IAGO
text:
O notable strumpet! Cassio, may you suspect
Who they should be that have thus mangled you?

speaker: CASSIO
text: No.

speaker: GRATIANO
text: I am sorry to find you thus; I have been to seek you.

speaker: IAGO
text:
Lend me a garter. So.—O for a chair
To bear him easily hence!

speaker: BIANCA
text: Alas, he faints. O, Cassio, Cassio, Cassio!

speaker: IAGO
text:
Gentlemen all, I do suspect this trash
To be a party in this injury.—
Patience awhile, good Cassio.—Come, come;
Lend me a light. Know we this face or no?
Alas, my friend and my dear countryman
Roderigo? No! Yes, sure. O heaven, Roderigo!

speaker: GRATIANO
text: What, of Venice?

speaker: IAGO
text: Even he, sir. Did you know him?

speaker: GRATIANO
text: Know him? Ay.

speaker: IAGO
text:
Signior Gratiano? I cry your gentle pardon.
These bloody accidents must excuse my manners
That so neglected you.

speaker: GRATIANO
text: I am glad to see you.

speaker: IAGO
text: How do you, Cassio?—O, a chair, a chair!

speaker: GRATIANO
text: Roderigo?

speaker: IAGO
text:
He, he, ’tis he! O, that’s well said; the chair.—
Some good man bear him carefully from hence.
I’ll fetch the General’s surgeon.— For you, mistress,
Save you your labor.—He that lies slain here, Cassio,
Was my dear friend. What malice was between you?

speaker: CASSIO
text: None in the world. Nor do I know the man.

speaker: IAGO
text:
What, look you pale?—O, bear him out o’ th’ air.
Stay you, good gentlemen.—Look you pale, mistress?—
Do you perceive the gastness of her eye?—
Nay, if you stare, we shall hear more anon.—
Behold her well. I pray you, look upon her.
Do you see, gentlemen? Nay, guiltiness will speak
Though tongues were out of use.

speaker: EMILIA
text: Alas, what is the matter? What is the matter, husband?

speaker: IAGO
text:
Cassio hath here been set on in the dark
By Roderigo and fellows that are scaped.
He’s almost slain, and Roderigo dead.

speaker: EMILIA
text: Alas, good gentleman! Alas, good Cassio!

speaker: IAGO
text:
This is the fruits of whoring. Prithee, Emilia,
Go know of Cassio where he supped tonight.
What, do you shake at that?

speaker: BIANCA
text: He supped at my house, but I therefore shake not.

speaker: IAGO
text: O, did he so? I charge you go with me.

speaker: EMILIA
text: O fie upon thee, strumpet!

speaker: BIANCA
text:
I am no strumpet, but of life as honest
As you that thus abuse me.

speaker: EMILIA
text: As I? Faugh! Fie upon thee!

speaker: IAGO
text:
Kind gentlemen, let’s go see poor Cassio dressed.—
Come, mistress, you must tell ’s another tale.—
Emilia, run you to the citadel
And tell my lord and lady what hath happed.—
Will you go on afore? This is the night
That either makes me or fordoes me quite.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
It is the cause, it is the cause, my soul.
Let me not name it to you, you chaste stars.
It is the cause. Yet I’ll not shed her blood,
Nor scar that whiter skin of hers than snow,
And smooth as monumental alabaster.
Yet she must die, else she’ll betray more men.
Put out the light, and then put out the light.
If I quench thee, thou flaming minister,
I can again thy former light restore
Should I repent me. But once put out thy light,
Thou cunning’st pattern of excelling nature,
I know not where is that Promethean heat
That can thy light relume. When I have plucked the rose,
I cannot give it vital growth again.
It needs must wither. I’ll smell it on the tree.
O balmy breath, that dost almost persuade
Justice to break her sword! One more, one more.
Be thus when thou art dead, and I will kill thee
And love thee after. One more, and this the last.
So sweet was ne’er so fatal. I must weep,
But they are cruel tears. This sorrow’s heavenly:
It strikes where it doth love. She wakes.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Who’s there? Othello?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Ay, Desdemona.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Will you come to bed, my lord?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Have you prayed tonight, Desdemon?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Ay, my lord.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
If you bethink yourself of any crime
Unreconciled as yet to heaven and grace,
Solicit for it straight.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
Alack, my lord,
What may you mean by that?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Well, do it, and be brief. I will walk by.
I would not kill thy unpreparèd spirit.
No, heaven forfend! I would not kill thy soul.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Talk you of killing?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Ay, I do.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Then heaven have mercy on me.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Amen, with all my heart.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: If you say so, I hope you will not kill me.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Humh.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
And yet I fear you, for you’re fatal then
When your eyes roll so. Why I should fear I know not,
Since guiltiness I know not, but yet I feel I fear.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Think on thy sins.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: They are loves I bear to you.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Ay, and for that thou diest.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
That death’s unnatural that kills for loving.
Alas, why gnaw you so your nether lip?
Some bloody passion shakes your very frame.
These are portents, but yet I hope, I hope
They do not point on me.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Peace, and be still.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: I will so. What’s the matter?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
That handkerchief
Which I so loved, and gave thee, thou gav’st to Cassio.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
No, by my life and soul! Send for the man
And ask him.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Sweet soul, take heed, take heed of perjury.
Thou art on thy deathbed.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Ay, but not yet to die.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Yes, presently.
Therefore confess thee freely of thy sin.
For to deny each article with oath
Cannot remove nor choke the strong conception
That I do groan withal. Thou art to die.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Then Lord have mercy on me!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: I say “Amen.”

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
And have you mercy, too. I never did
Offend you in my life, never loved Cassio
But with such general warranty of heaven
As I might love. I never gave him token.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
By heaven, I saw my handkerchief in ’s hand!
O perjured woman, thou dost stone my heart
And mak’st me call what I intend to do
A murder, which I thought a sacrifice!
I saw the handkerchief!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
He found it, then.
I never gave it him. Send for him hither.
Let him confess a truth.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: He hath confessed.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: What, my lord?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: That he hath used thee.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: How? Unlawfully?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Ay.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: He will not say so.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
No. His mouth is stopped.
Honest Iago hath ta’en order for ’t.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: O, my fear interprets. What, is he dead?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Had all his hairs been lives, my great revenge
Had stomach for them all.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Alas, he is betrayed, and I undone.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Out, strumpet! Weep’st thou for him to my face?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: O banish me, my lord, but kill me not!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Down, strumpet!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: Kill me tomorrow, let me live tonight.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Nay, if you strive—

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: But half an hour!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Being done, there is no pause.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: But while I say one prayer!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: It is too late.

speaker: EMILIA
text: My lord, my lord? What ho! My lord, my lord!

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
What noise is this?—Not dead? Not yet quite dead?
I that am cruel am yet merciful.
I would not have thee linger in thy pain.
So, so.

speaker: EMILIA
text: What, ho! My lord, my lord!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Who’s there?

speaker: EMILIA
text: O, good my lord, I would speak a word with you.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Yes. ’Tis Emilia.—By and by.—She’s dead.
’Tis like she comes to speak of Cassio’s death.
The noise was here. Ha, no more moving?
Still as the grave. Shall she come in? Were ’t good?
I think she stirs again. No. What’s best to do?
If she come in, she’ll sure speak to my wife.
My wife, my wife! What wife? I have no wife.
O insupportable! O heavy hour!
Methinks it should be now a huge eclipse
Of sun and moon, and that th’ affrighted globe
Should yawn at alteration.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
I do beseech you
That I may speak with you. O, good my lord—

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
I had forgot thee. O, come in, Emilia.—
Soft, by and by, let me the curtains draw.—
Where art thou?
What’s the matter with thee now?

speaker: EMILIA
text: O, my good lord, yonder’s foul murders done.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: What? Now?

speaker: EMILIA
text: But now, my lord.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
It is the very error of the moon.
She comes more nearer Earth than she was wont
And makes men mad.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
Cassio, my lord, hath killed
A young Venetian called Roderigo.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Roderigo killed? And Cassio killed?

speaker: EMILIA
text: No, Cassio is not killed.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Not Cassio killed? Then murder’s out of tune,
And sweet revenge grows harsh.

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: O falsely, falsely murdered.

speaker: EMILIA
text: O Lord, what cry is that?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: That? What?

speaker: EMILIA
text:
Out, and alas, that was my lady’s voice!
Help! Help ho! Help! O lady, speak again!
Sweet Desdemona, O sweet mistress, speak!

speaker: DESDEMONA
text: A guiltless death I die.

speaker: EMILIA
text: O, who hath done this deed?

speaker: DESDEMONA
text:
Nobody. I myself. Farewell.
Commend me to my kind lord. O, farewell.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Why, how should she be murdered?

speaker: EMILIA
text: Alas, who knows?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: You heard her say herself, it was not I.

speaker: EMILIA
text: She said so. I must needs report the truth.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
She’s like a liar gone to burning hell!
’Twas I that killed her.

speaker: EMILIA
text: O, the more angel she, and you the blacker devil!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: She turned to folly, and she was a whore.

speaker: EMILIA
text: Thou dost belie her, and thou art a devil!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: She was false as water.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
Thou art rash as fire to say
That she was false. O, she was heavenly true!

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Cassio did top her. Ask thy husband else.
O, I were damned beneath all depth in hell
But that I did proceed upon just grounds
To this extremity. Thy husband knew it all.

speaker: EMILIA
text: My husband?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Thy husband.

speaker: EMILIA
text: That she was false to wedlock?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Ay, with Cassio. Had she been true,
If heaven would make me such another world
Of one entire and perfect chrysolite,
I’d not have sold her for it.

speaker: EMILIA
text: My husband?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Ay, ’twas he that told me on her first.
An honest man he is, and hates the slime
That sticks on filthy deeds.

speaker: EMILIA
text: My husband?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: What needs this iterance, woman? I say, thy husband.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
O mistress, villainy hath made mocks with love!—
My husband say she was false?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
He, woman.
I say thy husband. Dost understand the word?
My friend, thy husband; honest, honest Iago.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
If he say so, may his pernicious soul
Rot half a grain a day! He lies to th’ heart!
She was too fond of her most filthy bargain.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Hah?

speaker: EMILIA
text:
Do thy worst!
This deed of thine is no more worthy heaven
Than thou wast worthy her.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Peace, you were best!

speaker: EMILIA
text:
Thou hast not half that power to do me harm
As I have to be hurt. O gull! O dolt,
As ignorant as dirt! Thou hast done a deed—
I care not for thy sword. I’ll make thee known,
Though I lost twenty lives. Help! Help, ho! Help!
The Moor hath killed my mistress! Murder, murder!

speaker: MONTANO
text: What is the matter? How now, general?

speaker: EMILIA
text:
O, are you come, Iago? You have done well,
That men must lay their murders on your neck.

speaker: GRATIANO
text: What is the matter?

speaker: EMILIA
text:
Disprove this villain, if thou be’st a man.
He says thou told’st him that his wife was false.
I know thou didst not. Thou ’rt not such a villain.
Speak, for my heart is full.

speaker: IAGO
text:
I told him what I thought, and told no more
Than what he found himself was apt and true.

speaker: EMILIA
text: But did you ever tell him she was false?

speaker: IAGO
text: I did.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
You told a lie, an odious, damnèd lie!
Upon my soul, a lie, a wicked lie!
She false with Cassio? Did you say with Cassio?

speaker: IAGO
text: With Cassio, mistress. Go to! Charm your tongue.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
I will not charm my tongue. I am bound to speak.
My mistress here lies murdered in her bed.

speaker: ALL
text: O heavens forfend!

speaker: EMILIA
text: And your reports have set the murder on!

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Nay, stare not, masters; it is true indeed.

speaker: GRATIANO
text: ’Tis a strange truth.

speaker: MONTANO
text: O monstrous act!

speaker: EMILIA
text:
Villainy, villainy, villainy!
I think upon ’t, I think! I smell ’t! O villainy!
I thought so then. I’ll kill myself for grief!
O villainy! Villainy!

speaker: IAGO
text: What, are you mad? I charge you get you home.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
Good gentlemen, let me have leave to speak.
’Tis proper I obey him, but not now.
Perchance, Iago, I will ne’er go home.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: O, O, O!

speaker: EMILIA
text:
Nay, lay thee down, and roar!
For thou hast killed the sweetest innocent
That e’er did lift up eye.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
O, she was foul!—
I scarce did know you, uncle. There lies your niece,
Whose breath indeed these hands have newly stopped.
I know this act shows horrible and grim.

speaker: GRATIANO
text:
Poor Desdemon, I am glad thy father’s dead.
Thy match was mortal to him, and pure grief
Shore his old thread in twain. Did he live now,
This sight would make him do a desperate turn,
Yea, curse his better angel from his side,
And fall to reprobance.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
’Tis pitiful. But yet Iago knows
That she with Cassio hath the act of shame
A thousand times committed. Cassio confessed it,
And she did gratify his amorous works
With that recognizance and pledge of love
Which I first gave her. I saw it in his hand.
It was a handkerchief, an antique token
My father gave my mother.

speaker: EMILIA
text: O God! O heavenly God!

speaker: IAGO
text: Zounds, hold your peace!

speaker: EMILIA
text:
’Twill out, ’twill out. I peace?
No, I will speak as liberal as the north.
Let heaven and men and devils, let them all,
All, all, cry shame against me, yet I’ll speak.

speaker: IAGO
text: Be wise, and get you home.

speaker: EMILIA
text: I will not.

speaker: GRATIANO
text: Fie, your sword upon a woman!

speaker: EMILIA
text:
O thou dull Moor, that handkerchief thou speak’st of
I found by fortune, and did give my husband—
For often, with a solemn earnestness
(More than indeed belonged to such a trifle),
He begged of me to steal ’t.

speaker: IAGO
text: Villainous whore!

speaker: EMILIA
text:
She give it Cassio? No, alas, I found it,
And I did give ’t my husband.

speaker: IAGO
text: Filth, thou liest!

speaker: EMILIA
text:
By heaven, I do not, I do not, gentlemen!
O murd’rous coxcomb, what should such a fool
Do with so good a wife?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Are there no stones in heaven
But what serves for the thunder?—Precious villain!

speaker: GRATIANO
text: The woman falls! Sure he hath killed his wife.

speaker: EMILIA
text: Ay, ay! O, lay me by my mistress’ side.

speaker: GRATIANO
text: He’s gone, but his wife’s killed.

speaker: MONTANO
text:
’Tis a notorious villain. Take you this weapon
Which I have here recovered from the Moor.
Come, guard the door without. Let him not pass,
But kill him rather. I’ll after that same villain,
For ’tis a damnèd slave.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
I am not valiant neither,
But every puny whipster gets my sword.
But why should honor outlive honesty?
Let it go all.

speaker: EMILIA
text:
What did thy song bode, lady?
Hark, canst thou hear me? I will play the swan
And die in music.
Willow, willow, willow.
Moor, she was chaste. She loved thee, cruel Moor.
So come my soul to bliss, as I speak true.
So speaking as I think, alas, I die.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
I have another weapon in this chamber.
It is a sword of Spain, the ice brook’s temper.
O, here it is.—Uncle, I must come forth.

speaker: GRATIANO
text:
If thou attempt it, it will cost thee dear;
Thou hast no weapon and perforce must suffer.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Look in upon me, then, and speak with me,
Or naked as I am I will assault thee.

speaker: GRATIANO
text: What is the matter?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Behold, I have a weapon.
A better never did itself sustain
Upon a soldier’s thigh. I have seen the day
That with this little arm and this good sword
I have made my way through more impediments
Than twenty times your stop. But—O vain boast!—
Who can control his fate? ’Tis not so now.
Be not afraid, though you do see me weaponed.
Here is my journey’s end, here is my butt
And very sea-mark of my utmost sail.
Do you go back dismayed? ’Tis a lost fear.
Man but a rush against Othello’s breast,
And he retires. Where should Othello go?
Now, how dost thou look now? O ill-starred wench,
Pale as thy smock, when we shall meet at compt,
This look of thine will hurl my soul from heaven,
And fiends will snatch at it. Cold, cold, my girl?
Even like thy chastity.—O cursèd, cursèd slave!—
Whip me, you devils,
From the possession of this heavenly sight!
Blow me about in winds, roast me in sulfur,
Wash me in steep-down gulfs of liquid fire!
O Desdemon! Dead, Desdemon! Dead! O, O!

speaker: LODOVICO
text: Where is this rash and most unfortunate man?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: That’s he that was Othello. Here I am.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: Where is that viper? Bring the villain forth.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
I look down towards his feet; but that’s a fable.—
If that thou be’st a devil, I cannot kill thee.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: Wrench his sword from him.

speaker: IAGO
text: I bleed, sir, but not killed.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
I am not sorry neither. I’d have thee live,
For in my sense ’tis happiness to die.

speaker: LODOVICO
text:
O thou Othello, that wert once so good,
Fall’n in the practice of a damnèd slave,
What shall be said to thee?

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Why, anything.
An honorable murderer, if you will,
For naught I did in hate, but all in honor.

speaker: LODOVICO
text:
This wretch hath part confessed his villainy.
Did you and he consent in Cassio’s death?

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Ay.

speaker: CASSIO
text: Dear general, I never gave you cause.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
I do believe it, and I ask your pardon.
Will you, I pray, demand that demi-devil
Why he hath thus ensnared my soul and body?

speaker: IAGO
text:
Demand me nothing. What you know, you know.
From this time forth I never will speak word.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: What? Not to pray?

speaker: GRATIANO
text: Torments will ope your lips.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: Well, thou dost best.

speaker: LODOVICO
text:
Sir,
You shall understand what hath befall’n,
Which, as I think, you know not. Here is a letter
Found in the pocket of the slain Roderigo,
And here another. The one of them imports
The death of Cassio, to be undertook
By Roderigo.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: O villain!

speaker: CASSIO
text: Most heathenish and most gross.

speaker: LODOVICO
text:
Now here’s another discontented paper
Found in his pocket, too; and this it seems
Roderigo meant t’ have sent this damnèd villain,
But that, belike, Iago in the interim
Came in and satisfied him.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
O, thou pernicious caitiff!—
How came you, Cassio, by that handkerchief
That was my wife’s?

speaker: CASSIO
text:
I found it in my chamber.
And he himself confessed it but even now,
That there he dropped it for a special purpose
Which wrought to his desire.

speaker: OTHELLO
text: O fool, fool, fool!

speaker: CASSIO
text:
There is besides, in Roderigo’s letter,
How he upbraids Iago, that he made him
Brave me upon the watch, whereon it came
That I was cast. And even but now he spake,
After long seeming dead: Iago hurt him,
Iago set him on.

speaker: LODOVICO
text:
You must forsake this room and go with us.
Your power and your command is taken off,
And Cassio rules in Cyprus. For this slave,
If there be any cunning cruelty
That can torment him much and hold him long,
It shall be his. You shall close prisoner rest,
Till that the nature of your fault be known
To the Venetian state.—Come, bring away.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
Soft you. A word or two before you go.
I have done the state some service, and they know ’t.
No more of that. I pray you in your letters,
When you shall these unlucky deeds relate,
Speak of me as I am. Nothing extenuate,
Nor set down aught in malice. Then must you speak
Of one that loved not wisely, but too well;
Of one not easily jealous, but being wrought,
Perplexed in the extreme; of one whose hand,
Like the base Judean, threw a pearl away
Richer than all his tribe; of one whose subdued eyes,
Albeit unused to the melting mood,
Drops tears as fast as the Arabian trees
Their medicinable gum. Set you down this.
And say besides, that in Aleppo once,
Where a malignant and a turbanned Turk
Beat a Venetian and traduced the state,
I took by th’ throat the circumcisèd dog,
And smote him, thus.

speaker: LODOVICO
text: O bloody period!

speaker: GRATIANO
text: All that is spoke is marred.

speaker: OTHELLO
text:
