And, like this insubstantial pageant faded,
Leave not a rack behind. We are such stuff
As dreams are made on, and our little life
Is rounded with a sleep. Sir, I am vexed.
Bear with my weakness. My old brain is troubled.
Be not disturbed with my infirmity.
If you be pleased, retire into my cell
And there repose. A turn or two I’ll walk
To still my beating mind.

speaker: FERDINAND / MIRANDA
text: We wish your peace.

speaker: PROSPERO
text: Come with a thought. I thank thee, Ariel. Come.

speaker: ARIEL
text: Thy thoughts I cleave to. What’s thy pleasure?

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
Spirit,
We must prepare to meet with Caliban.

speaker: ARIEL
text:
Ay, my commander. When I presented Ceres,
I thought to have told thee of it, but I feared
Lest I might anger thee.

speaker: PROSPERO
text: Say again, where didst thou leave these varlets?

speaker: ARIEL
text:
I told you, sir, they were red-hot with drinking,
So full of valor that they smote the air
For breathing in their faces, beat the ground
For kissing of their feet; yet always bending
Towards their project. Then I beat my tabor,
At which, like unbacked colts, they pricked their ears,
Advanced their eyelids, lifted up their noses
As they smelt music. So I charmed their ears
That, calf-like, they my lowing followed through
Toothed briers, sharp furzes, pricking gorse, and thorns,
Which entered their frail shins. At last I left them
I’ th’ filthy-mantled pool beyond your cell,
There dancing up to th’ chins, that the foul lake
O’erstunk their feet.

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
This was well done, my bird.
Thy shape invisible retain thou still.
The trumpery in my house, go bring it hither
For stale to catch these thieves.

speaker: ARIEL
text: I go, I go.

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
A devil, a born devil, on whose nature
Nurture can never stick; on whom my pains,
Humanely taken, all, all lost, quite lost;
And as with age his body uglier grows,
So his mind cankers. I will plague them all
Even to roaring.
Come, hang them on this line.

speaker: CALIBAN
text:
Pray you, tread softly, that the blind mole
may not hear a footfall. We now are near his cell.

speaker: STEPHANO
text:
Monster, your fairy, which you say is a
harmless fairy, has done little better than played the
jack with us.

speaker: TRINCULO
text:
Monster, I do smell all horse piss, at which
my nose is in great indignation.

speaker: STEPHANO
text:
So is mine.—Do you hear, monster. If I
should take a displeasure against you, look you—

speaker: TRINCULO
text: Thou wert but a lost monster.

speaker: CALIBAN
text:
Good my lord, give me thy favor still.
Be patient, for the prize I’ll bring thee to
Shall hoodwink this mischance. Therefore speak softly.
All’s hushed as midnight yet.

speaker: TRINCULO
text: Ay, but to lose our bottles in the pool!

speaker: STEPHANO
text:
There is not only disgrace and dishonor in
that, monster, but an infinite loss.

speaker: TRINCULO
text:
That’s more to me than my wetting. Yet this
is your harmless fairy, monster!

speaker: STEPHANO
text:
I will fetch off my bottle, though I be o’er
ears for my labor.

speaker: CALIBAN
text:
Prithee, my king, be quiet. Seest thou here,
This is the mouth o’ th’ cell. No noise, and enter.
Do that good mischief which may make this island
Thine own forever, and I, thy Caliban,
For aye thy foot-licker.

speaker: STEPHANO
text:
Give me thy hand. I do begin to have bloody
thoughts.

speaker: TRINCULO
text:
O King Stephano, O
peer, O worthy Stephano, look what a wardrobe
here is for thee!

speaker: CALIBAN
text: Let it alone, thou fool. It is but trash.

speaker: TRINCULO
text:
Oho, monster, we know what belongs to a
frippery. O King
Stephano!

speaker: STEPHANO
text:
Put off that gown, Trinculo. By this hand,
I’ll have that gown.

speaker: TRINCULO
text: Thy Grace shall have it.

speaker: CALIBAN
text:
The dropsy drown this fool! What do you mean
To dote thus on such luggage? Let ’t alone,
And do the murder first. If he awake,
From toe to crown he’ll fill our skins with pinches,
Make us strange stuff.

speaker: STEPHANO
text:
Be you quiet, monster.—Mistress Line, is
not this my jerkin?
Now is the jerkin under the line.—Now, jerkin, you
are like to lose your hair and prove a bald jerkin.

speaker: TRINCULO
text:
Do, do. We steal by line and level, an ’t like
your Grace.

speaker: STEPHANO
text:
I thank thee for that jest. Here’s a garment
for ’t. Wit shall not go unrewarded while I am king
of this country. “Steal by line and level” is an excellent
pass of pate. There’s another garment for ’t.

speaker: TRINCULO
text:
Monster, come, put some lime upon your
fingers, and away with the rest.

speaker: CALIBAN
text:
I will have none on ’t. We shall lose our time
And all be turned to barnacles or to apes
With foreheads villainous low.

speaker: STEPHANO
text:
Monster, lay to your fingers. Help to bear
this away where my hogshead of wine is, or I’ll turn
you out of my kingdom. Go to, carry this.

speaker: TRINCULO
text: And this.

speaker: STEPHANO
text: Ay, and this.

speaker: PROSPERO
text: Hey, Mountain, hey!

speaker: ARIEL
text: Silver! There it goes, Silver!

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
Fury, Fury! There, Tyrant, there! Hark, hark!
Go, charge my goblins that they grind their joints
With dry convulsions, shorten up their sinews
With agèd cramps, and more pinch-spotted make them
Than pard or cat o’ mountain.

speaker: ARIEL
text: Hark, they roar.

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
Let them be hunted soundly. At this hour
Lies at my mercy all mine enemies.
Shortly shall all my labors end, and thou
Shalt have the air at freedom. For a little
Follow and do me service.

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
Now does my project gather to a head.
My charms crack not, my spirits obey, and time
Goes upright with his carriage.—How’s the day?

speaker: ARIEL
text:
On the sixth hour, at which time, my lord,
You said our work should cease.

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
I did say so
When first I raised the tempest. Say, my spirit,
How fares the King and ’s followers?

speaker: ARIEL
text:
Confined together
In the same fashion as you gave in charge,
Just as you left them; all prisoners, sir,
In the line grove which weather-fends your cell.
They cannot budge till your release. The King,
His brother, and yours abide all three distracted,
And the remainder mourning over them,
Brimful of sorrow and dismay; but chiefly
Him that you termed, sir, the good old Lord Gonzalo.
His tears runs down his beard like winter’s drops
From eaves of reeds. Your charm so strongly works ’em
That if you now beheld them, your affections
Would become tender.

speaker: PROSPERO
text: Dost thou think so, spirit?

speaker: ARIEL
text: Mine would, sir, were I human.

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
And mine shall.
Hast thou, which art but air, a touch, a feeling
Of their afflictions, and shall not myself,
One of their kind, that relish all as sharply
Passion as they, be kindlier moved than thou art?
Though with their high wrongs I am struck to th’ quick,
Yet with my nobler reason ’gainst my fury
Do I take part. The rarer action is
In virtue than in vengeance. They being penitent,
The sole drift of my purpose doth extend
Not a frown further. Go, release them, Ariel.
My charms I’ll break, their senses I’ll restore,
And they shall be themselves.

speaker: ARIEL
text: I’ll fetch them, sir.

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
You elves of hills, brooks, standing lakes, and groves,
And you that on the sands with printless foot
Do chase the ebbing Neptune, and do fly him
When he comes back; you demi-puppets that
By moonshine do the green sour ringlets make,
Whereof the ewe not bites; and you whose pastime
Is to make midnight mushrumps, that rejoice
To hear the solemn curfew; by whose aid,
Weak masters though you be, I have bedimmed
The noontide sun, called forth the mutinous winds,
And ’twixt the green sea and the azured vault
Set roaring war; to the dread rattling thunder
Have I given fire, and rifted Jove’s stout oak
With his own bolt; the strong-based promontory
Have I made shake, and by the spurs plucked up
The pine and cedar; graves at my command
Have waked their sleepers, oped, and let ’em forth
By my so potent art. But this rough magic
I here abjure, and when I have required
Some heavenly music, which even now I do,
To work mine end upon their senses that
This airy charm is for, I’ll break my staff,
Bury it certain fathoms in the earth,
And deeper than did ever plummet sound
I’ll drown my book.
A solemn air, and the best comforter
To an unsettled fancy, cure thy brains,
Now useless, boiled within thy skull. There stand,
For you are spell-stopped.—
Holy Gonzalo, honorable man,
Mine eyes, e’en sociable to the show of thine,
Fall fellowly drops.—The charm dissolves apace,
And as the morning steals upon the night,
Melting the darkness, so their rising senses
Begin to chase the ignorant fumes that mantle
Their clearer reason.—O good Gonzalo,
My true preserver and a loyal sir
To him thou follow’st, I will pay thy graces
Home, both in word and deed.—Most cruelly
Didst thou, Alonso, use me and my daughter.
Thy brother was a furtherer in the act.—
Thou art pinched for ’t now, Sebastian.—Flesh and blood,
You, brother mine, that entertained ambition,
Expelled remorse and nature, whom, with Sebastian,
Whose inward pinches therefore are most strong,
Would here have killed your king, I do forgive thee,
Unnatural though thou art.—Their understanding
Begins to swell, and the approaching tide
Will shortly fill the reasonable shore
That now lies foul and muddy. Not one of them
That yet looks on me or would know me.—Ariel,
Fetch me the hat and rapier in my cell.
I will discase me and myself present
As I was sometime Milan.—Quickly, spirit,
Thou shalt ere long be free.

speaker: ARIEL
text:
Where the bee sucks, there suck I.
In a cowslip’s bell I lie.
There I couch when owls do cry.
On the bat’s back I do fly
After summer merrily.
Merrily, merrily shall I live now
Under the blossom that hangs on the bow.

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
Why, that’s my dainty Ariel. I shall miss
Thee, but yet thou shalt have freedom. So, so, so.
To the King’s ship, invisible as thou art.
There shalt thou find the mariners asleep
Under the hatches. The master and the boatswain
Being awake, enforce them to this place,
And presently, I prithee.

speaker: ARIEL
text:
I drink the air before me, and return
Or ere your pulse twice beat.

speaker: GONZALO
text:
All torment, trouble, wonder, and amazement
Inhabits here. Some heavenly power guide us
Out of this fearful country!

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
Behold, sir king,
The wrongèd Duke of Milan, Prospero.
For more assurance that a living prince
Does now speak to thee, I embrace thy body,
And to thee and thy company I bid
A hearty welcome.

speaker: ALONSO
text:
Whe’er thou be’st he or no,
Or some enchanted trifle to abuse me
(As late I have been) I not know. Thy pulse
Beats as of flesh and blood; and since I saw thee,
Th’ affliction of my mind amends, with which
I fear a madness held me. This must crave,
An if this be at all, a most strange story.
Thy dukedom I resign, and do entreat
Thou pardon me my wrongs. But how should Prospero
Be living and be here?

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
First, noble friend,
Let me embrace thine age, whose honor cannot
Be measured or confined.

speaker: GONZALO
text:
Whether this be
Or be not, I’ll not swear.

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
You do yet taste
Some subtleties o’ th’ isle, that will not let you
Believe things certain. Welcome, my friends all.
But you, my brace of lords, were I so minded,
I here could pluck his Highness’ frown upon you
And justify you traitors. At this time
I will tell no tales.

speaker: SEBASTIAN
text: The devil speaks in him.

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
No.
For you, most wicked sir, whom to call brother
Would even infect my mouth, I do forgive
Thy rankest fault, all of them, and require
My dukedom of thee, which perforce I know
Thou must restore.

speaker: ALONSO
text:
If thou be’st Prospero,
Give us particulars of thy preservation,
How thou hast met us here, whom three hours since
Were wracked upon this shore, where I have lost—
How sharp the point of this remembrance is!—
My dear son Ferdinand.

speaker: PROSPERO
text: I am woe for ’t, sir.

speaker: ALONSO
text:
Irreparable is the loss, and patience
Says it is past her cure.

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
I rather think
You have not sought her help, of whose soft grace,
For the like loss, I have her sovereign aid
And rest myself content.

speaker: ALONSO
text: You the like loss?

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
As great to me as late, and supportable
To make the dear loss have I means much weaker
Than you may call to comfort you, for I
Have lost my daughter.

speaker: ALONSO
text:
A daughter?
O heavens, that they were living both in Naples,
The King and Queen there! That they were, I wish
Myself were mudded in that oozy bed
Where my son lies!—When did you lose your daughter?

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
In this last tempest. I perceive these lords
At this encounter do so much admire
That they devour their reason, and scarce think
Their eyes do offices of truth, their words
Are natural breath.—But howsoe’er you have
Been justled from your senses, know for certain
That I am Prospero and that very duke
Which was thrust forth of Milan, who most strangely
Upon this shore, where you were wracked, was landed
To be the lord on ’t. No more yet of this.
For ’tis a chronicle of day by day,
Not a relation for a breakfast, nor
Befitting this first meeting. Welcome, sir.
This cell’s my court. Here have I few attendants,
And subjects none abroad. Pray you, look in.
My dukedom since you have given me again,
I will requite you with as good a thing,
At least bring forth a wonder to content you
As much as me my dukedom.

speaker: MIRANDA
text: Sweet lord, you play me false.

speaker: FERDINAND
text:
No, my dearest love,
I would not for the world.

speaker: MIRANDA
text:
Yes, for a score of kingdoms you should wrangle,
And I would call it fair play.

speaker: ALONSO
text:
If this prove
A vision of the island, one dear son
Shall I twice lose.

speaker: SEBASTIAN
text: A most high miracle!

speaker: FERDINAND
text:
Though the seas threaten, they are merciful.
I have cursed them without cause.

speaker: ALONSO
text:
Now, all the blessings
Of a glad father compass thee about!
Arise, and say how thou cam’st here.

speaker: MIRANDA
text:
O wonder!
How many goodly creatures are there here!
How beauteous mankind is! O, brave new world
That has such people in ’t!

speaker: PROSPERO
text: ’Tis new to thee.

speaker: ALONSO
text:
What is this maid with whom thou wast at play?
Your eld’st acquaintance cannot be three hours.
Is she the goddess that hath severed us
And brought us thus together?

speaker: FERDINAND
text:
Sir, she is mortal,
But by immortal providence she’s mine.
I chose her when I could not ask my father
For his advice, nor thought I had one. She
Is daughter to this famous Duke of Milan,
Of whom so often I have heard renown,
But never saw before, of whom I have
Received a second life; and second father
This lady makes him to me.

speaker: ALONSO
text:
I am hers.
But, O, how oddly will it sound that I
Must ask my child forgiveness!

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
There, sir, stop.
Let us not burden our remembrances with
A heaviness that’s gone.

speaker: GONZALO
text:
I have inly wept
Or should have spoke ere this. Look down, you gods,
And on this couple drop a blessèd crown,
For it is you that have chalked forth the way
Which brought us hither.

speaker: ALONSO
text: I say “Amen,” Gonzalo.

speaker: GONZALO
text:
Was Milan thrust from Milan, that his issue
Should become kings of Naples? O, rejoice
Beyond a common joy, and set it down
With gold on lasting pillars: in one voyage
Did Claribel her husband find at Tunis,
And Ferdinand, her brother, found a wife
Where he himself was lost; Prospero his dukedom
In a poor isle; and all of us ourselves
When no man was his own.

speaker: ALONSO
text:
Give me your hands.
Let grief and sorrow still embrace his heart
That doth not wish you joy!

speaker: GONZALO
text:
Be it so. Amen.
O, look, sir, look, sir, here is more of us.
I prophesied if a gallows were on land,
This fellow could not drown. Now, blasphemy,
That swear’st grace o’erboard, not an oath on shore?
Hast thou no mouth by land? What is the news?

speaker: BOATSWAIN
text:
The best news is that we have safely found
Our king and company. The next: our ship,
Which, but three glasses since, we gave out split,
Is tight and yare and bravely rigged as when
We first put out to sea.

speaker: ARIEL
text:
Sir, all this service
Have I done since I went.

speaker: PROSPERO
text: My tricksy spirit!

speaker: ALONSO
text:
These are not natural events. They strengthen
From strange to stranger.—Say, how came you hither?

speaker: BOATSWAIN
text:
If I did think, sir, I were well awake,
I’d strive to tell you. We were dead of sleep
And—how, we know not—all clapped under hatches,
Where, but even now, with strange and several noises
Of roaring, shrieking, howling, jingling chains,
And more diversity of sounds, all horrible,
We were awaked, straightway at liberty,
Where we, in all her trim, freshly beheld
Our royal, good, and gallant ship, our master
Cap’ring to eye her. On a trice, so please you,
Even in a dream were we divided from them
And were brought moping hither.

speaker: ARIEL
text: Was ’t well done?

speaker: PROSPERO
text: Bravely, my diligence. Thou shalt be free.

speaker: ALONSO
text:
This is as strange a maze as e’er men trod,
And there is in this business more than nature
Was ever conduct of. Some oracle
Must rectify our knowledge.

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
Sir, my liege,
Do not infest your mind with beating on
The strangeness of this business. At picked leisure,
Which shall be shortly, single I’ll resolve you,
Which to you shall seem probable, of every
These happened accidents; till when, be cheerful
And think of each thing well.Come hither, spirit;
Set Caliban and his companions free.
Untie the spell. How fares my gracious sir?
There are yet missing of your company
Some few odd lads that you remember not.

speaker: STEPHANO
text:
Every man shift for all the rest, and let no
man take care for himself, for all is but fortune.
Coraggio, bully monster, coraggio.

speaker: TRINCULO
text:
If these be true spies which I wear in my
head, here’s a goodly sight.

speaker: CALIBAN
text:
O Setebos, these be brave spirits indeed! How
fine my master is! I am afraid he will chastise me.

speaker: SEBASTIAN
text:
Ha, ha!
What things are these, my Lord Antonio?
Will money buy ’em?

speaker: ANTONIO
text:
Very like. One of them
Is a plain fish and no doubt marketable.

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
Mark but the badges of these men, my lords,
Then say if they be true. This misshapen knave,
His mother was a witch, and one so strong
That could control the moon, make flows and ebbs,
And deal in her command without her power.
These three have robbed me, and this demi-devil,
For he’s a bastard one, had plotted with them
To take my life. Two of these fellows you
Must know and own. This thing of darkness I
Acknowledge mine.

speaker: CALIBAN
text: I shall be pinched to death.

speaker: ALONSO
text: Is not this Stephano, my drunken butler?

speaker: SEBASTIAN
text: He is drunk now. Where had he wine?

speaker: ALONSO
text:
And Trinculo is reeling ripe. Where should they
Find this grand liquor that hath gilded ’em?
How cam’st thou in this pickle?

speaker: TRINCULO
text:
I have been in such a pickle since I saw you
last that I fear me will never out of my bones. I
shall not fear flyblowing.

speaker: SEBASTIAN
text: Why, how now, Stephano?

speaker: STEPHANO
text:
O, touch me not! I am not Stephano, but a
cramp.

speaker: PROSPERO
text: You’d be king o’ the isle, sirrah?

speaker: STEPHANO
text: I should have been a sore one, then.

speaker: ALONSO
text: This is as strange a thing as e’er I looked on.

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
He is as disproportioned in his manners
As in his shape. Go, sirrah, to my cell.
Take with you your companions. As you look
To have my pardon, trim it handsomely.

speaker: CALIBAN
text:
Ay, that I will, and I’ll be wise hereafter
And seek for grace. What a thrice-double ass
Was I to take this drunkard for a god,
And worship this dull fool!

speaker: PROSPERO
text: Go to, away!

speaker: ALONSO
text: Hence, and bestow your luggage where you found it.

speaker: SEBASTIAN
text: Or stole it, rather.

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
Sir, I invite your Highness and your train
To my poor cell, where you shall take your rest
For this one night, which part of it I’ll waste
With such discourse as, I not doubt, shall make it
Go quick away: the story of my life
And the particular accidents gone by
Since I came to this isle. And in the morn
I’ll bring you to your ship, and so to Naples,
Where I have hope to see the nuptial
Of these our dear-belovèd solemnized,
And thence retire me to my Milan, where
Every third thought shall be my grave.

speaker: ALONSO
text:
I long
To hear the story of your life, which must
Take the ear strangely.

speaker: PROSPERO
text:
I’ll deliver all,
And promise you calm seas, auspicious gales,
And sail so expeditious that shall catch
Your royal fleet far off. My Ariel, chick,
That is thy charge. Then to the elements
Be free, and fare thou well.—Please you, draw near.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Now my charms are all o’erthrown,
And what strength I have ’s mine own,
Which is most faint. Now ’tis true
I must be here confined by you,
Or sent to Naples. Let me not,
Since I have my dukedom got
And pardoned the deceiver, dwell
In this bare island by your spell,
But release me from my bands
With the help of your good hands.
Gentle breath of yours my sails
Must fill, or else my project fails,
Which was to please. Now I want
Spirits to enforce, art to enchant,
And my ending is despair,
Unless I be relieved by prayer,
Which pierces so that it assaults
Mercy itself, and frees all faults.
As you from crimes would pardoned be,
Let your indulgence set me free.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Cease to persuade, my loving Proteus.
Home-keeping youth have ever homely wits.
Were ’t not affection chains thy tender days
To the sweet glances of thy honored love,
I rather would entreat thy company
To see the wonders of the world abroad
Than, living dully sluggardized at home,
Wear out thy youth with shapeless idleness.
But since thou lov’st, love still and thrive therein,
Even as I would when I to love begin.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
Wilt thou be gone? Sweet Valentine, adieu.
Think on thy Proteus when thou haply seest
Some rare noteworthy object in thy travel.
Wish me partaker in thy happiness
When thou dost meet good hap; and in thy danger,
If ever danger do environ thee,
Commend thy grievance to my holy prayers,
For I will be thy beadsman, Valentine.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: And on a love-book pray for my success?

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Upon some book I love I’ll pray for thee.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
That’s on some shallow story of deep love,
How young Leander crossed the Hellespont.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
That’s a deep story of a deeper love,
For he was more than over shoes in love.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
’Tis true, for you are over boots in love,
And yet you never swam the Hellespont.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Over the boots? Nay, give me not the boots.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: No, I will not, for it boots thee not.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: What?

speaker: VALENTINE
PROTEUS
text: So, by your circumstance, you call me fool.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: So, by your circumstance, I fear you’ll prove.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: ’Tis love you cavil at; I am not Love.

speaker: VALENTINE
PROTEUS
text:
Yet writers say: as in the sweetest bud
The eating canker dwells, so eating love
Inhabits in the finest wits of all.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
And writers say: as the most forward bud
Is eaten by the canker ere it blow,
Even so by love the young and tender wit
Is turned to folly, blasting in the bud,
Losing his verdure, even in the prime,
And all the fair effects of future hopes.
But wherefore waste I time to counsel thee
That art a votary to fond desire?
Once more adieu. My father at the road
Expects my coming, there to see me shipped.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: And thither will I bring thee, Valentine.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Sweet Proteus, no. Now let us take our leave.
To Milan let me hear from thee by letters
Of thy success in love, and what news else
Betideth here in absence of thy friend.
And I likewise will visit thee with mine.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: All happiness bechance to thee in Milan.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: As much to you at home. And so farewell.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
He after honor hunts, I after love.
He leaves his friends, to dignify them more;
I leave myself, my friends, and all, for love.
Thou, Julia, thou hast metamorphosed me,
Made me neglect my studies, lose my time,
War with good counsel, set the world at nought;
Made wit with musing weak, heart sick with thought.

speaker: SPEED
text: Sir Proteus, ’save you. Saw you my master?

speaker: PROTEUS
text: But now he parted hence to embark for Milan.

speaker: SPEED
text:
Twenty to one, then, he is shipped already,
And I have played the sheep in losing him.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
Indeed a sheep doth very often stray,
An if the shepherd be awhile away.

speaker: SPEED
text:
You conclude that my master is a shepherd,
then, and I a sheep?

speaker: PROTEUS
text: I do.

speaker: SPEED
text:
Why, then my horns are his horns, whether I
wake or sleep.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: A silly answer, and fitting well a sheep.

speaker: SPEED
text: This proves me still a sheep.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: True, and thy master a shepherd.

speaker: SPEED
text: Nay, that I can deny by a circumstance.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: It shall go hard but I’ll prove it by another.

speaker: SPEED
text:
The shepherd seeks the sheep, and not the
sheep the shepherd; but I seek my master, and my
master seeks not me. Therefore I am no sheep.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
The sheep for fodder follow the shepherd; the
shepherd for food follows not the sheep. Thou for
wages followest thy master; thy master for wages
follows not thee. Therefore thou art a sheep.

speaker: SPEED
text: Such another proof will make me cry “baa.”

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
But dost thou hear? Gav’st thou my letter to
Julia?

speaker: SPEED
text:
Ay, sir. I, a lost mutton, gave your letter to her, a
laced mutton, and she, a laced mutton, gave me, a
lost mutton, nothing for my labor.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
Here’s too small a pasture for such store of
muttons.

speaker: SPEED
text:
If the ground be overcharged, you were best
stick her.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
Nay, in that you are astray; ’twere best pound
you.

speaker: SPEED
text:
Nay, sir, less than a pound shall serve me for
carrying your letter.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: You mistake; I mean the pound, a pinfold.

speaker: SPEED
text:
From a pound to a pin? Fold it over and over,
’Tis threefold too little for carrying a letter to your lover.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: But what said she?

speaker: SPEED
text: Ay.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Nod—“Ay.” Why, that’s “noddy.”

speaker: SPEED
text:
You mistook, sir. I say she did nod, and you ask
me if she did nod, and I say “ay.”

speaker: PROTEUS
text: And that set together is “noddy.”

speaker: SPEED
text:
Now you have taken the pains to set it together,
take it for your pains.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: No, no, you shall have it for bearing the letter.

speaker: SPEED
text: Well, I perceive I must be fain to bear with you.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Why, sir, how do you bear with me?

speaker: SPEED
text:
Marry, sir, the letter, very orderly, having nothing
but the word “noddy” for my pains.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Beshrew me, but you have a quick wit.

speaker: SPEED
text: And yet it cannot overtake your slow purse.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
Come, come, open the matter in brief. What
said she?

speaker: SPEED
text:
Open your purse, that the money and the matter
may be both at once delivered.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
Well, sir, here is for your
pains. What said she?

speaker: SPEED
text:
Truly, sir, I think you’ll
hardly win her.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
Why? Couldst thou perceive so much from
her?

speaker: SPEED
text:
Sir, I could perceive nothing at all from her, no,
not so much as a ducat for delivering your letter.
And being so hard to me that brought your mind, I
fear she’ll prove as hard to you in telling your mind.
Give her no token but stones, for she’s as hard as
steel.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: What said she? Nothing?

speaker: SPEED
text:
No, not so much as “Take this for thy pains.”
To testify your bounty, I thank you, you have
testerned me. In requital whereof, henceforth
carry your letters yourself. And so, sir, I’ll commend
you to my master.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
Go, go, begone, to save your ship from wrack,
Which cannot perish having thee aboard,
Being destined to a drier death on shore.
I must go send some better messenger.
I fear my Julia would not deign my lines,
Receiving them from such a worthless post.

speaker: JULIA
text:
But say, Lucetta, now we are alone,
Wouldst thou then counsel me to fall in love?

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Ay, madam, so you stumble not unheedfully.

speaker: JULIA
text:
Of all the fair resort of gentlemen
That every day with parle encounter me,
In thy opinion which is worthiest love?

speaker: LUCETTA
text:
Please you repeat their names, I’ll show my mind
According to my shallow simple skill.

speaker: JULIA
text: What think’st thou of the fair Sir Eglamour?

speaker: LUCETTA
text:
As of a knight well-spoken, neat, and fine;
But, were I you, he never should be mine.

speaker: JULIA
text: What think’st thou of the rich Mercatio?

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Well of his wealth, but of himself so-so.

speaker: JULIA
text: What think’st thou of the gentle Proteus?

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Lord, Lord, to see what folly reigns in us!

speaker: JULIA
text: How now? What means this passion at his name?

speaker: LUCETTA
text:
Pardon, dear madam, ’tis a passing shame
That I, unworthy body as I am,
Should censure thus on lovely gentlemen.

speaker: JULIA
text: Why not on Proteus, as of all the rest?

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Then thus: of many good, I think him best.

speaker: JULIA
text: Your reason?

speaker: LUCETTA
text:
I have no other but a woman’s reason:
I think him so because I think him so.

speaker: JULIA
text: And wouldst thou have me cast my love on him?

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Ay, if you thought your love not cast away.

speaker: JULIA
text: Why, he of all the rest hath never moved me.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Yet he of all the rest I think best loves you.

speaker: JULIA
text: His little speaking shows his love but small.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Fire that’s closest kept burns most of all.

speaker: JULIA
text: They do not love that do not show their love.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: O, they love least that let men know their love.

speaker: JULIA
text: I would I knew his mind.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Peruse this paper, madam.

speaker: JULIA
text: “To Julia.”—Say from whom.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: That the contents will show.

speaker: JULIA
text: Say, say who gave it thee.

speaker: LUCETTA
text:
Sir Valentine’s page; and sent, I think, from Proteus.
He would have given it you, but I, being in the way,
Did in your name receive it. Pardon the fault, I pray.

speaker: JULIA
text:
Now, by my modesty, a goodly broker!
Dare you presume to harbor wanton lines?
To whisper and conspire against my youth?
Now trust me, ’tis an office of great worth,
And you an officer fit for the place.
There, take the paper; see it be returned,
Or else return no more into my sight.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: To plead for love deserves more fee than hate.

speaker: JULIA
text: Will you be gone?

speaker: LUCETTA
text: That you may ruminate.

speaker: JULIA
text:
And yet I would I had o’erlooked the letter.
It were a shame to call her back again
And pray her to a fault for which I chid her.
What fool is she that knows I am a maid
And would not force the letter to my view,
Since maids in modesty say “no” to that
Which they would have the profferer construe “ay”!
Fie, fie, how wayward is this foolish love
That like a testy babe will scratch the nurse
And presently, all humbled, kiss the rod!
How churlishly I chid Lucetta hence,
When willingly I would have had her here!
How angerly I taught my brow to frown,
When inward joy enforced my heart to smile!
My penance is to call Lucetta back
And ask remission for my folly past.—
What ho, Lucetta!

speaker: LUCETTA
text: What would your Ladyship?

speaker: JULIA
text: Is ’t near dinner time?

speaker: LUCETTA
text:
I would it were,
That you might kill your stomach on your meat
And not upon your maid.

speaker: JULIA
text: What is ’t that you took up so gingerly?

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Nothing.

speaker: JULIA
text: Why didst thou stoop, then?

speaker: LUCETTA
text: To take a paper up that I let fall.

speaker: JULIA
text: And is that paper nothing?

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Nothing concerning me.

speaker: JULIA
text: Then let it lie for those that it concerns.

speaker: LUCETTA
text:
Madam, it will not lie where it concerns
Unless it have a false interpreter.

speaker: JULIA
text: Some love of yours hath writ to you in rhyme.

speaker: LUCETTA
text:
That I might sing it, madam, to a tune,
Give me a note. Your Ladyship can set—

speaker: JULIA
text:
As little by such toys as may be possible.
Best sing it to the tune of “Light o’ Love.”

speaker: LUCETTA
text: It is too heavy for so light a tune.

speaker: JULIA
text: Heavy? Belike it hath some burden then?

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Ay, and melodious were it, would you sing it.

speaker: JULIA
text: And why not you?

speaker: LUCETTA
text: I cannot reach so high.

speaker: JULIA
text: Let’s see your song. How now, minion!

speaker: LUCETTA
text:
Keep tune there still, so you will sing it out.
And yet methinks I do not like this tune.

speaker: JULIA
text: You do not?

speaker: LUCETTA
text: No, madam, ’tis too sharp.

speaker: JULIA
text: You, minion, are too saucy.

speaker: LUCETTA
text:
Nay, now you are too flat
And mar the concord with too harsh a descant.
There wanteth but a mean to fill your song.

speaker: JULIA
text: The mean is drowned with your unruly bass.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Indeed, I bid the base for Proteus.

speaker: JULIA
text:
This babble shall not henceforth trouble me.
Here is a coil with protestation.
Go, get you gone, and let the papers lie.
You would be fing’ring them to anger me.

speaker: LUCETTA
text:
She makes it strange, but she would be best pleased
To be so angered with another letter.

speaker: JULIA
text:
Nay, would I were so angered with the same!
O hateful hands, to tear such loving words!
Injurious wasps, to feed on such sweet honey
And kill the bees that yield it with your stings!
I’ll kiss each several paper for amends.
Look, here is writ “kind Julia.” Unkind Julia,
As in revenge of thy ingratitude,
I throw thy name against the bruising stones,
Trampling contemptuously on thy disdain.
And here is writ “love-wounded Proteus.”
Poor wounded name, my bosom as a bed
Shall lodge thee till thy wound be throughly healed,
And thus I search it with a sovereign kiss.
But twice or thrice was “Proteus” written down.
Be calm, good wind. Blow not a word away
Till I have found each letter in the letter
Except mine own name. That some whirlwind bear
Unto a ragged, fearful, hanging rock
And throw it thence into the raging sea.
Lo, here in one line is his name twice writ:
“Poor forlorn Proteus, passionate Proteus,
To the sweet Julia.” That I’ll tear away—
And yet I will not, sith so prettily
He couples it to his complaining names.
Thus will I fold them one upon another.
Now kiss, embrace, contend, do what you will.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Madam, dinner is ready, and your father stays.

speaker: JULIA
text: Well, let us go.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: What, shall these papers lie like telltales here?

speaker: JULIA
text: If you respect them, best to take them up.

speaker: LUCETTA
text:
Nay, I was taken up for laying them down.
Yet here they shall not lie, for catching cold.

speaker: JULIA
text: I see you have a month’s mind to them.

speaker: LUCETTA
text:
Ay, madam, you may say what sights you see;
I see things too, although you judge I wink.

speaker: JULIA
text: Come, come, will ’t please you go?

speaker: ANTONIO
text:
Tell me, Pantino, what sad talk was that
Wherewith my brother held you in the cloister?

speaker: PANTINO
text: ’Twas of his nephew Proteus, your son.

speaker: ANTONIO
text: Why, what of him?

speaker: PANTINO
text:
He wondered that your Lordship
Would suffer him to spend his youth at home
While other men, of slender reputation,
Put forth their sons to seek preferment out:
Some to the wars to try their fortune there,
Some to discover islands far away,
Some to the studious universities.
For any or for all these exercises
He said that Proteus your son was meet,
And did request me to importune you
To let him spend his time no more at home,
Which would be great impeachment to his age
In having known no travel in his youth.

speaker: ANTONIO
text:
Nor need’st thou much importune me to that
Whereon this month I have been hammering.
I have considered well his loss of time
And how he cannot be a perfect man,
Not being tried and tutored in the world.
Experience is by industry achieved
And perfected by the swift course of time.
Then tell me whither were I best to send him.

speaker: PANTINO
text:
I think your Lordship is not ignorant
How his companion, youthful Valentine,
Attends the Emperor in his royal court.

speaker: ANTONIO
text: I know it well.

speaker: PANTINO
text:
’Twere good, I think, your Lordship sent him thither.
There shall he practice tilts and tournaments,
Hear sweet discourse, converse with noblemen,
And be in eye of every exercise
Worthy his youth and nobleness of birth.

speaker: ANTONIO
text:
I like thy counsel. Well hast thou advised,
And that thou mayst perceive how well I like it,
The execution of it shall make known.
Even with the speediest expedition
I will dispatch him to the Emperor’s court.

speaker: PANTINO
text:
Tomorrow, may it please you, Don Alphonso,
With other gentlemen of good esteem,
Are journeying to salute the Emperor
And to commend their service to his will.

speaker: ANTONIO
text:
Good company. With them shall Proteus go.
And in good time! Now will we break with him.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
Sweet love, sweet lines, sweet life!
Here is her hand, the agent of her heart;
Here is her oath for love, her honor’s pawn.
O, that our fathers would applaud our loves
To seal our happiness with their consents.
O heavenly Julia!

speaker: ANTONIO
text: How now? What letter are you reading there?

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
May ’t please your Lordship, ’tis a word or two
Of commendations sent from Valentine,
Delivered by a friend that came from him.

speaker: ANTONIO
text: Lend me the letter. Let me see what news.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
There is no news, my lord, but that he writes
How happily he lives, how well beloved
And daily gracèd by the Emperor,
Wishing me with him, partner of his fortune.

speaker: ANTONIO
text: And how stand you affected to his wish?

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
As one relying on your Lordship’s will,
And not depending on his friendly wish.

speaker: ANTONIO
text:
My will is something sorted with his wish.
Muse not that I thus suddenly proceed,
For what I will, I will, and there an end.
I am resolved that thou shalt spend some time
With Valentinus in the Emperor’s court.
What maintenance he from his friends receives,
Like exhibition thou shalt have from me.
Tomorrow be in readiness to go.
Excuse it not, for I am peremptory.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
My lord, I cannot be so soon provided.
Please you deliberate a day or two.

speaker: ANTONIO
text:
Look what thou want’st shall be sent after thee.
No more of stay. Tomorrow thou must go.—
Come on, Pantino; you shall be employed
To hasten on his expedition.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
Thus have I shunned the fire for fear of burning
And drenched me in the sea, where I am drowned.
I feared to show my father Julia’s letter
Lest he should take exceptions to my love,
And with the vantage of mine own excuse
Hath he excepted most against my love.
O, how this spring of love resembleth
The uncertain glory of an April day,
Which now shows all the beauty of the sun,
And by and by a cloud takes all away.

speaker: PANTINO
text:
Sir Proteus, your father calls for you.
He is in haste. Therefore, I pray you, go.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
Why, this it is: my heart accords thereto.
And yet a thousand times it answers “no.”

speaker: SPEED
text: Sir, your glove.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Not mine. My gloves are on.

speaker: SPEED
text: Why, then, this may be yours, for this is but one.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Ha? Let me see. Ay, give it me, it’s mine.
Sweet ornament that decks a thing divine!
Ah, Sylvia, Sylvia!

speaker: SPEED
text: Madam Sylvia! Madam Sylvia!

speaker: VALENTINE
text: How now, sirrah?

speaker: SPEED
text: She is not within hearing, sir.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Why, sir, who bade you call her?

speaker: SPEED
text: Your Worship, sir, or else I mistook.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Well, you’ll still be too forward.

speaker: SPEED
text: And yet I was last chidden for being too slow.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Go to, sir. Tell me, do you know Madam
Sylvia?

speaker: SPEED
text: She that your Worship loves?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Why, how know you that I am in love?

speaker: SPEED
text:
Marry, by these special marks: first, you have
learned, like Sir Proteus, to wreathe your arms like
a malcontent; to relish a love song like a robin
redbreast; to walk alone like one that had the
pestilence; to sigh like a schoolboy that had lost his
ABC; to weep like a young wench that had buried
her grandam; to fast like one that takes diet; to
watch like one that fears robbing; to speak puling
like a beggar at Hallowmas. You were wont, when
you laughed, to crow like a cock; when you walked,
to walk like one of the lions. When you fasted, it was
presently after dinner; when you looked sadly, it
was for want of money. And now you are metamorphosed
with a mistress, that when I look on you, I
can hardly think you my master.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Are all these things perceived in me?

speaker: SPEED
text: They are all perceived without you.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Without me? They cannot.

speaker: SPEED
text:
Without you? Nay, that’s certain, for without
you were so simple, none else would. But you are so
without these follies, that these follies are within
you and shine through you like the water in an
urinal, that not an eye that sees you but is a
physician to comment on your malady.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
But tell me, dost thou know my Lady
Sylvia?

speaker: SPEED
text: She that you gaze on so as she sits at supper?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Hast thou observed that? Even she I mean.

speaker: SPEED
text: Why, sir, I know her not.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Dost thou know her by my gazing on her
and yet know’st her not?

speaker: SPEED
text: Is she not hard-favored, sir?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Not so fair, boy, as well-favored.

speaker: SPEED
text: Sir, I know that well enough.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: What dost thou know?

speaker: SPEED
text: That she is not so fair as, of you, well-favored.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
I mean that her beauty is exquisite but her
favor infinite.

speaker: SPEED
text:
That’s because the one is painted, and the other
out of all count.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: How painted? And how out of count?

speaker: SPEED
text:
Marry, sir, so painted to make her fair, that no
man counts of her beauty.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
How esteem’st thou me? I account of her
beauty.

speaker: SPEED
text: You never saw her since she was deformed.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: How long hath she been deformed?

speaker: SPEED
text: Ever since you loved her.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
I have loved her ever since I saw her, and
still I see her beautiful.

speaker: SPEED
text: If you love her, you cannot see her.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Why?

speaker: SPEED
text:
Because love is blind. O, that you had mine eyes,
or your own eyes had the lights they were wont to
have when you chid at Sir Proteus for going
ungartered!

speaker: VALENTINE
text: What should I see then?

speaker: SPEED
text:
Your own present folly and her passing deformity;
for he, being in love, could not see to garter his
hose, and you, being in love, cannot see to put on
your hose.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Belike, boy, then you are in love, for last
morning you could not see to wipe my shoes.

speaker: SPEED
text:
True, sir, I was in love with my bed. I thank you,
you swinged me for my love, which makes me the
bolder to chide you for yours.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: In conclusion, I stand affected to her.

speaker: SPEED
text:
I would you were set, so your affection would
cease.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Last night she enjoined me to write some
lines to one she loves.

speaker: SPEED
text: And have you?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: I have.

speaker: SPEED
text: Are they not lamely writ?

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
No, boy, but as well as I can do them.
Peace, here she comes.

speaker: SPEED
text:
O excellent motion! O exceeding puppet!
Now will he interpret to her.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Madam and mistress, a thousand
good-morrows.

speaker: SPEED
text:
O, give ye good ev’n! Here’s a million of
manners.

speaker: SYLVIA
text:
Sir Valentine, and servant, to you two
thousand.

speaker: SPEED
text:
He should give her interest, and she
gives it him.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
As you enjoined me, I have writ your letter
Unto the secret, nameless friend of yours,
Which I was much unwilling to proceed in
But for my duty to your Ladyship.

speaker: SYLVIA
text: I thank you, gentle servant, ’tis very clerkly done.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Now trust me, madam, it came hardly off,
For, being ignorant to whom it goes,
I writ at random, very doubtfully.

speaker: SYLVIA
text: Perchance you think too much of so much pains?

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
No, madam. So it stead you, I will write,
Please you command, a thousand times as much,
And yet—

speaker: SYLVIA
text:
A pretty period. Well, I guess the sequel;
And yet I will not name it And yet I care not.
And yet take this again.
And yet I thank you,
Meaning henceforth to trouble you no more.

speaker: SPEED
text: And yet you will; and yet another “yet.”

speaker: VALENTINE
text: What means your Ladyship? Do you not like it?

speaker: SYLVIA
text:
Yes, yes, the lines are very quaintly writ,
But, since unwillingly, take them again.
Nay, take them.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Madam, they are for you.

speaker: SYLVIA
text:
Ay, ay. You writ them, sir, at my request,
But I will none of them. They are for you.
I would have had them writ more movingly.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Please you, I’ll write your Ladyship another.

speaker: SYLVIA
text:
And when it’s writ, for my sake read it over,
And if it please you, so; if not, why, so.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: If it please me, madam? What then?

speaker: SYLVIA
text:
Why, if it please you, take it for your labor.
And so good-morrow, servant.

speaker: SPEED
text:
O jest unseen, inscrutable, invisible
As a nose on a man’s face, or a weathercock on a steeple!
My master sues to her, and she hath taught her suitor,
He being her pupil, to become her tutor.
O excellent device! Was there ever heard a better?
That my master, being scribe, to himself should write the letter?

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
How now, sir? What, are you reasoning
with yourself?

speaker: SPEED
text:
Nay, I was rhyming. ’Tis you that have the
reason.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: To do what?

speaker: SPEED
text: To be a spokesman from Madam Sylvia.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: To whom?

speaker: SPEED
text: To yourself. Why, she woos you by a figure.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: What figure?

speaker: SPEED
text: By a letter, I should say.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Why, she hath not writ to me!

speaker: SPEED
text:
What need she when she hath made you write
to yourself? Why, do you not perceive the jest?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: No, believe me.

speaker: SPEED
text:
No believing you indeed, sir. But did you perceive
her earnest?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: She gave me none, except an angry word.

speaker: SPEED
text: Why, she hath given you a letter.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: That’s the letter I writ to her friend.

speaker: SPEED
text:
And that letter hath she delivered, and there an
end.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: I would it were no worse.

speaker: SPEED
text:
I’ll warrant you, ’tis as well.
For often have you writ to her, and she, in modesty
Or else for want of idle time, could not again reply,
Or fearing else some messenger that might her mind discover,
Herself hath taught her love himself to write unto her lover.
All this I speak in print, for in print I found it. Why
muse you, sir? ’Tis dinnertime.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: I have dined.

speaker: SPEED
text:
Ay, but hearken, sir, though the chameleon love
can feed on the air, I am one that am nourished by
my victuals and would fain have meat. O, be not like
your mistress! Be moved, be moved.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Have patience, gentle Julia.

speaker: JULIA
text: I must where is no remedy.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: When possibly I can, I will return.

speaker: JULIA
text:
If you turn not, you will return the sooner.
Keep this remembrance for thy Julia’s sake.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Why, then we’ll make exchange. Here, take you this.

speaker: JULIA
text: And seal the bargain with a holy kiss.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
Here is my hand for my true constancy.
And when that hour o’erslips me in the day
Wherein I sigh not, Julia, for thy sake,
The next ensuing hour some foul mischance
Torment me for my love’s forgetfulness.
My father stays my coming. Answer not.
The tide is now—nay, not thy tide of tears;
That tide will stay me longer than I should.
Julia, farewell.
What, gone without a word?
Ay, so true love should do. It cannot speak,
For truth hath better deeds than words to grace it.

speaker: PANTINO
text: Sir Proteus, you are stayed for.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
Go. I come, I come.
Alas, this parting strikes poor lovers dumb.

speaker: LANCE
text:
Nay,’twill be this hour ere I have done weeping.
All the kind of the Lances have this very fault. I have
received my proportion like the Prodigious Son and
am going with Sir Proteus to the Imperial’s court. I
think Crab my dog be the sourest-natured dog that
lives: my mother weeping, my father wailing, my
sister crying, our maid howling, our cat wringing
her hands, and all our house in a great perplexity,
yet did not this cruel-hearted cur shed one tear. He
is a stone, a very pibble stone, and has no more pity
in him than a dog. A Jew would have wept to have
seen our parting. Why, my grandam, having no
eyes, look you, wept herself blind at my parting.
Nay, I’ll show you the manner of it.
This shoe is my father. No, this left shoe is
my father; no, no, this left shoe is my mother. Nay,
that cannot be so neither. Yes, it is so, it is so; it hath
the worser sole. This shoe with the hole in it is my
mother; and this my father. A vengeance on ’t, there
’tis! Now sir, this staff is my sister, for, look you, she
is as white as a lily and as small as a wand. This hat
is Nan, our maid. I am the dog. No, the dog is
himself, and I am the dog. O, the dog is me, and I
am myself. Ay, so, so. Now come I to my father:
“Father, your blessing.” Now should not the shoe
speak a word for weeping. Now should I kiss my
father. Well, he weeps on. Now
come I to my mother. O, that she could speak now
like a wold woman! Well, I kiss her.
Why, there ’tis; here’s my mother’s
breath up and down. Now come I to my sister. Mark
the moan she makes! Now the dog all this while
sheds not a tear nor speaks a word. But see how I
lay the dust with my tears.

speaker: PANTINO
text:
Lance, away, away! Aboard. Thy master is
shipped, and thou art to post after with oars. What’s
the matter? Why weep’st thou, man? Away, ass.
You’ll lose the tide if you tarry any longer.

speaker: LANCE
text:
It is no matter if the tied were lost, for it is the
unkindest tied that ever any man tied.

speaker: PANTINO
text: What’s the unkindest tide?

speaker: LANCE
text: Why, he that’s tied here, Crab my dog.

speaker: PANTINO
text:
Tut, man. I mean thou ’lt lose the flood and, in
losing the flood, lose thy voyage and, in losing thy
voyage, lose thy master and, in losing thy master,
lose thy service and, in losing thy service—
Why dost thou stop my
mouth?

speaker: LANCE
text: For fear thou shouldst lose thy tongue.

speaker: PANTINO
text: Where should I lose my tongue?

speaker: LANCE
text: In thy tale.

speaker: PANTINO
text: In thy tail!

speaker: LANCE
text:
Lose the tide, and the voyage, and the master,
and the service, and the tied. Why, man, if the river
were dry, I am able to fill it with my tears; if the
wind were down, I could drive the boat with my
sighs.

speaker: PANTINO
text:
Come. Come away, man. I was sent to call
thee.

speaker: LANCE
text: Sir, call me what thou dar’st.

speaker: PANTINO
text: Wilt thou go?

speaker: LANCE
text: Well, I will go.

speaker: SYLVIA
text: Servant!

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Mistress?

speaker: SPEED
text: Master, Sir Thurio frowns on you.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Ay, boy, it’s for love.

speaker: SPEED
text: Not of you.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Of my mistress, then.

speaker: SPEED
text: ’Twere good you knocked him.

speaker: SYLVIA
text: Servant, you are sad.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Indeed, madam, I seem so.

speaker: THURIO
text: Seem you that you are not?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Haply I do.

speaker: THURIO
text: So do counterfeits.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: So do you.

speaker: THURIO
text: What seem I that I am not?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Wise.

speaker: THURIO
text: What instance of the contrary?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Your folly.

speaker: THURIO
text: And how quote you my folly?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: I quote it in your jerkin.

speaker: THURIO
text: My “jerkin” is a doublet.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Well, then, I’ll double your folly.

speaker: THURIO
text: How!

speaker: SYLVIA
text: What, angry, Sir Thurio? Do you change color?

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Give him leave, madam. He is a kind of
chameleon.

speaker: THURIO
text:
That hath more mind to feed on your blood
than live in your air.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: You have said, sir.

speaker: THURIO
text: Ay, sir, and done too for this time.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
I know it well, sir. You always end ere you
begin.

speaker: SYLVIA
text:
A fine volley of words, gentlemen, and quickly
shot off.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: ’Tis indeed, madam. We thank the giver.

speaker: SYLVIA
text: Who is that, servant?

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Yourself, sweet lady, for you gave the fire.
Sir Thurio borrows his wit from your Ladyship’s
looks and spends what he borrows kindly in your
company.

speaker: THURIO
text:
Sir, if you spend word for word with me, I shall
make your wit bankrupt.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
I know it well, sir. You have an exchequer
of words and, I think, no other treasure to give your
followers, for it appears by their bare liveries that
they live by your bare words.

speaker: SYLVIA
text: No more, gentlemen, no more. Here comes my father.

speaker: DUKE
text:
Now, daughter Sylvia, you are hard beset.—
Sir Valentine, your father is in good health.
What say you to a letter from your friends
Of much good news?

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
My lord, I will be thankful
To any happy messenger from thence.

speaker: DUKE
text: Know you Don Antonio, your countryman?

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Ay, my good lord, I know the gentleman
To be of worth and worthy estimation,
And not without desert so well reputed.

speaker: DUKE
text: Hath he not a son?

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Ay, my good lord, a son that well deserves
The honor and regard of such a father.

speaker: DUKE
text: You know him well?

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
I knew him as myself, for from our infancy
We have conversed and spent our hours together,
And though myself have been an idle truant,
Omitting the sweet benefit of time
To clothe mine age with angel-like perfection,
Yet hath Sir Proteus—for that’s his name—
Made use and fair advantage of his days:
His years but young, but his experience old;
His head unmellowed, but his judgment ripe;
And in a word—for far behind his worth
Comes all the praises that I now bestow—
He is complete in feature and in mind,
With all good grace to grace a gentleman.

speaker: DUKE
text:
Beshrew me, sir, but if he make this good,
He is as worthy for an empress’ love,
As meet to be an emperor’s counselor.
Well, sir, this gentleman is come to me
With commendation from great potentates,
And here he means to spend his time awhile.
I think ’tis no unwelcome news to you.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Should I have wished a thing, it had been he.

speaker: DUKE
text:
Welcome him then according to his worth.
Sylvia, I speak to you—and you, Sir Thurio.
For Valentine, I need not cite him to it.
I will send him hither to you presently.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
This is the gentleman I told your Ladyship
Had come along with me but that his mistress
Did hold his eyes locked in her crystal looks.

speaker: SYLVIA
text:
Belike that now she hath enfranchised them
Upon some other pawn for fealty.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Nay, sure, I think she holds them prisoners still.

speaker: SYLVIA
text:
Nay, then, he should be blind, and being blind
How could he see his way to seek out you?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Why, lady, love hath twenty pair of eyes.

speaker: THURIO
text: They say that Love hath not an eye at all.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
To see such lovers, Thurio, as yourself.
Upon a homely object, Love can wink.

speaker: SYLVIA
text: Have done, have done. Here comes the gentleman.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Welcome, dear Proteus.—Mistress, I beseech you
Confirm his welcome with some special favor.

speaker: SYLVIA
text:
His worth is warrant for his welcome hither,
If this be he you oft have wished to hear from.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Mistress, it is. Sweet lady, entertain him
To be my fellow-servant to your Ladyship.

speaker: SYLVIA
text: Too low a mistress for so high a servant.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
Not so, sweet lady, but too mean a servant
To have a look of such a worthy mistress.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Leave off discourse of disability.
Sweet lady, entertain him for your servant.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: My duty will I boast of, nothing else.

speaker: SYLVIA
text:
And duty never yet did want his meed.
Servant, you are welcome to a worthless mistress.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: I’ll die on him that says so but yourself.

speaker: SYLVIA
text: That you are welcome?

speaker: PROTEUS
text: That you are worthless.

speaker: SERVANT
text: Madam, my lord your father would speak with you.

speaker: SYLVIA
text:
I wait upon his pleasure. Come, Sir Thurio,
Go with me.—Once more, new servant, welcome.
I’ll leave you to confer of home affairs.
When you have done, we look to hear from you.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: We’ll both attend upon your Ladyship.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Now tell me, how do all from whence you came?

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Your friends are well and have them much commended.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: And how do yours?

speaker: PROTEUS
text: I left them all in health.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: How does your lady? And how thrives your love?

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
My tales of love were wont to weary you.
I know you joy not in a love discourse.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Ay, Proteus, but that life is altered now.
I have done penance for contemning Love,
Whose high imperious thoughts have punished me
With bitter fasts, with penitential groans,
With nightly tears, and daily heartsore sighs,
For in revenge of my contempt of love,
Love hath chased sleep from my enthrallèd eyes
And made them watchers of mine own heart’s sorrow.
O gentle Proteus, Love’s a mighty lord
And hath so humbled me as I confess
There is no woe to his correction,
Nor, to his service, no such joy on Earth.
Now, no discourse except it be of love.
Now can I break my fast, dine, sup, and sleep
Upon the very naked name of Love.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
Enough; I read your fortune in your eye.
Was this the idol that you worship so?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Even she. And is she not a heavenly saint?

speaker: PROTEUS
text: No, but she is an earthly paragon.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Call her divine.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: I will not flatter her.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: O, flatter me, for love delights in praises.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
When I was sick, you gave me bitter pills,
And I must minister the like to you.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Then speak the truth by her; if not divine,
Yet let her be a principality,
Sovereign to all the creatures on the Earth.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Except my mistress.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Sweet, except not any,
Except thou wilt except against my love.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Have I not reason to prefer mine own?

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
And I will help thee to prefer her too:
She shall be dignified with this high honor—
To bear my lady’s train, lest the base earth
Should from her vesture chance to steal a kiss
And, of so great a favor growing proud,
Disdain to root the summer-swelling flower
And make rough winter everlastingly.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Why, Valentine, what braggartism is this?

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Pardon me, Proteus, all I can is nothing
To her whose worth makes other worthies nothing.
She is alone—

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Then let her alone.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Not for the world! Why, man, she is mine own,
And I as rich in having such a jewel
As twenty seas if all their sand were pearl,
The water nectar, and the rocks pure gold.
Forgive me that I do not dream on thee,
Because thou seest me dote upon my love.
My foolish rival, that her father likes
Only for his possessions are so huge,
Is gone with her along, and I must after,
For love, thou know’st, is full of jealousy.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: But she loves you?

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Ay, and we are betrothed; nay more, our marriage hour,
With all the cunning manner of our flight
Determined of: how I must climb her window,
The ladder made of cords, and all the means
Plotted and ’greed on for my happiness.
Good Proteus, go with me to my chamber,
In these affairs to aid me with thy counsel.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
Go on before. I shall inquire you forth.
I must unto the road to disembark
Some necessaries that I needs must use,
And then I’ll presently attend you.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Will you make haste?

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
I will.
Even as one heat another heat expels,
Or as one nail by strength drives out another,
So the remembrance of my former love
Is by a newer object quite forgotten.
Is it mine eye, or Valentine’s praise,
Her true perfection, or my false transgression,
That makes me reasonless to reason thus?
She is fair, and so is Julia that I love—
That I did love, for now my love is thawed,
Which like a waxen image ’gainst a fire
Bears no impression of the thing it was.
Methinks my zeal to Valentine is cold,
And that I love him not as I was wont.
O, but I love his lady too too much,
And that’s the reason I love him so little.
How shall I dote on her with more advice
That thus without advice begin to love her?
’Tis but her picture I have yet beheld,
And that hath dazzled my reason’s light;
But when I look on her perfections,
There is no reason but I shall be blind.
If I can check my erring love, I will;
If not, to compass her I’ll use my skill.

speaker: SPEED
text: Lance, by mine honesty, welcome to Padua.

speaker: LANCE
text:
Forswear not thyself, sweet youth, for I am not
welcome. I reckon this always: that a man is never
undone till he be hanged, nor never welcome to a
place till some certain shot be paid and the Hostess
say welcome.

speaker: SPEED
text:
Come on, you madcap. I’ll to the alehouse with
you presently, where, for one shot of five pence,
thou shalt have five thousand welcomes. But, sirrah,
how did thy master part with Madam Julia?

speaker: LANCE
text:
Marry, after they closed in earnest, they parted
very fairly in jest.

speaker: SPEED
text: But shall she marry him?

speaker: LANCE
text: No.

speaker: SPEED
text: How then? Shall he marry her?

speaker: LANCE
text: No, neither.

speaker: SPEED
text: What, are they broken?

speaker: LANCE
text: No, they are both as whole as a fish.

speaker: SPEED
text: Why then, how stands the matter with them?

speaker: LANCE
text:
Marry, thus: when it stands well with him, it
stands well with her.

speaker: SPEED
text: What an ass art thou! I understand thee not.

speaker: LANCE
text:
What a block art thou that thou canst not! My
staff understands me.

speaker: SPEED
text: What thou sayst?

speaker: LANCE
text:
Ay, and what I do too. Look thee, I’ll but lean,
and my staff understands me.

speaker: SPEED
text: It stands under thee indeed.

speaker: LANCE
text:
Why, “stand under” and “understand” is all
one.

speaker: SPEED
text: But tell me true, will ’t be a match?

speaker: LANCE
text:
Ask my dog. If he say “Ay,” it will; if he say
“No,” it will; if he shake his tail and say nothing, it
will.

speaker: SPEED
text: The conclusion is, then, that it will.

speaker: LANCE
text:
Thou shalt never get such a secret from me but
by a parable.

speaker: SPEED
text:
’Tis well that I get it so. But, Lance, how sayst
thou that my master is become a notable lover?

speaker: LANCE
text: I never knew him otherwise.

speaker: SPEED
text: Than how?

speaker: LANCE
text: A notable lubber, as thou reportest him to be.

speaker: SPEED
text: Why, thou whoreson ass, thou mistak’st me.

speaker: LANCE
text: Why, fool, I meant not thee; I meant thy master.

speaker: SPEED
text: I tell thee, my master is become a hot lover.

speaker: LANCE
text:
Why, I tell thee, I care not though he burn
himself in love. If thou wilt, go with me to the
alehouse; if not, thou art an Hebrew, a Jew, and not
worth the name of a Christian.

speaker: SPEED
text: Why?

speaker: LANCE
text:
Because thou hast not so much charity in thee
as to go to the ale with a Christian. Wilt thou go?

speaker: SPEED
text: At thy service.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
To leave my Julia, shall I be forsworn.
To love fair Sylvia, shall I be forsworn.
To wrong my friend, I shall be much forsworn.
And ev’n that power which gave me first my oath
Provokes me to this threefold perjury.
Love bade me swear, and love bids me forswear.
O sweet-suggesting Love, if thou hast sinned,
Teach me, thy tempted subject, to excuse it.
At first I did adore a twinkling star,
But now I worship a celestial sun;
Unheedful vows may heedfully be broken,
And he wants wit that wants resolvèd will
To learn his wit t’ exchange the bad for better.
Fie, fie, unreverend tongue, to call her bad
Whose sovereignty so oft thou hast preferred
With twenty thousand soul-confirming oaths.
I cannot leave to love, and yet I do.
But there I leave to love where I should love.
Julia I lose, and Valentine I lose;
If I keep them, I needs must lose myself;
If I lose them, thus find I by their loss:
For Valentine, myself; for Julia, Sylvia.
I to myself am dearer than a friend,
For love is still most precious in itself,
And Sylvia—witness heaven that made her fair—
Shows Julia but a swarthy Ethiope.
I will forget that Julia is alive,
Rememb’ring that my love to her is dead;
And Valentine I’ll hold an enemy,
Aiming at Sylvia as a sweeter friend.
I cannot now prove constant to myself
Without some treachery used to Valentine.
This night he meaneth with a corded ladder
To climb celestial Sylvia’s chamber window,
Myself in counsel his competitor.
Now presently I’ll give her father notice
Of their disguising and pretended flight,
Who, all enraged, will banish Valentine,
For Thurio he intends shall wed his daughter.
But Valentine being gone, I’ll quickly cross
By some sly trick blunt Thurio’s dull proceeding.
Love, lend me wings to make my purpose swift,
As thou hast lent me wit to plot this drift.

speaker: JULIA
text:
Counsel, Lucetta. Gentle girl, assist me;
And ev’n in kind love I do conjure thee—
Who art the table wherein all my thoughts
Are visibly charactered and engraved—
To lesson me and tell me some good mean
How with my honor I may undertake
A journey to my loving Proteus.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Alas, the way is wearisome and long.

speaker: JULIA
text:
A true-devoted pilgrim is not weary
To measure kingdoms with his feeble steps;
Much less shall she that hath Love’s wings to fly,
And when the flight is made to one so dear,
Of such divine perfection, as Sir Proteus.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Better forbear till Proteus make return.

speaker: JULIA
text:
O, know’st thou not his looks are my soul’s food?
Pity the dearth that I have pinèd in
By longing for that food so long a time.
Didst thou but know the inly touch of love,
Thou wouldst as soon go kindle fire with snow
As seek to quench the fire of love with words.

speaker: LUCETTA
text:
I do not seek to quench your love’s hot fire,
But qualify the fire’s extreme rage,
Lest it should burn above the bounds of reason.

speaker: JULIA
text:
The more thou damm’st it up, the more it burns.
The current that with gentle murmur glides,
Thou know’st, being stopped, impatiently doth rage,
But when his fair course is not hinderèd,
He makes sweet music with th’ enameled stones,
Giving a gentle kiss to every sedge
He overtaketh in his pilgrimage;
And so by many winding nooks he strays
With willing sport to the wild ocean.
Then let me go and hinder not my course.
I’ll be as patient as a gentle stream
And make a pastime of each weary step
Till the last step have brought me to my love,
And there I’ll rest as after much turmoil
A blessèd soul doth in Elysium.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: But in what habit will you go along?

speaker: JULIA
text:
Not like a woman, for I would prevent
The loose encounters of lascivious men.
Gentle Lucetta, fit me with such weeds
As may beseem some well-reputed page.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Why, then, your Ladyship must cut your hair.

speaker: JULIA
text:
No, girl, I’ll knit it up in silken strings
With twenty odd-conceited true-love knots.
To be fantastic may become a youth
Of greater time than I shall show to be.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: What fashion, madam, shall I make your breeches?

speaker: JULIA
text:
That fits as well as “Tell me, good my lord,
What compass will you wear your farthingale?”
Why, ev’n what fashion thou best likes, Lucetta.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: You must needs have them with a codpiece, madam.

speaker: JULIA
text: Out, out, Lucetta. That will be ill-favored.

speaker: LUCETTA
text:
A round hose, madam, now’s not worth a pin
Unless you have a codpiece to stick pins on.

speaker: JULIA
text:
Lucetta, as thou lov’st me, let me have
What thou think’st meet and is most mannerly.
But tell me, wench, how will the world repute me
For undertaking so unstaid a journey?
I fear me it will make me scandalized.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: If you think so, then stay at home and go not.

speaker: JULIA
text: Nay, that I will not.

speaker: LUCETTA
text:
Then never dream on infamy, but go.
If Proteus like your journey when you come,
No matter who’s displeased when you are gone.
I fear me he will scarce be pleased withal.

speaker: JULIA
text:
That is the least, Lucetta, of my fear.
A thousand oaths, an ocean of his tears,
And instances of infinite of love
Warrant me welcome to my Proteus.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: All these are servants to deceitful men.

speaker: JULIA
text:
Base men that use them to so base effect!
But truer stars did govern Proteus’ birth.
His words are bonds, his oaths are oracles,
His love sincere, his thoughts immaculate,
His tears pure messengers sent from his heart,
His heart as far from fraud as heaven from Earth.

speaker: LUCETTA
text: Pray heav’n he prove so when you come to him.

speaker: JULIA
text:
Now, as thou lov’st me, do him not that wrong
To bear a hard opinion of his truth.
Only deserve my love by loving him.
And presently go with me to my chamber
To take a note of what I stand in need of
To furnish me upon my longing journey.
All that is mine I leave at thy dispose,
My goods, my lands, my reputation.
Only, in lieu thereof, dispatch me hence.
Come, answer not, but to it presently.
I am impatient of my tarriance.

speaker: DUKE
PROTEUS
text:
My gracious lord, that which I would discover
The law of friendship bids me to conceal,
But when I call to mind your gracious favors
Done to me, undeserving as I am,
My duty pricks me on to utter that
Which else no worldly good should draw from me.
Know, worthy prince, Sir Valentine my friend
This night intends to steal away your daughter;
Myself am one made privy to the plot.
I know you have determined to bestow her
On Thurio, whom your gentle daughter hates,
And should she thus be stol’n away from you,
It would be much vexation to your age.
Thus, for my duty’s sake, I rather chose
To cross my friend in his intended drift
Than, by concealing it, heap on your head
A pack of sorrows which would press you down,
Being unprevented, to your timeless grave.

speaker: DUKE
text:
Proteus, I thank thee for thine honest care,
Which to requite command me while I live.
This love of theirs myself have often seen,
Haply when they have judged me fast asleep,
And oftentimes have purposed to forbid
Sir Valentine her company and my court.
But fearing lest my jealous aim might err
And so, unworthily, disgrace the man—
A rashness that I ever yet have shunned—
I gave him gentle looks, thereby to find
That which thyself hast now disclosed to me.
And that thou mayst perceive my fear of this,
Knowing that tender youth is soon suggested,
I nightly lodge her in an upper tower,
The key whereof myself have ever kept,
And thence she cannot be conveyed away.

speaker: PROTEUS
text:
Know, noble lord, they have devised a mean
How he her chamber-window will ascend
And with a corded ladder fetch her down;
For which the youthful lover now is gone,
And this way comes he with it presently,
Where, if it please you, you may intercept him.
But, good my lord, do it so cunningly
That my discovery be not aimèd at;
For love of you, not hate unto my friend,
Hath made me publisher of this pretense.

speaker: DUKE
text:
Upon mine honor, he shall never know
That I had any light from thee of this.

speaker: PROTEUS
text: Adieu, my lord. Sir Valentine is coming.

speaker: DUKE
text: Sir Valentine, whither away so fast?

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Please it your Grace, there is a messenger
That stays to bear my letters to my friends,
And I am going to deliver them.

speaker: DUKE
text: Be they of much import?

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
The tenor of them doth but signify
My health and happy being at your court.

speaker: DUKE
text:
Nay then, no matter. Stay with me awhile;
I am to break with thee of some affairs
That touch me near, wherein thou must be secret.
’Tis not unknown to thee that I have sought
To match my friend Sir Thurio to my daughter.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
I know it well, my lord, and sure the match
Were rich and honorable. Besides, the gentleman
Is full of virtue, bounty, worth, and qualities
Beseeming such a wife as your fair daughter.
Cannot your Grace win her to fancy him?

speaker: DUKE
text:
No. Trust me, she is peevish, sullen, froward,
Proud, disobedient, stubborn, lacking duty,
Neither regarding that she is my child
Nor fearing me as if I were her father;
And may I say to thee, this pride of hers,
Upon advice, hath drawn my love from her,
And where I thought the remnant of mine age
Should have been cherished by her childlike duty,
I now am full resolved to take a wife
And turn her out to who will take her in.
Then let her beauty be her wedding dower,
For me and my possessions she esteems not.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: What would your Grace have me to do in this?

speaker: DUKE
text:
There is a lady in Verona here
Whom I affect; but she is nice, and coy,
And nought esteems my agèd eloquence.
Now therefore would I have thee to my tutor—
For long agone I have forgot to court;
Besides, the fashion of the time is changed—
How and which way I may bestow myself
To be regarded in her sun-bright eye.

speaker: VALENTINE
DUKE
text: But she did scorn a present that I sent her.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
A woman sometime scorns what best contents her.
Send her another; never give her o’er,
For scorn at first makes after-love the more.
If she do frown, ’tis not in hate of you,
But rather to beget more love in you.
If she do chide, ’tis not to have you gone,
Forwhy the fools are mad if left alone.
Take no repulse, whatever she doth say;
For “get you gone” she doth not mean “away.”
Flatter and praise, commend, extol their graces;
Though ne’er so black, say they have angels’ faces.
That man that hath a tongue, I say, is no man
If with his tongue he cannot win a woman.

speaker: DUKE
text:
But she I mean is promised by her friends
Unto a youthful gentleman of worth
And kept severely from resort of men,
That no man hath access by day to her.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Why, then, I would resort to her by night.

speaker: DUKE
text:
Ay, but the doors be locked and keys kept safe,
That no man hath recourse to her by night.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: What lets but one may enter at her window?

speaker: DUKE
text:
Her chamber is aloft, far from the ground,
And built so shelving that one cannot climb it
Without apparent hazard of his life.

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
Why, then a ladder quaintly made of cords
To cast up, with a pair of anchoring hooks,
Would serve to scale another Hero’s tower,
So bold Leander would adventure it.

speaker: DUKE
text:
Now, as thou art a gentleman of blood,
Advise me where I may have such a ladder.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: When would you use it? Pray sir, tell me that.

speaker: DUKE
text:
This very night; for love is like a child
That longs for everything that he can come by.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: By seven o’clock I’ll get you such a ladder.

speaker: DUKE
text:
But hark thee: I will go to her alone;
How shall I best convey the ladder thither?

speaker: VALENTINE
text:
It will be light, my lord, that you may bear it
Under a cloak that is of any length.

speaker: DUKE
text: A cloak as long as thine will serve the turn?

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Ay, my good lord.

speaker: DUKE
text:
Then let me see thy cloak;
I’ll get me one of such another length.

speaker: VALENTINE
text: Why, any cloak will serve the turn, my lord.

speaker: DUKE
text:
How shall I fashion me to wear a cloak?
I pray thee, let me feel thy cloak upon me.
What letter is this same? What’s here? To Sylvia .
And here an engine fit for my proceeding.
I’ll be so bold to break the seal for once.
My thoughts do harbor with my Sylvia nightly,
And slaves they are to me that send them flying.
O, could their master come and go as lightly,
Himself would lodge where, senseless, they are lying.
My herald thoughts in thy pure bosom rest them,
While I, their king, that thither them importune,
Do curse the grace that with such grace hath blest them,
Because myself do want my servants’ fortune.
I curse myself, for they are sent by me,
That they should harbor where their lord should be.
What’s here?
Sylvia, this night I will enfranchise thee.
’Tis so. And here’s the ladder for the purpose.
Why, Phaëton—for thou art Merops’ son—
Wilt thou aspire to guide the heavenly car
And with thy daring folly burn the world?
Wilt thou reach stars because they shine on thee?
Go, base intruder, overweening slave,
Bestow thy fawning smiles on equal mates
And think my patience, more than thy desert,
Is privilege for thy departure hence.
Thank me for this more than for all the favors
Which all too much I have bestowed on thee.
But if thou linger in my territories
